# ENTERPRISE CUSTOMER SUCCESS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT & SUPPORT OPERATIONS CANON
## Stage 5 — Service Governance, Resolution Authority, Customer Recovery & Support Excellence Canon

---

# 5.1 Purpose

The **Enterprise Customer Success, Service Management & Support Operations Domain** requires a permanent governance framework defining who may:

- Classify service issues.
- set priorities.
- assign ownership.
- approve resolutions.
- authorize refunds.
- authorize replacements.
- approve goodwill.
- escalate Cases.
- close severe complaints.
- revise service policy.
- oversee Customer Success.
- audit service decisions.

Stages 1–4 established:

- Domain foundation.
- Service entity architecture.
- Case operating model.
- Service Management service architecture.
- Refund, replacement, recovery, escalation, Customer Health, and Customer Success execution.

Stage 5 establishes the authority, accountability, policy, quality, and governance structure that ensures Customer Service remains:

- Fair.
- consistent.
- customer-aware.
- financially controlled.
- operationally feasible.
- privacy-aware.
- auditable.
- resilient.
- accountable.

The permanent objective is:

> **Empower frontline service teams to resolve customer needs quickly while preserving clear authority for high-impact, financial, exceptional, and strategic decisions.**

---

# 5.2 Service Governance Philosophy

The Domain permanently follows:

---

## Empowerment Within Authority

Frontline staff should resolve routine issues without unnecessary escalation.

Empowerment must operate within certified policy.

---

## Facts Before Remedy

A customer remedy should reflect the verified situation.

---

## Resolution Authority Before Promise

Employees may only promise outcomes they can legitimately authorize or reliably execute.

---

## Fairness Before Inconsistency

Similar material Cases should receive reasonably consistent treatment unless relevant differences justify another outcome.

---

## Customer Outcome Before Metric Protection

Cases must not be manipulated to protect SLA or closure statistics.

---

## Accountability Before Handoff

Escalation does not eliminate responsibility for customer communication.

---

## Evidence Before Disciplinary Interpretation

Service records should support improvement and accountability without converting every customer complaint into automatic employee fault.

---

## Human Authority Before Irreversible Automation

High-impact service decisions remain governed by accountable humans.

---

# 5.3 Service Governance Layers

The permanent governance architecture operates across eight layers.

---

# Layer 1 — Customer Service Strategy Governance

Controls:

- Service philosophy.
- customer experience principles.
- support-channel strategy.
- Customer Success priorities.

---

# Layer 2 — Case Governance

Controls:

- Case definitions.
- status.
- ownership.
- categories.
- priorities.
- closure.

---

# Layer 3 — Resolution Governance

Controls:

- Resolution types.
- eligibility.
- authority.
- completion requirements.

---

# Layer 4 — Recovery Governance

Controls:

- Refund coordination.
- replacement.
- goodwill.
- compensation.
- recovery concessions.

---

# Layer 5 — SLA & Escalation Governance

Controls:

- Service commitments.
- breach handling.
- escalation rules.
- priority treatment.

---

# Layer 6 — Service Quality Governance

Controls:

- Handling standards.
- quality reviews.
- complaint recurrence.
- Case reopen patterns.

---

# Layer 7 — Customer Success Governance

Controls:

- Customer Health.
- retention risk.
- proactive actions.
- strategic account service.

---

# Layer 8 — Audit, Privacy & Service Integrity Governance

Controls:

- History.
- communication evidence.
- internal-note protection.
- sensitive information.
- service audit.

---

# 5.4 Canonical Governance Roles

The permanent role architecture includes:

- Enterprise Service Authority.
- Customer Service Manager.
- Customer Success Manager.
- Service Agent.
- Case Owner.
- Queue Owner.
- Service Supervisor.
- Resolution Approver.
- Recovery Approver.
- Refund Authority.
- Replacement Authority.
- Escalation Authority.
- Service Quality Reviewer.
- Service Administrator.
- Service Auditor.

One individual may perform multiple roles in a smaller enterprise.

The business responsibilities remain distinct.

---

# 5.5 Enterprise Service Authority

The Enterprise Service Authority is accountable for:

- Service governance standards.
- major customer-service policy.
- high-impact resolution principles.
- service-quality philosophy.
- cross-domain conflict resolution.
- enterprise support maturity.

It does not replace operational domain ownership.

---

# 5.6 Customer Service Manager

Responsibilities include:

- Day-to-day support performance.
- Case backlog.
- queue health.
- SLA risk.
- escalation management.
- service consistency.
- staff enablement.

The manager should not personally approve every routine Case.

---

# 5.7 Customer Success Manager

Responsible for proactive relationship outcomes such as:

- B2B Customer Health.
- retention actions.
- service-recovery follow-up.
- proactive risk intervention.

Customer Success governance should remain connected to CRM and Sales without becoming duplicate account management.

---

# 5.8 Service Agent

A Service Agent may:

- Create/update Cases.
- communicate with customers.
- investigate standard issues.
- resolve within delegated authority.
- request internal actions.
- escalate when necessary.

Agents should have enough authority to solve routine Cases efficiently.

---

# 5.9 Case Owner

The Case Owner is accountable for:

- Progress.
- communication.
- coordination.
- next action.
- closure readiness.

The Case Owner may depend on other departments but retains customer-facing accountability.

---

# 5.10 Queue Owner

The Queue Owner governs:

- Workload.
- assignment.
- aging.
- unowned Cases.
- capacity.
- queue-level escalation.

---

# 5.11 Service Supervisor

A Service Supervisor may:

- Reassign Cases.
- review complex Cases.
- approve certain resolutions.
- coach agents.
- manage operational escalations.

---

# 5.12 Resolution Approver

A Resolution Approver may authorize defined customer outcomes.

Examples:

- Replacement.
- partial refund.
- recovery action.
- exception.

Authority must be explicitly delegated.

---

# 5.13 Refund Authority

Refund authority may be separated between:

- Service recommendation.
- business approval.
- Finance execution.

Canonical distinction:

```text id="refund-authority-distinction"
Customer Service:
Why Refund Is Needed

↓

Authorized Approver:
Whether Refund Is Approved

↓

Finance:
Executes Financial Refund
```

---

# 5.14 Replacement Authority

Replacement authority may consider:

- Product cost.
- production effort.
- customer impact.
- finding.
- repeat history.

Routine low-cost remakes may be delegated.

High-impact replacements may require management approval.

---

# 5.15 Recovery Approver

A Recovery Approver governs non-standard goodwill such as:

- Coupon.
- discount.
- expedited shipping.
- added item.
- account credit.

Commercial concessions remain aligned with Domain 31.

---

# 5.16 Escalation Authority

Escalation authority determines when Cases require:

- Functional specialist.
- manager.
- executive.
- legal/compliance.

Escalation authority does not mean the recipient automatically owns the entire Case.

---

# 5.17 Service Quality Reviewer

Responsible for:

- Case-quality sampling.
- severe-Case review.
- communication-quality review.
- closure-quality assessment.
- recurring error detection.

Quality review must focus on learning as well as control.

---

# 5.18 Service Administrator

A Service Administrator may technically configure:

- Categories.
- queues.
- SLAs.
- templates.
- routing rules.

Technical configuration permission does not automatically confer customer-remedy authority.

---

# 5.19 Service Auditor

The Service Auditor may inspect:

- Case history.
- refunds.
- replacements.
- escalations.
- internal notes where authorized.
- closure decisions.
- policy adherence.

Audit should remain independent from routine Case execution where possible.

---

# 5.20 Service Authority Matrix

| Decision | Primary Authority |
|---|---|
| Routine information response | Service Agent |
| Case classification | Agent / Rules |
| Priority within standard policy | Agent / System |
| Queue reassignment | Supervisor / Queue Owner |
| Standard correction | Agent |
| Low-impact replacement | Delegated Service Authority |
| Significant replacement | Manager |
| Refund recommendation | Service |
| Refund approval | Delegated Business Authority |
| Refund execution | Finance |
| Goodwill discount | Commercial Authority |
| Severe complaint closure | Supervisor / Manager |
| Executive escalation | Designated Authority |
| Service policy change | Service Governance |
| Service audit | Auditor |

---

# 5.21 Separation of Duties

High-impact service actions should separate where practical:

- Requester.
- approver.
- executor.
- auditor.

Example:

```text id="service-separation"
Agent Recommends Refund

↓

Manager Approves

↓

Finance Executes

↓

Case Owner Communicates

↓

Audit Preserves Evidence
```

---

# 5.22 Frontline Empowerment

Governance should not create unnecessary bureaucracy.

Frontline employees should be able to complete routine actions such as:

- Answer standard questions.
- request missing personalization.
- resend information.
- update customers.
- initiate standard internal tasks.

The objective is controlled speed.

---

# 5.23 Resolution Authority Tiers

A permanent tier model may include:

```text id="resolution-authority-tiers"
Tier 1
Standard Agent Resolution

↓

Tier 2
Supervisor Resolution

↓

Tier 3
Manager Resolution

↓

Tier 4
Cross-Domain / Executive Exception
```

Exact monetary thresholds remain configurable.

---

# 5.24 Standard Resolution Policy

Standard resolutions should define:

- Eligible Case types.
- evidence required.
- permissible action.
- authority.
- completion criteria.

This enables consistency.

---

# 5.25 Exception Resolution Policy

Non-standard resolutions require:

- Reason.
- expected customer impact.
- financial/operational impact.
- authority.
- evidence.

---

# 5.26 Resolution Consistency

The enterprise should periodically review whether materially similar Cases receive wildly different outcomes.

Differences may be legitimate due to:

- Severity.
- customer impact.
- event urgency.
- evidence.
- relationship context.

Consistency does not mean mechanical uniformity.

---

# 5.27 Resolution Fairness

Customer treatment should not depend on:

- arbitrary employee preference.
- emotional pressure alone.
- irrelevant personal characteristics.

Resolution should be based on:

- Facts.
- policy.
- impact.
- authority.
- legitimate relationship context.

---

# 5.28 Complaint Governance

Complaints should be handled through:

```text id="complaint-governance"
Complaint Received

↓

Acknowledgment

↓

Classification

↓

Investigation

↓

Finding

↓

Resolution

↓

Customer Outcome

↓

Learning
```

---

# 5.29 Severe Complaint Governance

Severe Cases may require:

- Priority ownership.
- management visibility.
- structured investigation.
- communication cadence.
- closure review.

---

# 5.30 Complaint Closure Authority

High-severity complaints should not be closed without appropriate evidence that:

- Resolution actions are complete.
- required communication occurred.
- escalation obligations are complete.

---

# 5.31 Refund Governance

Refund policy should define:

- Eligibility.
- amount.
- authority.
- execution process.
- financial confirmation.
- customer communication.

---

# 5.32 Refund Amount Governance

Potential refund structures include:

- Full.
- partial.
- shipping-only.
- line-item.
- service adjustment.

The amount must remain explicit.

---

# 5.33 Refund Without Return

Some situations may allow refund without physical return.

This requires policy based on:

- Product.
- defect.
- recovery cost.
- shipping economics.
- legal requirements.

---

# 5.34 Replacement Governance

Replacement policy should define:

- Eligible situations.
- evidence.
- personalization revalidation.
- production Priority.
- QC requirements.
- shipping treatment.
- authority.

---

# 5.35 Repeat Replacement Governance

A second replacement for the same issue should normally trigger enhanced review.

Potential causes:

- Persistent Product defect.
- bad personalization source.
- production process failure.
- shipping problem.

---

# 5.36 Return Governance

Return governance should define:

- Eligibility.
- personalization restrictions.
- authorization.
- inspection.
- resulting refund/replacement.

---

# 5.37 Personalized Product Return Governance

Personalized-product Cases require particular care because an item may be unsellable after personalization.

Governance must distinguish:

- Enterprise defect.
- customer-entry error.
- shipping damage.
- change of mind.
- legal entitlement.

---

# 5.38 Customer Recovery Governance

Customer Recovery should be used when:

- A valid issue created significant dissatisfaction.
- normal Resolution alone may not restore trust.

Recovery is an additional relationship intervention.

---

# 5.39 Recovery Proportionality

Recovery should reflect:

- Harm.
- inconvenience.
- time sensitivity.
- relationship.
- commercial value.
- responsibility.

Canonical rule:

```text id="recovery-proportionality"
Customer Impact

+

Business Responsibility

+

Relationship Context

↓

Proportionate Recovery
```

---

# 5.40 Recovery Authority

Potential authority structure:

```text id="recovery-authority"
Standard Apology / Priority Follow-Up
→ Agent

Low-Value Goodwill
→ Supervisor

Material Discount / Credit
→ Commercial Authority

Large Strategic Recovery
→ Management / Executive
```

---

# 5.41 Goodwill Governance

Goodwill must remain clearly distinguishable from:

- Refund entitlement.
- contractual remedy.
- discount.
- compensation.

This distinction supports proper analytics.

---

# 5.42 Commercial Concession Boundary

If the recovery instrument is:

- Coupon.
- future discount.
- price concession.

Domain 31 governs commercial authority.

Domain 32 governs why the recovery exists.

---

# 5.43 Finance Boundary

If the recovery involves actual financial movement:

Finance remains authoritative for execution.

Customer Service owns customer communication and Case coordination.

---

# 5.44 Production Boundary

A service agent cannot promise:

- Same-day remake.
- rush completion.

unless Production feasibility is confirmed.

---

# 5.45 Shipping Boundary

A service agent cannot promise:

- Guaranteed carrier delivery date.

unless the Shipping architecture supports that commitment.

---

# 5.46 Customer Promise Governance

Every material customer promise should satisfy:

```text id="customer-promise-governance"
Authority

+

Feasibility

+

Due Time

+

Owner

=

Valid Service Commitment
```

---

# 5.47 Promise Review

Promises should be reviewed for:

- Overdue state.
- repeated missed commitments.
- unrealistic dates.
- dependency problems.

---

# 5.48 SLA Governance

SLA governance defines:

- Which Cases receive SLAs.
- response targets.
- resolution targets.
- pause conditions.
- escalation thresholds.

---

# 5.49 SLA Design Principle

SLA targets should be:

- Meaningful.
- achievable.
- differentiated by Case type.
- aligned with customer impact.

A universally aggressive SLA may create superficial behavior.

---

# 5.50 SLA Pause Governance

Valid pause reasons may include:

- Waiting on customer information.
- externally controlled delay where policy permits.

Internal inactivity must not be disguised as a pause.

---

# 5.51 SLA Breach Governance

A breach requires:

- Evidence.
- reason.
- owner.
- customer impact review.
- potential escalation.

Breach history remains immutable.

---

# 5.52 Escalation Governance

Escalation should define:

- Trigger.
- type.
- destination.
- response expectation.
- Case ownership.

---

# 5.53 Escalation Discipline

Escalation should not become a substitute for normal ownership.

The objective is:

- Additional authority.
- expertise.
- urgency.

not dumping responsibility.

---

# 5.54 Executive Escalation Governance

Executive escalation is reserved for matters such as:

- Strategic account risk.
- systemic service failure.
- major reputation issue.
- severe unresolved complaint.

Routine Cases should remain within operational management.

---

# 5.55 Legal / Compliance Escalation

Cases involving:

- Legal claims.
- regulatory obligations.
- privacy incidents.
- serious allegations.

may require Legal/Compliance involvement.

Domain 24 remains authoritative for legal/compliance governance.

---

# 5.56 Service Incident Governance

Systemic incidents require:

- Incident owner.
- scope.
- affected customers.
- common response strategy.
- root cause.
- closure review.

---

# 5.57 Incident vs Case Governance

Permanent distinction:

```text id="incident-vs-case"
Service Incident
= Systemic Business Problem

Customer Case
= Individual Customer Impact
```

Closing the Incident does not automatically close individual Cases.

---

# 5.58 Backlog Governance

Backlog management should protect:

- Critical Cases.
- old Cases.
- SLA risk.
- high-impact dependencies.

Managers should not optimize backlog by prematurely closing difficult Cases.

---

# 5.59 Queue Governance

Each Queue should define:

- Purpose.
- owner.
- membership.
- routing rules.
- capacity expectation.
- escalation path.

---

# 5.60 Unassigned Case Governance

Unassigned Cases are a service-control failure.

The platform should monitor:

- Unassigned count.
- age.
- severity.

High-priority Cases must not remain invisible in shared queues.

---

# 5.61 Case Reassignment Governance

Reassignment requires:

- Reason.
- new owner.
- handoff context.

Repeated reassignment may indicate poor routing or ownership avoidance.

---

# 5.62 Case Reopen Governance

Reopened Cases require review of:

- Previous Resolution.
- reopen reason.
- failed execution.
- new evidence.

Repeated reopen may trigger Service Quality review.

---

# 5.63 Closure Governance

Case closure requires:

- Valid closure reason.
- completed required actions.
- no unresolved critical dependencies.
- required customer communication.

---

# 5.64 Premature Closure Control

The platform should detect patterns such as:

- Closure immediately before SLA breach.
- repeated reopening.
- closing while refund still processing.
- closing while replacement not shipped.

These may indicate process weakness.

---

# 5.65 Service Quality Governance

Service Quality is assessed across:

- Correctness.
- completeness.
- timeliness.
- communication.
- policy.
- customer outcome.

---

# 5.66 Quality Sampling

Case review may use:

- Random sample.
- severe Cases.
- high-value refunds.
- repeated reopen.
- new-agent Cases.

Sampling must remain fair and purposeful.

---

# 5.67 Quality Review Findings

Potential findings include:

- Excellent Handling.
- Meets Standard.
- Coaching Opportunity.
- Process Failure.
- Policy Gap.
- System Limitation.

This avoids treating every issue as an individual employee failure.

---

# 5.68 Employee Accountability Boundary

Service performance evidence may contribute to HCM processes.

But Domain 32 does not independently govern:

- Discipline.
- performance appraisal.
- employment actions.

Domain 25 remains authoritative.

---

# 5.69 Service Error Classification

Service errors may arise from:

- Agent mistake.
- Process design.
- unclear policy.
- system defect.
- missing information.
- operational dependency.

Root cause should be evaluated before assigning accountability.

---

# 5.70 Customer Feedback Governance

Customer feedback should remain:

- Voluntary where required.
- linked to service context.
- interpreted carefully.

A single score should not define the entire service experience.

---

# 5.71 CSAT Governance

CSAT analysis should account for:

- Case type.
- severity.
- outcome.
- channel.

Comparing incompatible Case types can produce misleading employee/team judgments.

---

# 5.72 Service Metric Governance

Potential measures include:

- First Response Time.
- Resolution Time.
- SLA Compliance.
- Reopen Rate.
- Escalation Rate.
- Backlog.
- CSAT.
- replacement/refund rate.

Domain 30 governs official KPI definitions and targets.

---

# 5.73 Metric Gaming Prevention

The governance model should identify harmful behavior such as:

- Premature closure.
- unnecessary Case splitting.
- ignoring complex Cases.
- artificial SLA pauses.

Operational metrics must serve customer outcomes.

---

# 5.74 Customer Success Governance

Customer Success may operate proactively for:

- B2B accounts.
- repeat customers.
- high-risk recoveries.
- Orders with known service risk.

---

# 5.75 Proactive Service Authority

Customer Success may:

- Send status communication.
- request missing information.
- schedule follow-up.

Commercial incentives still require appropriate authority.

---

# 5.76 Customer Health Governance

Customer Health models require:

- Defined indicators.
- explainable results.
- review cadence.
- restricted use.

Health should not create arbitrary discrimination.

---

# 5.77 Retention Risk Governance

Retention Risk may influence:

- Follow-up Priority.
- account-manager attention.
- recovery review.

It should not automatically trigger discounts.

---

# 5.78 B2B Service Governance

Corporate support may define differentiated:

- ownership.
- escalation.
- service commitment.

Differences should reflect legitimate contractual/account requirements.

---

# 5.79 Strategic Account Governance

Important accounts may receive:

- Dedicated owner.
- priority communication.
- executive escalation thresholds.

Strategic status should not justify false facts or bypass legal controls.

---

# 5.80 Marketplace Service Governance

Marketplace Cases must comply with:

- Marketplace procedures.
- internal policy.
- financial controls.

External platform pressure must not cause inaccurate internal records.

---

# 5.81 Channel Consistency

Customers may contact through:

- WhatsApp.
- email.
- marketplace.

The platform should strive for consistent service policy across channels unless channel-specific contractual rules differ.

---

# 5.82 Service Template Governance

Templates require:

- Owner.
- version.
- appropriate use case.
- approval where necessary.

Templates containing:

- Refund promises.
- delivery commitments.
- legal language.

require stronger control.

---

# 5.83 Knowledge Governance

Agents should use current approved:

- Policies.
- SOPs.
- Product information.
- troubleshooting.

Obsolete guidance should be retired.

---

# 5.84 Internal Note Governance

Internal Notes must:

- Remain professional.
- avoid unnecessary sensitive data.
- distinguish fact from opinion.

Internal visibility does not justify careless documentation.

---

# 5.85 Customer Communication Governance

Customer communication must be:

- Accurate.
- clear.
- respectful.
- policy-aligned.
- appropriately personalized.

---

# 5.86 Communication Approval

High-risk communications may require review.

Examples:

- Legal disputes.
- major compensation.
- severe corporate escalation.
- public/reputation incident.

Routine communication should not require unnecessary approval.

---

# 5.87 Privacy Governance

Cases may include:

- Customer identity.
- address.
- photographs.
- complaint details.
- financial references.

Access should follow:

- Least privilege.
- business need.
- data classification.

---

# 5.88 Sensitive Evidence Governance

Sensitive attachments must not be:

- Forwarded casually.
- duplicated unnecessarily.
- exposed in broad channels.

Domain 29 governs information lifecycle and privacy controls.

---

# 5.89 Service Audit Governance

Material actions requiring audit may include:

- Refund approval.
- replacement approval.
- Case ownership changes.
- high-severity priority changes.
- escalations.
- closure.
- reopen.
- internal evidence corrections.

---

# 5.90 Historical Service Integrity

Historical Case data should preserve:

- Original communications.
- findings.
- Resolution.
- approvals.
- timestamps.

Corrections must be additive and traceable.

---

# 5.91 Service Fraud / Abuse Governance

Potential abuse indicators may include:

- Repeated unsupported refund patterns.
- excessive goodwill usage.
- contradictory evidence.

Such signals trigger investigation.

They are not automatic proof of wrongdoing.

---

# 5.92 Employee Abuse Prevention

Governance should also detect internal misuse such as:

- Unauthorized refunds.
- inappropriate concessions.
- manipulation of SLA.
- deleting evidence.
- falsely marking actions complete.

These require evidence and appropriate cross-domain investigation.

---

# 5.93 AI Service Governance

AI may assist with:

- Case summary.
- classification.
- routing.
- response drafting.
- knowledge suggestions.
- risk detection.

AI assistance must be clearly bounded.

---

# 5.94 AI Authority Matrix

AI may potentially auto-execute low-risk actions such as:

- Suggest category.
- route standard Case.
- send receipt acknowledgment.

AI must not independently:

- Approve material refund.
- deny statutory entitlement.
- accuse customer of fraud.
- approve significant compensation.
- close severe complaints.
- alter financial records.

---

# 5.95 AI Communication Governance

AI-generated customer messages must be grounded in authoritative:

- Order.
- Shipment.
- Finance.
- policy.
- Case.

Material responses may require human review.

---

# 5.96 AI Bias & Fairness

AI must not provide inferior service based on inappropriate sensitive attributes.

Service prioritization should use legitimate operational/customer-impact factors.

---

# 5.97 AI Confidence Governance

Low-confidence:

- Classification.
- identity match.
- resolution suggestions.

should not silently become authoritative.

---

# 5.98 GiftHatke Governance Specialization

GiftHatke requires service governance suitable for:

- Personalized products.
- occasion-sensitive deliveries.
- marketplaces.
- B2B customers.
- manufacturing-related complaints.
- customer-submitted assets.

---

# 5.99 GiftHatke Personalization Governance

Personalization disputes should compare:

```text id="gift-personalization-governance"
Customer Submitted Details

↓

Approved / Stored Personalization

↓

Production Input

↓

Produced Result

↓

Finding
```

This prevents unsupported assumptions.

---

# 5.100 GiftHatke Wrong-Name Case

Example:

```text id="gift-wrong-name-case"
Customer:
"Wrong name engraved"

↓

Submitted Text:
"Riya"

Produced:
"Rina"

↓

Enterprise Error Confirmed

↓

Replacement Authority

↓

Priority Remake + Enhanced QC
```

---

# 5.101 GiftHatke Customer-Input Error

Example:

```text id="gift-customer-input-error"
Customer:
"Name is wrong"

Submitted:
"Rina"

Produced:
"Rina"

↓

Production Matches Submitted Input

↓

Finding:
Customer Input Mismatch

↓

Resolution Governed by Policy / Goodwill
```

The customer should still be treated respectfully.

---

# 5.102 GiftHatke Occasion-Sensitive Priority

A gift required for:

- Wedding tomorrow.
- birthday today.
- Rakhi deadline.

may justify higher urgency.

It does not automatically justify:

- Impossible remake.
- unsupported delivery promise.

---

# 5.103 GiftHatke Replacement Governance

Replacement approval should consider:

- Defect evidence.
- personalization source.
- material/production cost.
- event urgency.
- repeat failure.

---

# 5.104 GiftHatke Enhanced QC

A replacement after enterprise error should normally receive stronger verification before dispatch.

This protects customer recovery.

---

# 5.105 GiftHatke Refund Governance

Customer Success may recommend refund.

Approvals and Finance execution remain governed.

Case closure requires actual refund completion where refund is the Resolution.

---

# 5.106 GiftHatke Recovery Discount Governance

Customer Success may propose recovery discount.

Domain 31 governs:

- Value.
- validity.
- stacking.
- authorization.

---

# 5.107 GiftHatke Shipping Complaint Governance

Shipping complaints should use authoritative:

- Tracking.
- carrier events.
- promised dispatch/delivery context.

Agents must not invent delivery dates.

---

# 5.108 GiftHatke Marketplace Governance

Marketplace service governance should preserve both:

- Marketplace-facing actions.
- internal Case truth.

A marketplace-issued refund must reconcile with Finance/Order state where applicable.

---

# 5.109 GiftHatke Corporate Service Governance

Corporate support may require:

- Dedicated Case owner.
- higher communication cadence.
- account-level visibility.
- escalation.

Commercial and operational facts remain authoritative in their domains.

---

# 5.110 GiftHatke Service Recovery Example

```text id="gift-service-recovery-example"
Corporate Order:
100 Personalized Gifts

Issue:
10 Units Damaged

↓

Impact Assessed

↓

Quality Confirms Damage

↓

Resolution:
10 Replacements

↓

Production Feasibility:
Confirmed

↓

Priority Production

↓

Enhanced QC

↓

Shipment

↓

Corporate Customer Follow-Up
```

---

# 5.111 GiftHatke High-Risk Resolution Example

```text id="gift-high-risk-resolution"
Customer Requests:
Full Refund + Replacement + 30% Future Discount

↓

Standard Policy:
Replacement OR Refund Depending Finding

↓

Agent Authority Insufficient

↓

Manager + Commercial Review

↓

Proportionate Resolution Approved
```

Customer pressure alone does not define remedy.

---

# 5.112 GiftHatke Service Governance Dashboard

Management should eventually monitor:

- Critical Cases.
- overdue Cases.
- SLA breaches.
- refund backlog.
- replacement backlog.
- recurring personalization failures.
- Shipping complaints.
- B2B risks.
- repeated recovery concessions.

---

# 5.113 Service Governance Metrics

Governance-health measures may include:

- Unassigned Case rate.
- reopened Case rate.
- refund approval exception rate.
- replacement recurrence.
- SLA pause rate.
- closure before downstream completion.
- policy exceptions.
- outdated template usage.

---

# 5.114 Governance Exception

Temporary governance exceptions may occur due to:

- System outage.
- unavailable approver.
- marketplace deadline.
- urgent recovery.

Each exception should record:

- Reason.
- scope.
- temporary authority.
- expiry.
- review.

---

# 5.115 Emergency Service Authority

Emergency authority may be necessary when immediate customer action is required.

Emergency authority still requires:

- Defined boundary.
- named accountable authority.
- audit.
- later review.

Urgency does not create unlimited power.

---

# 5.116 Service Governance Review Cadence

## Daily

- Critical Cases.
- SLA risk.
- escalations.

## Weekly

- Backlog.
- repeat failures.
- recovery actions.
- refund/replacement issues.

## Monthly

- Service Quality.
- Customer Health.
- policy exceptions.
- root-cause themes.

## Quarterly

- Service strategy.
- authority design.
- SLA appropriateness.
- automation maturity.

---

# 5.117 Service Governance Maturity Model

The permanent maturity progression is:

```text id="service-governance-maturity"
Ad Hoc Support

↓

Defined Service Processes

↓

Governed Case Management

↓

Integrated Customer Service

↓

Proactive Customer Success

↓

Intelligent Customer Operations
```

---

# 5.118 Ad Hoc Support

Characteristics:

- Disconnected messages.
- unclear ownership.
- inconsistent remedies.
- limited history.

This is not the target state.

---

# 5.119 Defined Service Processes

Characteristics:

- Cases.
- basic categories.
- owners.
- standard Resolutions.

---

# 5.120 Governed Case Management

Characteristics:

- Authority.
- SLAs.
- escalation.
- audit.
- refund/replacement control.

---

# 5.121 Integrated Customer Service

Characteristics:

- CRM, Orders, Personalization, Production, Quality, Shipping, Finance integrated.
- one customer Case view.
- resolution completion traceable.

---

# 5.122 Proactive Customer Success

Characteristics:

- Risk detection.
- proactive communication.
- Customer Health.
- recovery follow-up.
- B2B relationship support.

---

# 5.123 Intelligent Customer Operations

Characteristics:

- AI triage.
- predictive service risk.
- knowledge assistance.
- issue prevention.
- governance-aware automation.

Human accountability remains.

---

# 5.124 Service Knowledge Preservation

The enterprise should preserve:

- Why policy changed.
- why certain recovery approaches worked.
- which issues recur.
- which escalations were avoidable.
- which customer promises failed.
- what operational improvements reduced complaints.

This becomes organizational service memory.

---

# 5.125 SMP1 Governance Requirement

During **SMP1**, historical Customer/Order/service-relevant truth must be preserved.

New service governance may be introduced after migration.

It must not rewrite historical customer/business facts.

---

# 5.126 SMP1 No-Fabrication Rule

If the Apps Script baseline lacks:

- Formal Case.
- SLA.
- Resolution approval.
- service classification.

SMP1 must not fabricate these as historical facts.

Canonical rule:

```text id="smp1-service-no-fabrication"
Preserve What Existed

↓

Document What Did Not Exist

↓

Introduce Governed Service Model
After Cutover
```

---

# 5.127 Standalone v1.0 Governance Foundation

Standalone v1.0 should preserve foundations for:

- Stable Customer identity.
- Order/service relationships.
- audit logs.
- permissions.
- downstream status.

Advanced service authority structures may be progressively implemented.

---

# 5.128 ERP9 Governance Integration

ERP9 may introduce configurable:

- Case categories.
- priorities.
- queue settings.
- SLAs.
- Resolution types.
- escalation rules.
- recovery thresholds.

These configurations must inherit this Canon.

---

# 5.129 ERP10 Governance Certification

ERP10 should validate:

- Service authority.
- Case ownership.
- resolution consistency.
- refund/replacement governance.
- escalation.
- SLA integrity.
- closure integrity.
- customer-recovery controls.
- service auditability.
- frontline usability.

---

# 5.130 Permanent Governance Standards

The **Enterprise Customer Success, Service Management & Support Operations Domain** permanently follows:

- Empowerment within authority.
- facts before remedy.
- resolution authority before promise.
- fairness before arbitrary concession.
- ownership before handoff.
- completion before closure.
- customer outcome before metric protection.
- evidence before disciplinary interpretation.
- privacy before convenience.
- auditability before service certification.
- human accountability before irreversible automation.

---

# ENTERPRISE CUSTOMER SUCCESS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT & SUPPORT OPERATIONS CANON
## Stage 6 — Service Events, Omnichannel Synchronization & Customer Resolution Coordination Canon

---

# 6.1 Purpose

The **Enterprise Customer Success, Service Management & Support Operations Domain** requires a permanent event and synchronization architecture defining how customer-service state changes propagate across:

- Customer Service.
- CRM.
- Orders.
- Personalization.
- Production.
- Quality.
- Shipping.
- Finance.
- Commercial Governance.
- Knowledge.
- marketplace channels.
- communication systems.

Stages 1–5 established:

- Domain foundation.
- Service entity architecture.
- Case operating model.
- Service Management service architecture.
- Resolution authority and governance.

Stage 6 defines how material service changes become:

- Canonical service events.
- omnichannel synchronization signals.
- internal coordination triggers.
- customer communication triggers.
- resolution-completion signals.
- Customer Success alerts.
- service-risk signals.
- audit evidence.

The objective is:

> **One customer issue must remain one coherent service truth even when resolution spans many channels, teams, systems, and operational domains.**

---

# 6.2 Service Event Philosophy

A **Service Event** represents a verified change in customer-service state.

Examples:

- Case Created.
- Case Assigned.
- Customer Replied.
- SLA At Risk.
- Complaint Confirmed.
- Resolution Approved.
- Refund Completed.
- Replacement Shipped.
- Case Reopened.
- Case Closed.

Events communicate service facts.

They do not transfer authoritative ownership of underlying:

- Order.
- Shipment.
- payment.
- production.
- Product.

---

# 6.3 Permanent Event Principles

The Domain permanently follows:

---

## Authoritative State Before Event

A Case change must become committed before publication.

---

## Customer Meaning Before Transport

Whether an event moves by:

- Queue.
- webhook.
- API.
- stream.
- direct integration.

is secondary to its business meaning.

---

## One Case Before Channel Fragmentation

Multiple communication channels should converge into a coherent Case history.

---

## Idempotency Before Retry

Repeated delivery must not duplicate:

- Refund requests.
- replacements.
- escalations.
- customer messages.
- Case creation.

---

## Operational Fact Before Customer Assurance

Customer communication should follow verified business state.

---

## Correlation Before Isolation

Customer, Order, Case, Resolution, and operational actions should remain traceable end-to-end.

---

## Minimum Necessary Disclosure

Events must expose only required customer and commercial information.

---

# 6.4 Canonical Service Event Landscape

The permanent architecture includes the following event groups.

---

# Case Lifecycle Events

Examples:

- Case Created.
- Case Acknowledged.
- Case Assigned.
- Case Reassigned.
- Case Status Changed.
- Case Resolved.
- Case Closed.
- Case Reopened.
- Cases Merged.

---

# Customer Interaction Events

Examples:

- Customer Message Received.
- Customer Response Sent.
- Call Logged.
- Attachment Received.
- Customer Follow-Up Completed.

---

# Classification Events

Examples:

- Case Classified.
- Case Category Changed.
- Priority Changed.
- Severity Changed.

---

# SLA Events

Examples:

- SLA Started.
- SLA Paused.
- SLA Resumed.
- SLA At Risk.
- SLA Breached.
- SLA Completed.

---

# Investigation Events

Examples:

- Investigation Opened.
- Evidence Added.
- Internal Review Requested.
- Finding Recorded.
- Investigation Completed.

---

# Resolution Events

Examples:

- Resolution Proposed.
- Resolution Approval Requested.
- Resolution Approved.
- Resolution Rejected.
- Resolution Execution Started.
- Resolution Completed.
- Resolution Failed.

---

# Refund Events

Examples:

- Refund Requested.
- Refund Approved.
- Refund Processing.
- Refund Completed.
- Refund Failed.

---

# Replacement Events

Examples:

- Replacement Requested.
- Replacement Approved.
- Replacement Job Created.
- Replacement Produced.
- Replacement QC Passed.
- Replacement Shipped.
- Replacement Delivered.

---

# Return Events

Examples:

- Return Requested.
- Return Authorized.
- Return Received.
- Return Inspected.
- Return Completed.

---

# Recovery Events

Examples:

- Customer Recovery Requested.
- Recovery Approved.
- Recovery Instrument Created.
- Recovery Communicated.
- Recovery Completed.

---

# Escalation Events

Examples:

- Case Escalated.
- Functional Escalation Created.
- SLA Escalation Created.
- Executive Escalation Created.
- Escalation Resolved.

---

# Service Incident Events

Examples:

- Service Incident Detected.
- Incident Created.
- Customer Cases Linked.
- Incident Update Published.
- Incident Resolved.

---

# Customer Success Events

Examples:

- Success Action Created.
- Retention Risk Detected.
- Customer Health Changed.
- Proactive Contact Required.
- Recovery Follow-Up Due.

---

# Service Quality Events

Examples:

- Case Quality Review Requested.
- Case Quality Review Completed.
- Reopen Pattern Detected.
- Complaint Pattern Detected.
- Service Risk Detected.

---

# 6.5 Canonical Event Envelope

A material service event may include:

- Event ID.
- event type.
- event version.
- timestamp.
- effective timestamp where relevant.
- Case ID.
- Customer reference.
- related Order/Shipment/Refund reference.
- source service.
- actor/system.
- prior state where appropriate.
- new state.
- correlation ID.
- severity/classification.
- audit reference.

Exact schemas may evolve.

Business semantics remain permanent.

---

# 6.6 Event Publication Lifecycle

Canonical flow:

```text id="service-event-publication"
Service Action

↓

Validation / Authority

↓

Authoritative State Commit

↓

Audit Evidence

↓

Service Event Published

↓

Authorized Consumers
```

An event must not claim:

- Refund Completed.
- Replacement Shipped.
- Case Resolved.

before authoritative state confirms it.

---

# 6.7 Case Creation Event

Canonical flow:

```text id="case-created-event"
Incoming Customer Contact

↓

Normalize

↓

Existing Case Check

↓

Customer / Context Resolution

↓

Case Created

↓

Initial Interaction Stored

↓

CaseCreated Event
```

---

# 6.8 Duplicate Case Event Control

If the same inbound message is received twice because of integration retry:

The system should recognize the source event ID/thread ID and avoid creating two Cases.

---

# 6.9 Case Assignment Event

When ownership changes:

```text id="case-assignment-event"
Assignment Validated

↓

New Owner Committed

↓

CaseAssigned Event

↓

New Owner / Queue Notified
```

---

# 6.10 Reassignment Synchronization

Reassignment may update:

- Agent workspace.
- queue dashboard.
- notifications.
- SLA oversight.

The previous owner should no longer appear as authoritative owner after successful transfer.

---

# 6.11 Customer Reply Event

When a customer replies:

```text id="customer-reply-event"
Message Received

↓

Channel Source Preserved

↓

Case Matched

↓

Interaction Stored

↓

CustomerReplied Event

↓

Case Owner Alerted
```

---

# 6.12 Reply to Closed Case

If a customer replies to a recently closed Case, policy may:

- Reopen existing Case.
- create a related follow-up Case.

The original communication thread must remain traceable.

---

# 6.13 Omnichannel Conversation Synchronization

Canonical objective:

```text id="omnichannel-conversation"
Email

WhatsApp

Phone

Marketplace

Website

↓

One Service Timeline
```

The platform must preserve channel identity while presenting a unified service history.

---

# 6.14 Channel Source Integrity

A WhatsApp message must remain identifiable as WhatsApp.

An Amazon message must remain identifiable as Amazon.

Unification does not erase channel provenance.

---

# 6.15 Email Synchronization

Email integration should support:

- Thread matching.
- inbound capture.
- outbound delivery.
- delivery failure where available.
- attachment linkage.

Email threading errors must not silently attach one customer's message to another Case.

---

# 6.16 WhatsApp Synchronization

Future WhatsApp integration may support:

- Inbound service messages.
- outbound updates.
- media/attachment references.
- Case linking.

Customer consent and applicable communication rules remain binding.

---

# 6.17 Phone Call Synchronization

Phone interactions may be recorded through:

- Agent call log.
- integrated telephony.
- call disposition.

Where recordings exist, they require stronger privacy governance.

---

# 6.18 Marketplace Message Synchronization

Marketplace integrations may synchronize:

- Customer message.
- marketplace Order.
- marketplace Case reference.
- response status.

Internal GiftHatkeOS Case remains the enterprise service record where designated authoritative.

---

# 6.19 Social Channel Synchronization

Public/social complaints may require:

- Public response.
- private Case creation.
- identity matching.

Sensitive Order/customer information must not be exposed publicly.

---

# 6.20 SLA Start Event

SLA may start when:

- Case is created.

or according to explicit service policy.

The start event must record:

- Applicable SLA version.
- target times.
- Case context.

---

# 6.21 SLA Pause Event

A pause requires an approved reason such as:

- Waiting on Customer.

The event should record:

- Pause time.
- reason.
- actor/system.

---

# 6.22 SLA Resume Event

When required information arrives:

```text id="sla-resume-event"
Customer Reply

↓

Waiting Condition Cleared

↓

SLA Resumed

↓

Owner Alerted
```

---

# 6.23 SLA At-Risk Event

An SLA At-Risk event may trigger:

- Owner reminder.
- manager visibility.
- queue reprioritization.

This should occur before breach when practical.

---

# 6.24 SLA Breach Event

On actual breach:

```text id="sla-breach-event"
SLA Deadline Reached

↓

Required Action Incomplete

↓

Breach Recorded

↓

SLA_BREACHED Event

↓

Manager / Escalation Logic
```

The breach remains historical truth.

---

# 6.25 Investigation Event Flow

Canonical flow:

```text id="investigation-event-flow"
Investigation Opened

↓

Evidence Requests

↓

Evidence Added

↓

Finding Recorded

↓

Investigation Completed
```

---

# 6.26 Internal Domain Request Events

Customer Service may publish:

- Production Investigation Requested.
- Quality Review Requested.
- Shipment Investigation Requested.
- Finance Refund Review Requested.

These requests must connect to the originating Case.

---

# 6.27 Domain Response Events

Operational domains may return:

- Production Review Completed.
- Quality Finding Available.
- Shipment Investigation Completed.
- Refund Status Updated.

Customer Service then updates the Case.

---

# 6.28 Finding Recorded Event

A Finding Recorded event may include:

- Finding classification.
- confidence.
- evidence reference.

It should not expose unnecessary internal detail to every subscriber.

---

# 6.29 Resolution Proposed Event

A Resolution Proposal may trigger:

- Authority evaluation.
- Commercial approval.
- Finance review.
- operational feasibility checks.

---

# 6.30 Resolution Approved Event

When approved:

```text id="resolution-approved-event"
Resolution Decision

↓

Authority Committed

↓

Conditions Stored

↓

ResolutionApproved Event

↓

Execution Services Enabled
```

---

# 6.31 Resolution Rejected Event

A rejected proposed Resolution should preserve:

- Reason.
- approver.
- alternative action where applicable.

The Case remains active until another valid resolution exists.

---

# 6.32 Resolution Execution Started Event

This distinguishes:

- Approved resolution.

from:

- Actual execution.

Example:

**Replacement Approved** is not **Replacement Started**.

---

# 6.33 Resolution Completed Event

A resolution completes only when required downstream actions are confirmed.

Example:

```text id="resolution-completed"
Replacement Delivered

+

Required Customer Communication Sent

↓

Resolution Completed
```

---

# 6.34 Refund Coordination Events

Canonical sequence:

```text id="refund-event-sequence"
Refund Requested

↓

Refund Approved

↓

Finance Processing

↓

Refund Completed
```

Each is a distinct state/event.

---

# 6.35 Refund Failure Event

If Finance execution fails:

- RefundFailed event.
- Case owner notified.
- Case remains unresolved.
- customer communication may be required.

---

# 6.36 Refund Idempotency

A repeated **RefundRequested** event must not initiate multiple refunds.

A stable refund request identity is mandatory.

---

# 6.37 Replacement Event Sequence

```text id="replacement-event-sequence"
Replacement Approved

↓

Replacement Job Created

↓

Production Started

↓

Production Completed

↓

QC Passed

↓

Shipped

↓

Delivered

↓

Case Follow-Up
```

---

# 6.38 Replacement Failure Event

Potential failures:

- Production cannot complete.
- personalization missing.
- QC failed.
- shipment failed.

These must return to the Case owner.

---

# 6.39 Replacement Personalization Synchronization

Before remake:

```text id="replacement-personalization-sync"
Replacement Approved

↓

Correct Personalization Verified

↓

Production Job Created
```

This prevents repeating the original error.

---

# 6.40 Return Event Coordination

Return events may synchronize:

- Customer Service.
- Shipping.
- Warehouse/Inventory.
- Quality.
- Finance.

Example:

```text id="return-event-coordination"
Return Authorized

↓

Return Shipment

↓

Return Received

↓

Inspection

↓

Refund / Replacement Decision
```

---

# 6.41 Recovery Event Coordination

Recovery may involve:

- Service Case.
- Domain 31 commercial concession.
- Customer communication.

Canonical flow:

```text id="recovery-event-coordination"
Recovery Need Confirmed

↓

Commercial Approval

↓

Coupon / Discount Created

↓

Recovery Instrument Available

↓

Customer Communicated
```

---

# 6.42 Escalation Event Flow

Canonical escalation:

```text id="escalation-event-flow"
Trigger

↓

CaseEscalated

↓

Destination Notified

↓

Escalation Acknowledged

↓

Action

↓

Escalation Resolved
```

Case ownership remains separately tracked.

---

# 6.43 Executive Escalation Event

Executive escalation events should be reserved for material Cases.

They may include only summarized information necessary for decision-making.

---

# 6.44 Service Incident Detection Event

A systemic pattern may trigger:

- Incident suggestion.

Examples:

- 40 shipping delay Cases.
- repeated batch defect.
- widespread payment failure.

Human/rules review may confirm incident creation.

---

# 6.45 Incident-to-Case Linking

Canonical flow:

```text id="incident-case-linking"
Service Incident

↓

Affected Transaction / Customer Identification

↓

Existing Cases Linked

↓

Proactive Cases / Success Actions Created if Needed
```

---

# 6.46 Incident Update Coordination

Incident updates may be reused across:

- Internal teams.
- affected Case owners.
- customer communications.

Customer-facing messages should still respect individual context.

---

# 6.47 Incident Resolution Event

Incident resolution does not automatically mean every customer outcome is resolved.

Canonical rule:

```text id="incident-resolution-rule"
Underlying Incident Resolved

≠

Every Customer Case Resolved
```

---

# 6.48 Proactive Customer Success Event

A Customer Success event may be triggered before complaint creation.

Example:

```text id="proactive-success-event"
Personalization Missing

↓

Production Blocked

↓

Success Action Created

↓

Customer Contact
```

---

# 6.49 Shipping Delay Proactive Event

```text id="proactive-delay-event"
Shipping Delay Confirmed

↓

Affected Orders Identified

↓

Open Case?
YES → Update

NO → Customer Success Action / Proactive Case

↓

Customer Communication
```

---

# 6.50 Customer Health Change Event

Potential change:

```text id="customer-health-event"
Repeated Severe Case

+

Failed Recovery

↓

Customer Health:
Healthy → At Risk
```

Health-change logic must remain explainable.

---

# 6.51 Retention Risk Event

Retention Risk may trigger:

- Customer Success review.
- account-manager attention.
- follow-up.

It must not automatically create a discount.

---

# 6.52 B2B Account Service Events

Potential events:

- Corporate Case Escalated.
- Service Commitment Missed.
- Account Recovery Required.
- Corporate Follow-Up Due.

These may synchronize with CRM/Sales.

---

# 6.53 CRM Coordination

CRM may consume:

- Important Case status.
- Customer Health.
- severe complaint.
- recovery status.

Customer Service consumes authoritative:

- Customer identity.
- account owner.
- relationship context.

---

# 6.54 Order Coordination

Order Management may consume service commands/events requiring:

- Approved cancellation.
- modification.
- replacement relationship.

Customer Service must not mutate Order state directly outside certified interfaces.

---

# 6.55 Personalization Coordination

Personalization may publish:

- Details Missing.
- Customer Approval Required.
- Personalization Updated.

Customer Success may respond proactively.

---

# 6.56 Production Coordination

Production may publish:

- Remake Started.
- remake completed.
- production blocked.
- rush feasibility.

Customer Service uses this to communicate accurate status.

---

# 6.57 Quality Coordination

Quality may publish:

- Defect Confirmed.
- defect not confirmed.
- QC failure.
- corrective action initiated.

This feeds service findings and resolution.

---

# 6.58 Shipping Coordination

Shipping events may include:

- Dispatched.
- delayed.
- delivery exception.
- delivered.
- lost.

Customer Service should consume authoritative Shipping events rather than maintaining duplicate shipping truth.

---

# 6.59 Finance Coordination

Finance events may include:

- Refund Processing.
- Refund Completed.
- Refund Failed.

Customer Service consumes them to update the Case.

---

# 6.60 Commercial Coordination

Domain 31 may publish:

- Recovery Discount Approved.
- Coupon Created.
- Recovery Offer Expired.

Customer Service manages communication and outcome.

---

# 6.61 Workflow Coordination

Workflow may execute:

- Internal tasks.
- approval routing.
- escalation tasks.

Customer Service remains authoritative for the customer-facing Case.

---

# 6.62 Notification Coordination

Notification triggers may include:

- New urgent Case.
- SLA At Risk.
- customer replied.
- refund failed.
- replacement delivered.
- escalation overdue.

Notifications should be role-specific and actionable.

---

# 6.63 Knowledge Coordination

A service event such as:

- New Recurring Complaint Pattern Detected.

may trigger:

- Knowledge review.
- SOP update.
- article creation request.

---

# 6.64 Product Feedback Events

Repeated confirmed product complaints may produce:

**Product Service Risk Detected**

This can trigger Product review without automatically changing the Product.

---

# 6.65 Production Feedback Events

Repeated production-related findings may trigger:

- Production Quality Review Requested.
- SOP Review Recommended.

---

# 6.66 Shipping Feedback Events

Repeated carrier complaints may trigger:

- Carrier Performance Review.
- Packaging Review.

---

# 6.67 Finance Feedback Events

Repeated refund-processing failure may trigger:

- Finance Process Risk.
- payment integration review.

---

# 6.68 Service-to-Performance Coordination

Domain 30 may consume events for:

- SLA.
- Response Time.
- Resolution Time.
- reopen.
- Recovery Success.

Domain 32 remains authoritative for service-state semantics.

---

# 6.69 Data Governance Coordination

Domain 29 may identify:

- Customer identity conflict.
- missing Order mapping.
- untrusted shipment data.

Service processes must expose resulting uncertainty.

---

# 6.70 Security Coordination

Access to events must respect:

- Customer privacy.
- account ownership.
- Case sensitivity.
- refund details.
- internal notes.

---

# 6.71 Event Correlation

A correlation chain may connect:

```text id="service-event-correlation"
Customer Message

↓

Case

↓

Investigation

↓

Resolution

↓

Replacement

↓

Shipment

↓

Follow-Up
```

This creates end-to-end service traceability.

---

# 6.72 Correlation With Order

Case ID and Order ID should remain distinct.

Correlation allows:

- All Cases for Order.
- all Orders affected by Incident.
- all service actions resulting from one complaint.

---

# 6.73 Event Ordering

Event ordering matters.

Example:

```text id="refund-event-ordering"
Refund Approved

must precede

Refund Processing

must precede

Refund Completed
```

Out-of-order events must be handled safely.

---

# 6.74 Event Deduplication

Consumers must deduplicate repeated:

- CaseCreated.
- RefundCompleted.
- ReplacementJobCreated.
- CustomerMessageReceived.

Duplicate delivery must not duplicate business action.

---

# 6.75 Event Replay

Future systems may replay events to:

- Rebuild service timelines.
- rebuild projections.
- validate migration.
- reconstruct analytics.

Replay must not send customer communications or financial actions again unless explicitly in simulation mode.

---

# 6.76 Replay Side-Effect Safety

Permanent rule:

```text id="event-replay-sideeffect"
Event Replay

≠

Re-Execute External Business Effect
```

Replaying RefundCompleted should rebuild state.

It must not issue another refund.

---

# 6.77 Event Versioning

Service event schemas require:

- Version.
- compatibility.
- semantic documentation.

Changing technical payload must not silently change business meaning.

---

# 6.78 Timestamp Architecture

Events may preserve multiple times:

- Occurred At.
- Recorded At.
- effective At.
- received At.

This is useful for delayed marketplace/carrier integrations.

---

# 6.79 External Event Delay

An external shipment event may arrive late.

The system should preserve the real event time where available rather than pretending it occurred when received.

---

# 6.80 Service Failure Events

Potential failure events include:

- Case Intake Failed.
- Identity Resolution Failed.
- Outbound Message Failed.
- Refund Sync Failed.
- Replacement Creation Failed.
- Marketplace Sync Failed.
- SLA Processor Failed.

Critical failures require operational visibility.

---

# 6.81 Retry Architecture

Canonical flow:

```text id="service-event-retry"
Processing Failure

↓

Failure Recorded

↓

Retry Eligible?

↓

Idempotency Check

↓

Retry

↓

Success / Exception Queue
```

---

# 6.82 Dead-Letter / Exception Handling

Events that cannot be processed safely may enter a controlled exception queue.

Required information:

- Event.
- Case.
- error.
- severity.
- retry count.
- owner.
- resolution status.

---

# 6.83 Reconciliation

After synchronization failure:

```text id="service-reconciliation"
Authoritative Case / Domain State

vs

External / Projection State

↓

Difference

↓

Reconcile

↓

Audit
```

---

# 6.84 Customer Message Delivery Reconciliation

If system records:

**Message Sent**

but external provider reports delivery failure:

The Case must reflect the failure.

It must not imply the customer received the update.

---

# 6.85 Marketplace Reconciliation

Internal Case state may differ from marketplace ticket state.

Reconciliation should identify:

- Expected internal state.
- external state.
- reason for difference.
- required action.

---

# 6.86 External Refund Reconciliation

Where marketplace refunds occur externally, the architecture should reconcile:

- Marketplace refund.
- Order state.
- Finance state.
- Service Case.

---

# 6.87 Service Event Security

The event architecture requires:

- Authenticated producers.
- authorized consumers.
- encrypted transport where appropriate.
- audit.
- least-privilege access.

---

# 6.88 Customer Data Minimization

A generic CaseAssigned event generally does not need:

- Full address.
- full customer message.
- payment details.

The payload should contain only what the consumer needs.

---

# 6.89 Internal Note Exclusion

Internal Notes must not be included in broad service-event payloads unless a specific authorized consumer requires them.

---

# 6.90 Service Automation

Events may automate low-risk operations such as:

- Route Case.
- create internal task.
- send standard acknowledgment.
- remind owner.
- update SLA.
- schedule follow-up.

---

# 6.91 Automation Authority Boundary

Automation must not independently:

- Authorize material refund.
- approve major replacement.
- create large goodwill concession.
- close severe unresolved complaints.
- create false customer promises.

---

# 6.92 AI Event Consumption

AI may consume governed service events to:

- summarize Case development.
- identify patterns.
- detect escalation risk.
- predict SLA risk.
- recommend next actions.

---

# 6.93 AI Event Production

AI may publish:

- Case Classification Suggested.
- Service Risk Detected.
- Response Draft Generated.
- Resolution Recommendation Generated.

These are advisory events.

---

# 6.94 AI Recommendation Boundary

Permanent distinction:

```text id="ai-service-event-boundary"
AI Resolution Recommended

≠

Resolution Approved
```

---

# 6.95 AI Autonomous Low-Risk Actions

Future AI may autonomously perform approved low-risk actions such as:

- Categorize simple informational Case.
- route to correct queue.
- send receipt acknowledgment.

Each autonomous action remains auditable.

---

# 6.96 GiftHatke Event Specialization

GiftHatke requires event coordination across:

- Customer Success.
- personalization.
- Production.
- Quality.
- Shipping.
- marketplaces.
- Finance.

---

# 6.97 GiftHatke Personalization Missing Event

Canonical flow:

```text id="gift-personalization-missing-event"
Order Created

↓

Required Personalization Missing

↓

PersonalizationMissing Event

↓

Customer Success Action Created

↓

Customer Contacted

↓

Details Received

↓

Production Ready
```

---

# 6.98 GiftHatke Wrong Personalization Event

```text id="gift-wrong-personalization-event"
Complaint Case

↓

Personalization Investigation

↓

Enterprise Error Confirmed

↓

Replacement Approved

↓

Corrected Personalization Verified

↓

Remake Job
```

---

# 6.99 GiftHatke Production Defect Event

Canonical flow:

```text id="gift-production-defect-event"
Customer Damage / Defect Report

↓

Case

↓

Quality Assessment

↓

DefectConfirmed

↓

Replacement / Refund Decision

↓

Quality Feedback
```

---

# 6.100 GiftHatke Replacement Coordination Event

```text id="gift-replacement-coordination"
ReplacementApproved

↓

ReplacementJobCreated

↓

ProductionCompleted
```

This creates a practical daily operating system.

# 6.109 Event Observability

The platform should monitor:

- Service events produced.
- failed deliveries.
- processing latency.
- duplicate events.
- consumer lag.
- dead-letter events.
- marketplace integration failures.
- customer-message delivery failures.

---

# 6.110 Event Health Dashboard

A technical/operations view may show:

- Event type.
- volume.
- failure rate.
- oldest unprocessed event.
- retry count.
- affected Cases.

This protects service continuity.

---

# 6.111 Business Observability

Service managers should see business effects such as:

- Cases not assigned.
- refunds not synchronized.
- replacements stuck.
- customer replies not acknowledged.
- incident communications pending.

Technical observability must translate into business risk.

---

# 6.112 SMP1 Event Architecture Requirement

During **SMP1**, the standalone architecture may introduce:

- Event bus.
- queues.
- webhooks.
- message processors.
- communication connectors.

But these technologies must preserve certified service semantics.

Canonical rule:

```text id="smp1-service-event-rule"
Certified Customer / Order Truth

+

Canonical Service Events

+

Standalone Event Technology

=

Valid Service Evolution
```

---

# 6.113 SMP1 Historical Event Reconstruction

The Apps Script baseline may not contain native Case events.

If historical service-relevant activity is reconstructed:

It must be marked as:

- Reconstructed Historical Event.

and not confused with:

- Native post-cutover event.

---

# 6.114 SMP1 No-Fabrication Rule

A missing historical:

- SLA event.
- Case status event.
- Resolution approval event.

must not be invented merely to create a complete event history.

---

# 6.115 SMP1 Cutover Authority

For post-cutover Cases, one service platform must become authoritative.

Canonical transition:

```text id="smp1-service-authority-transition"
Legacy Business Context

↓

Standalone Service Shadow / Validation

↓

Controlled Cutover

↓

Standalone Service Authority

↓

Legacy Historical Reference
```

---

# 6.116 Dual-Write Risk

Uncontrolled dual Case entry between:

- Legacy notes/messages.
- standalone Case system.

can create fragmented customer history.

Cutover must clearly define where new service activity is recorded.

---

# 6.117 Standalone v1.0 Event Foundation

Standalone v1.0 should preserve:

- Stable Customer IDs.
- Order IDs.
- timestamps.
- communication references.
- audit trail.
- service relationship identifiers.

These support progressive event-driven Service Management.

---

# 6.118 ERP9 Event Integration

ERP9 service settings may publish events when:

- SLA policy changes.
- Case category changes.
- queue configuration changes.
- recovery threshold changes.

Configuration events should remain auditable.

---

# 6.119 ERP10 Event Certification

ERP10 should validate:

- Omnichannel Case continuity.
- Customer reply synchronization.
- SLA event correctness.
- refund/replacement event integrity.
- failure recovery.
- marketplace reconciliation.
- audit evidence.

---

# 6.120 Future Omnichannel Architecture

The Canon supports evolution toward:

```text id="future-omnichannel-architecture"
Customer Channels

↓

Unified Interaction Layer

↓

Case Management

↓

Operational Domains

↓

Resolution Orchestration

↓

Customer Communication

↓

Customer Success Intelligence
```

---

# 6.121 Future Autonomous Service Architecture

Future AI agents may respond to service events and perform approved low-risk workflows.

They remain bound by:

- Case authority.
- privacy.
- resolution governance.
- financial boundaries.
- human escalation requirements.

---

# 6.122 Service Event Quality Standards

Service Events must prioritize:

## Correctness

They represent real state.

## Timeliness

Material service changes propagate quickly enough.

## Idempotency

Duplicates do not duplicate business effect.

## Traceability

They link to the Case and source action.

## Privacy

They disclose minimum necessary information.

## Recoverability

Failures can be identified and reconciled.

---

# 6.123 Permanent Coordination Standards

The **Enterprise Customer Success, Service Management & Support Operations Domain** permanently follows:

- Authoritative state before event.
- one Case before channel fragmentation.
- source provenance before aggregation.
- operational fact before customer assurance.
- correlation before isolation.
- idempotency before retry.
- reconciliation after synchronization failure.
- minimum necessary customer data before distribution.
- auditability before automation.
- human authority before irreversible service action.

---

# ENTERPRISE CUSTOMER SUCCESS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT & SUPPORT OPERATIONS CANON
## Stage 7 — Customer Service Workspace, Agent Experience & Customer Success Command Center Canon

---

# 7.1 Purpose

The **Enterprise Customer Success, Service Management & Support Operations Domain** requires a permanent experience architecture through which:

- Service Agents.
- Customer Success Executives.
- supervisors.
- managers.
- B2B account teams.
- quality reviewers.
- Finance stakeholders.
- executives.
- future AI assistants.

interact with customer-service work.

Stages 1–6 established:

- Domain foundation.
- Service entity architecture.
- Case operating model.
- Service Management service architecture.
- Service Governance.
- Service Event and Omnichannel Coordination architecture.

Stage 7 defines how these capabilities become:

- Visible.
- understandable.
- actionable.
- role-aware.
- customer-centered.
- operationally efficient.

The objective is not merely to create a ticketing interface.

The objective is to create a unified **Customer Service Operating Workspace** that helps users answer:

- Which customers need attention now?
- What exactly happened?
- Which Order or Product is involved?
- What are we waiting for?
- Who owns the next action?
- Is the Case approaching SLA risk?
- What remedy is permitted?
- Has the refund or replacement actually completed?
- What should be communicated to the customer?
- Which recurring service problems require management action?

---

# 7.2 Service Experience Philosophy

The Domain permanently follows:

---

## Customer Story Before System Fragmentation

The user should see the customer's service story across relevant systems.

---

## Next Action Before Data Overload

The interface should make the next required action clear.

---

## Context Before Navigation

Agents should not repeatedly search separate modules for information already linked to the Case.

---

## Ownership Before Queue Noise

Each Case must clearly show who owns it.

---

## Actionability Before Dashboard Decoration

A service dashboard should lead users toward work.

---

## Customer Truth Before Internal Convenience

The experience should reflect actual service state, not what is easiest to display.

---

## Role Before Sensitive Detail

Internal cost, refund authority, private notes, and sensitive evidence must remain permission-controlled.

---

# 7.3 Canonical Experience Landscape

The permanent experience architecture includes:

- Customer Service Command Center.
- Customer Success Command Center.
- Agent Workspace.
- Supervisor Workspace.
- Case Workspace.
- Case Timeline.
- Customer 360 Service View.
- Order-Centric Service View.
- Omnichannel Interaction Workspace.
- Investigation Workspace.
- Resolution Workspace.
- Refund Workspace.
- Replacement Workspace.
- Return Workspace.
- Recovery Workspace.
- Escalation Workspace.
- SLA Workspace.
- Queue Management Workspace.
- B2B Service Workspace.
- Customer Health Workspace.
- Service Incident Workspace.
- Service Quality Workspace.
- Service Intelligence Workspace.
- Knowledge Assistance Panel.
- Service Audit Workspace.

---

# 7.4 Customer Service Command Center

The Customer Service Command Center should summarize:

## Immediate Attention

- Critical Cases.
- urgent Cases.
- SLA At Risk.
- overdue commitments.
- high-severity complaints.

## Operational Work

- New Cases.
- unassigned Cases.
- waiting internal dependencies.
- waiting on customer.
- reopened Cases.

## Resolution Operations

- Refunds pending.
- replacements pending.
- returns pending.
- recovery actions pending.

## Risk

- Severe aging Cases.
- repeated complaints.
- marketplace support failures.
- B2B account issues.
- major service incidents.

Its central question is:

> **What customer-service work requires attention right now?**

---

# 7.5 Priority-Based Attention Model

The Command Center may group work as:

```text id="service-attention-model"
Critical Now

↓

Due Soon

↓

Normal Active Work

↓

Waiting / Monitoring

↓

Follow-Up
```

This is more useful than presenting Cases only by creation date.

---

# 7.6 Customer Success Command Center

Customer Success requires a broader proactive view.

Potential sections:

- Orders blocked by missing customer input.
- customers affected by known delays.
- recovery follow-ups.
- B2B Customer Health risk.
- repeat-customer issues.
- proactive communication opportunities.
- customer retention risks.

The Command Center answers:

> **Which customer relationships can be protected before a complaint becomes worse?**

---

# 7.7 Agent Workspace

The frontline Agent Workspace should support a focused daily operating experience.

It may show:

```text id="agent-workspace"
My New Cases

↓

Urgent Cases

↓

Customer Replies

↓

Waiting Internal Teams

↓

SLA At Risk

↓

Refund / Replacement Follow-Ups

↓

Customer Follow-Ups
```

The interface should minimize unnecessary switching between modules.

---

# 7.8 Agent Workspace Principles

The Agent Workspace should prioritize:

- Work ownership.
- next action.
- customer context.
- due date.
- recent activity.
- authoritative operational status.

It should not overwhelm agents with every enterprise field.

---

# 7.9 Case List Experience

A Case list may show:

- Case ID.
- customer.
- issue.
- related Order.
- priority.
- status.
- owner.
- SLA state.
- last customer contact.
- next action.

Lists should support filtering and sorting without hiding high-risk Cases.

---

# 7.10 Case Row Signals

Visual signals may indicate:

- New customer reply.
- SLA At Risk.
- escalation.
- refund pending.
- replacement pending.
- internal blocker.
- customer waiting.

Warnings must not rely on color alone.

---

# 7.11 Case Workspace

The Case Workspace is the primary service execution surface.

Canonical layout may contain:

```text id="case-workspace-layout"
Customer + Case Header

↓

Issue Summary

↓

Order / Product / Shipment Context

↓

Current Status + Owner + SLA

↓

Conversation Timeline

↓

Investigation / Evidence

↓

Resolution / Internal Actions

↓

Next Action
```

---

# 7.12 Case Header

The Case header should immediately communicate:

- Case ID.
- customer.
- category.
- priority.
- severity.
- status.
- owner.
- SLA.
- related Order.

This prevents basic context from being buried.

---

# 7.13 Case Summary

The workspace may contain a concise summary answering:

- What is the customer reporting?
- What is currently known?
- What is pending?

AI may assist with summary generation.

Underlying source history remains authoritative.

---

# 7.14 Customer Statement Panel

The customer's original complaint/request should remain visible distinctly from internal findings.

Example:

```text id="customer-statement-panel"
Customer Says:
"Photo on the lamp is wrong."

Current Finding:
Investigation in progress
```

This avoids rewriting the customer's statement through internal interpretation.

---

# 7.15 Case Timeline

The timeline should combine:

- Customer messages.
- agent messages.
- internal notes.
- status changes.
- assignments.
- internal tasks.
- escalations.
- refund/replacement updates.
- customer follow-ups.

Canonical view:

```text id="case-timeline-view"
09:10 Customer Message

09:15 Case Created

09:22 Agent Response

10:05 Production Review Requested

10:42 Production Evidence Added

11:10 Resolution Proposed

11:30 Replacement Approved
```

---

# 7.16 Timeline Filtering

Users may filter timeline by:

- Customer Communication.
- Internal Actions.
- Status Changes.
- Financial Actions.
- Operational Actions.

Full history remains preserved.

---

# 7.17 Omnichannel Timeline

The same Case timeline may combine:

- Email.
- WhatsApp.
- phone.
- Amazon.
- website.

Each interaction must display its channel origin.

---

# 7.18 Customer 360 Service View

The Customer 360 Service View should help an authorized user understand:

- Open Cases.
- previous Cases.
- Orders.
- replacements.
- refunds.
- service-recovery history.
- Customer Health.
- B2B/account context.

---

# 7.19 Customer 360 Boundary

The service view should surface relevant relationship context without duplicating the full CRM.

CRM remains authoritative for Customer master data.

---

# 7.20 Customer Service History

Example:

```text id="customer-service-history"
Customer

Case 001
Delivery Question
Resolved

Case 012
Damaged Lamp
Replacement

Case 021
Current:
Missing Personalization
```

This provides continuity across agent changes.

---

# 7.21 Order-Centric Service View

An Order page should allow users to see:

- Related Cases.
- customer communication.
- personalization issues.
- refunds.
- replacements.
- shipment issues.

Canonical navigation:

```text id="order-service-view"
Order #1234

↓

Service Cases

↓

Case #87
Wrong Personalization

↓

Replacement #02
```

---

# 7.22 Personalization Context Panel

For personalized products, the Case may show:

- Submitted customer text.
- submitted image.
- source channel.
- approval state.
- production-used personalization.

This is critical for fair investigation.

---

# 7.23 Production Context Panel

Authorized service users may see:

- Production Job.
- state.
- production completion.
- remake feasibility.
- related QC.

They should not be able to directly manipulate Production state without authority.

---

# 7.24 Quality Context Panel

For defect Cases, the workspace may show:

- Quality finding.
- QC record.
- defect status.
- corrective action link.

This prevents service decisions from relying only on customer description where technical evidence exists.

---

# 7.25 Shipping Context Panel

The Case should provide:

- Carrier.
- tracking.
- latest scan.
- dispatch time.
- delivery status.
- exception.

This reduces manual switching between systems.

---

# 7.26 Finance Context Panel

Authorized users may see:

- Payment state.
- refund request.
- refund approval.
- Finance processing state.
- completion.

Customer-facing agents need clear state without requiring access to the full Finance module.

---

# 7.27 Current Next Action Panel

Every active Case should answer:

> **What needs to happen next?**

Examples:

- Reply to customer.
- wait for customer photo.
- chase Production.
- review replacement.
- refund processing.
- schedule follow-up.

This becomes one of the most important service UX elements.

---

# 7.28 Case Task Panel

Internal tasks may display:

- Task.
- owner.
- due date.
- status.
- dependency.

The Case owner should immediately see blockers.

---

# 7.29 Internal Dependency View

Example:

```text id="internal-dependency-view"

Finance

Action:
Confirm ₹799 refund

Requested:
Today 10:30

Due:
Today 15:00
```

This provides accountable internal coordination.

---

# 7.30 Investigation Workspace

For more complex Cases, the Investigation Workspace may organize:

- Investigation question.
- evidence.
- domain requests.
- hypotheses.
- findings.
- confidence.

---

# 7.31 Evidence Comparison Experience

For personalization disputes:

```text id="evidence-comparison"
Customer Submitted:
"Riya"

Production Input:
"Rina"

Final Product:
"Rina"

↓

Finding:
Internal transcription error
```

Side-by-side comparison improves fairness and speed.

---

# 7.32 Evidence Integrity Indicators

The UI may distinguish:

- Customer-provided evidence.
- authoritative system record.
- employee note.
- AI interpretation.

Not all information carries equal evidentiary weight.

---

# 7.33 Finding Experience

The Case should clearly distinguish:

- Customer allegation.
- factual evidence.
- internal finding.

```text id="finding-experience"
Finding:
Enterprise Error Confirmed

Confidence:
Confirmed

Evidence:
```

# 7.34 Resolution Workspace

The Resolution Workspace should help users select permitted outcomes.

It may show:

- Finding.
- standard policy.
- eligible resolutions.
- authority requirement.
- operational feasibility.

# 7.35 Resolution Recommendation Experience

```text id="resolution-recommendation"
Refund
```

```text id="resolution-authority-ui"
Within Your Authority
```

```text id="resolution-execution-tracker"
✓

✓

Production
In Progress

QC

Pending

Pending
```

# 7.42 Return Workspace

The Return Workspace may show:

- Eligibility.

- final outcome.

# 7.43 Recovery Workspace

# 7.45 Escalation Workspace

The Escalation Workspace may show:

- escalation owner.

- repeated functional escalation.

The SLA experience should show:

# 7.50 Queue Management Workspace

- oldest Cases.
- SLA risk.
- workloads.
- categories.

- Case count.
- severity.
- complexity.
- overdue work.

Not all Cases should be treated as equal units.

```text id="supervisor-workspace"
Recurring Service Problems
```

# 7.54 Manager Command Center

Customer Service managers may see:

- Service volume.

- aging.
- SLA.
- reopen.
- refund/replacement backlog.
- customer recovery.
