# ENTERPRISE SUPPLY CHAIN PLANNING & DEMAND INTELLIGENCE CANON
## Stage 7 — Supply Chain Planning Workspace, Planner Experience & Operations Command Center Canon

---

# 7.1 Purpose

The **Enterprise Supply Chain Planning & Demand Intelligence Domain** requires a permanent experience architecture through which planners, procurement teams, Production teams, Sales, Marketing, Finance, management, and future AI assistants interact with forward-looking demand, supply, inventory, supplier, and capacity information.

Stages 1–6 established:

- Domain foundation.
- canonical planning entity architecture.
- Planning Lifecycle.
- planning service architecture.
- Forecast and planning governance.
- planning events, synchronization, and orchestration.

Stage 7 defines how those capabilities become:

- Visible.
- understandable.
- actionable.
- role-aware.
- exception-driven.
- scenario-capable.
- decision-oriented.
- operationally useful.

The objective is not merely to display Forecast tables.

The objective is to create a unified **Supply Chain Planning Operating Workspace** that helps the enterprise answer:

- What demand is coming?
- Which demand is committed?
- Which Forecast changed?
- What will run short?
- When will it run short?
- Which supplier or resource is causing the constraint?
- What inventory is surplus?
- Which B2B commitment is at risk?
- Is the planned promotion supply-ready?
- What action should happen next?
- Which planning decisions require approval?
- How will one decision affect the rest of the supply chain?

---

# 7.2 Planning Experience Philosophy

The Domain permanently follows:

---

## Exception Before Data Flood

Users should see what requires action before they see thousands of normal planning lines.

---

## Time Before Quantity Alone

Every planning workspace should communicate when demand, supply, or capacity matters.

---

## Constraint Before Optimistic Plan

A Plan should visibly expose the thing preventing fulfillment.

---

## Committed Demand Before Forecast Noise

Confirmed customer commitments should remain easy to distinguish from probabilistic planning demand.

---

## Recommendation Before Blind Automation

Users should understand what the system recommends and why.

---

## Scenario Before Major Commitment

High-impact decisions should be explorable before execution.

---

## Traceability Before Convenience

Users should be able to drill from recommendation to the underlying demand, supply, and assumptions.

---

# 7.3 Canonical Planning Experience Landscape

The permanent experience architecture includes:

- Supply Chain Planning Command Center.
- Demand Planner Workspace.
- Supply Planner Workspace.
- Inventory Planning Workspace.
- Procurement Planning Workspace.
- Capacity Planning Workspace.
- Product Planning Workspace.
- Material Planning Workspace.
- Supplier Planning Workspace.
- Forecast Workspace.
- Demand Plan Workspace.
- Supply Plan Workspace.
- Shortage Management Workspace.
- Surplus Management Workspace.
- Planning Exception Workspace.
- Scenario Planning Workspace.
- Promotion Readiness Workspace.
- B2B Commitment Readiness Workspace.
- Seasonal Planning Workspace.
- Planning Approval Workspace.
- Planning Intelligence Workspace.
- Planning Audit Workspace.

---

# 7.4 Supply Chain Planning Command Center

The Command Center should summarize:

## Immediate Risks

- Critical Shortages.
- Supplier delays.
- capacity overloads.
- major B2B readiness failures.
- promotion readiness failures.
- time-sensitive material risks.

## Demand

- Committed Demand.
- Forecast changes.
- major demand spikes.
- new Sales opportunities.
- seasonal uplift.

## Supply

- Inventory coverage.
- inbound supply.
- supplier risk.
- Procurement Requirements.

## Capacity

- Machine overload.
- personalization workload.
- QC overload.
- packaging constraints.

## Exceptions

- Unacknowledged.
- overdue.
- unresolved critical exceptions.

The central question is:

> **What future supply-chain problem requires action before it becomes an operational failure?**

---

# 7.5 Attention Model

The Command Center may group work as:

```text id="planning-attention-model"
Critical Now

↓

Action Required Soon

↓

Monitor

↓

Normal Planning State

↓

Future Opportunity
```

This is preferable to presenting every planning record equally.

---

# 7.6 Planner Daily Workspace

A planner's daily workspace may prioritize:

```text id="planner-daily-workspace"
Critical Shortages

↓

Supplier ETA Changes

↓

Capacity Overloads

↓

Major Order / B2B Changes

↓

Promotion Readiness

↓

Planning Approvals

↓

Planning Exceptions
```

---

# 7.7 Planner Workspace Principles

The interface should prioritize:

- Need date.
- risk.
- affected demand.
- cause.
- recommendation.
- owner.
- next action.

---

# 7.8 Demand Planner Workspace

The Demand Planner should see:

- Baseline Forecast.
- current Consensus Forecast.
- committed Demand.
- Sales input.
- Marketing input.
- Forecast exceptions.
- Forecast Accuracy.

# ENTERPRISE SUPPLY CHAIN PLANNING & DEMAND INTELLIGENCE CANON
## Stage 8 — Demand Forecast Intelligence, Supply Chain Analytics, Predictive Risk & Optimization Canon

---

# 8.1 Purpose

The **Enterprise Supply Chain Planning & Demand Intelligence Domain** requires a permanent intelligence architecture capable of transforming historical demand, Forecasts, Supply Plans, inventory positions, supplier performance, Production capacity, shortages, surpluses, planning exceptions, and execution outcomes into actionable forward-looking intelligence.

Stages 1–7 established:

- Domain foundation.
- canonical planning entity model.
- planning lifecycle.
- planning service architecture.
- planning governance.
- planning events and synchronization.
- Planner Workspace and Operations Command Center.

Stage 8 defines how the enterprise progresses from:

```text id="planning-intelligence-progression"
What Happened?

↓

What Is Happening?

↓

Why Is It Happening?

↓

What Is Likely to Happen?

↓

What Should We Do?

↓

What Is the Best Governed Option?
```

The objective is not to maximize Forecast sophistication.

The objective is to improve:

- availability.
- fulfillment reliability.
- inventory discipline.
- supplier resilience.
- capacity utilization.
- seasonal readiness.
- working-capital efficiency.
- decision quality.

---

# 8.2 Supply Chain Intelligence Philosophy

The Domain permanently follows:

---

## Operational Truth Before Analytics

Forecast and optimization must originate from trustworthy business data.

---

## Forecast Error Before Forecast Confidence

Prediction quality should be measured against reality.

---

## Constraint Before Optimization

An optimized Plan that ignores physical constraints is invalid.

---

## Probability Before Certainty

Predictions remain probabilistic.

---

## Service Level and Working Capital Together

Planning intelligence should not optimize only:

- Stock availability.

or only:

- Inventory reduction.

The tradeoff must remain visible.

---

## Root Cause Before Parameter Change

Repeated shortages should be understood before blindly increasing Safety Stock.

---

## Recommendation Before Commitment

Optimization systems recommend.

Governed authorities commit.

---

# 8.3 Intelligence Capability Landscape

The permanent intelligence architecture includes:

| Capability | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Demand Intelligence | Understand demand patterns |
| Forecast Accuracy Intelligence | Measure Forecast quality |
| Forecast Bias Intelligence | Detect systematic error |
| Forecast Value Add | Evaluate human/model intervention |
| Demand Driver Intelligence | Explain changes |
| Seasonality Intelligence | Understand recurring demand |
| Promotion Intelligence | Evaluate campaign demand |
| Channel Intelligence | Compare Shopify/marketplace/B2B demand |
| Inventory Intelligence | Analyze future stock position |
| Stockout Intelligence | Understand shortage risk |
| Surplus Intelligence | Identify excess inventory |
| Safety Stock Intelligence | Optimize buffers |
| Replenishment Intelligence | Improve timing/quantity |
| Procurement Intelligence | Analyze purchasing readiness |
| Supplier Intelligence | Understand lead-time and reliability risk |
| Lead-Time Intelligence | Analyze variability |
| Capacity Intelligence | Understand future resource load |
| Bottleneck Intelligence | Identify limiting resources |
| Production Planning Intelligence | Compare planned vs actual load |
| Scenario Intelligence | Compare alternative futures |
| Allocation Intelligence | Support constrained-supply decisions |
| Planning Risk Intelligence | Identify emerging threats |
| Predictive Supply Intelligence | Anticipate disruptions |
| Prescriptive Planning | Recommend responses |
| Optimization Intelligence | Search for better tradeoffs |
| AI-Assisted Planning Intelligence | Accelerate analysis |

---

# 8.4 Demand Intelligence

Demand Intelligence should analyze:

- Quantity.
- growth.
- trend.
- volatility.
- seasonality.
- channel.
- Product.
- Customer/account segment.

The enterprise should understand not only:

**How much demand?**

but also:

**What is driving it?**

---

# 8.5 Demand Trend Intelligence

Potential states:

- Rising.
- stable.
- declining.
- volatile.
- event-driven.

---

# 8.6 Demand Growth Decomposition

Example:

```text id="demand-growth-decomposition"
Total Demand Growth:
+28%

Drivers:
Shopify +8%
Amazon +12%
Corporate +6%
Seasonal Effect +2%
```

This is more actionable than one aggregate percentage.

- confidence.

```text id="stable-vs-volatile-demand"
Product A
Stable weekly demand

Product B
Large irregular campaign spikes
```

These should not necessarily use the same planning model.

# 8.10 Forecast Accuracy Intelligence

- Historical Forecast.
- actual demand.

It should be evaluated by:

- Product.
- channel.
- horizon.
- demand segment.
- model.

---

# 8.11 Forecast Error

```text id="forecast-error"
Forecast

-

Actual

=

Forecast Error
```

The specific statistical measure may vary.

---

# 8.12 Absolute Forecast Error

Absolute error helps measure magnitude without positive/negative cancellation.

Domain 30 governs official KPI definitions.

---

# 8.13 Forecast Accuracy by Horizon

A Forecast may be highly accurate:

- One week ahead.

but weak:

- Three months ahead.

Accuracy should be horizon-aware.

---

# 8.14 Forecast Accuracy by Segment

Intermittent demand may naturally have lower Forecast precision.

Performance expectations should reflect demand behavior.

---

# 8.15 Forecast Bias Intelligence

- Overforecasting.
- underforecasting.

Persistent overforecast may create:

- Excess inventory.
- working-capital lock.
- obsolescence.
- unnecessary Production.

---

# 8.17 Underforecasting Impact

Persistent underforecast may create:

- Stockouts.
- emergency procurement.
- rush Production.
- customer delays.

---

# 8.18 Bias Pattern Detection

Potential pattern:

```text id="forecast-bias-pattern"
Rakhi Forecast

2014? — not relevant
Current Historical Cycles:

Consistently 20% below Actual

↓

Underforecast Bias
```

The system should use valid business history only and preserve period context.

# 8.19 Forecast Value Add

```text id="forecast-value-add"

12%

After Sales Override
7%

↓

Positive Value Add
```

# 8.20 Negative Forecast Value Add

```text id="negative-fva"

8%

After Manual Override:
19%

↓

Manual Override Reduced Forecast Quality
```

This should support process learning without assuming employee misconduct.

# 8.90 Predictive Supplier Delay Risk

Future models may estimate the probability of Supplier delay.

This remains a risk signal.

It does not alter confirmed Supplier status automatically.

---

# 8.91 Predictive Capacity Risk

Potential input:

- Demand.
- current jobs.
- machine downtime.
- Product mix.
- historical cycle time.

---

# 8.92 Predictive Promotion Risk

The system may estimate whether planned promotion is likely to produce:

- Material shortage.
- capacity overload.
- fulfillment degradation.

---

# 8.93 Predictive B2B Readiness

A corporate opportunity may be scored for operational feasibility based on:

- materials.
- Lead Time.
- capacity.
- required date.

---

# 8.94 Prescriptive Planning

Prescriptive planning recommends what action may improve the expected outcome.

Examples:

- Order earlier.
- Buy more.
- switch Supplier.
- increase temporary capacity.
- reduce promotion.
- reallocate inventory.

---

# 8.95 Prescriptive Recommendation Boundary

Permanent distinction:

```text id="prescriptive-boundary"
Recommended Action

≠

Approved Action

≠

Executed Action
```

---

# 8.96 Optimization Objective

Any optimizer must explicitly identify what it is trying to optimize.

Potential objectives:

- Minimize stockouts.
- minimize inventory.
- minimize emergency Procurement.
- maximize service level.
- balance capacity.

---

# 8.97 Multi-Objective Optimization

Real Supply Chain planning often requires balancing:

```text id="multi-objective-optimization"
Service Level

+

Inventory Cost

+

Supplier Risk

+

Capacity Feasibility

+

Commercial Priorities
```

There may be no single universally optimal answer.

---

# 8.98 Hard Constraints

Optimization must respect:

- Inventory reality.
- physical capacity.
- Supplier availability.
- Product/BOM rules.
- approvals.
- committed customer requirements.

---

# 8.99 Soft Constraints

Some constraints may be flexible at a cost.

Examples:

- Overtime.
- expedited freight.
- alternate Supplier.
- temporary Safety Stock breach.

The model should distinguish hard from soft constraints.

---

# 8.100 Optimization Explainability

```text id="optimization-explainability"
Recommended Plan:
Order 300 LED Bases Today

Why:
Projected Stockout in 8 Days
Supplier Lead Time 7 Days
Rakhi Demand Rising

Alternative:
Order 200
Risk: 35% stockout probability
```

- reorder points.

Recommendations should consider:

- demand.
- Lead Time.
- MOQ.
- service target.
- surplus risk.

---

# 8.102 Procurement Optimization

May help determine:

- Order timing.
- consolidation.
- Supplier option.

Procurement authority remains human/governed.

---

# 8.103 Capacity Optimization

May recommend:

- Job sequence.
- temporary overtime.
- capacity reallocation.
- alternate resource.

---

# 8.104 Scenario Optimization

- best service.
- lowest inventory.
- lowest risk.
- balanced recommendation.

---

- Demand.

- Suppliers.
- Production.
- capacity.
- Shipping.

This enables fast simulation.

The Digital Twin remains a planning model, not authoritative transaction truth.

- Order velocity.
- marketplace changes.
- campaign response.

---

# 8.107 Demand Sensing Boundary

Short-term demand sensing should not repeatedly destabilize longer-term Plans without material evidence.

- Sudden demand spike.

# 8.109 Anomaly Investigation

An anomaly is a signal.

# ENTERPRISE SUPPLY CHAIN PLANNING & DEMAND INTELLIGENCE CANON
## Stage 9 — Supply Chain Planning Migration, Forecast Reconciliation, Validation, Testing & Operational Certification Canon

---

# 9.1 Purpose

The **Enterprise Supply Chain Planning & Demand Intelligence Domain** requires a permanent assurance architecture proving that planning inputs, Forecasts, Demand Plans, Supply Plans, material requirements, inventory projections, supplier assumptions, capacity models, shortages, scenarios, and planning decisions remain trustworthy when:

- ERP platforms change.
- MRP systems change.
- APS systems change.
- Forecasting engines change.
- supplier integrations change.
- Product or BOM models evolve.
- capacity models are modernized.
- AI planning systems are introduced.

Stages 1–8 established:

- Domain foundation.
- planning entity model.
- Planning Lifecycle.
- planning service architecture.
- Planning Governance.
- planning event architecture.
- Planner and management experiences.
- predictive and optimization intelligence.

Stage 9 establishes the permanent framework for:

- Planning migration.
- historical Forecast preservation.
- Demand reconciliation.
- Supply reconciliation.
- Inventory planning validation.
- Procurement Requirement validation.
- capacity reconciliation.
- Supplier/Lead-Time migration.
- Safety Stock migration.
- Scenario preservation.
- Planning Exception migration.
- AI/model validation.
- operational acceptance.
- Supply Chain Planning certification.

The central principle is:

> **A planning platform may change, but the enterprise must still be able to prove what demand existed, what assumptions were used, what supply was expected, which constraints were known, what decision was made, and what actually happened.**

---

# 9.2 Planning Migration Philosophy

The Domain permanently follows:

---

## Transaction Truth Before Historical Planning Reconstruction

Historical operational facts are stronger than invented planning history.

---

## Original Forecast Before Recomputed Forecast

A historical Forecast should remain what was actually predicted at that time.

---

## Plan Meaning Before Field Mapping

A migrated number is useless if its planning semantics change.

---

## Version Before Overwrite

Forecasts, Plans, parameters, and scenarios require historical continuity.

---

## Relationship Before Record Count

Planning entities must remain connected to:

- Products.
- Materials.
- Orders.
- Suppliers.
- Purchase Orders.
- Production.

---

## Reconciliation Before Cutover

Planning continuity must be demonstrated, not assumed.

---

## No Fabrication Before Apparent Completeness

If historical Forecasts or planning approvals never existed, do not create them retrospectively.

---

# 9.3 Migration Scope

Potential planning migration scope includes:

- Demand Signals.
- Demand Forecasts.
- Forecast Versions.
- Forecast Adjustments.
- Demand Plans.
- Planning Horizons.
- Planning Periods.
- Seasonal Profiles.
- Promotion Demand Plans.
- B2B Opportunity Demand.
- Product Requirements.
- Material Requirements.
- Inventory Planning positions.
- Safety Stock policies.
- Reorder Points.
- Replenishment Requirements.
- Procurement Requirements.
- Procurement Plans.
- Supplier Lead Times.
- Supplier Capacity constraints.
- Supply Plans.
- Production Requirements.
- Capacity Requirements.
- Resource calendars.
- Shortages.
- Surpluses.
- Allocation Plans.
- Planning Exceptions.
- Scenarios.
- Planning Decisions.
- Risk acceptance.
- Planning Recommendations.
- Planning Snapshots.
- Forecast Accuracy history.
- AI/model versions.
- Planning Audit records.

---

# 9.4 Planning Migration Inventory

Before migration, create an inventory of planning-relevant objects.

Each object may record:

- Source object.
- business meaning.
- source system.
- owner.
- historical/current status.
- target representation.
- migration method.
- relationship dependencies.
- reconciliation method.
- certification status.

---

# 9.5 Source Classification

Historical information should be classified as:

- Authoritative Transaction Data.
- Native Planning Record.
- Derived Planning Projection.
- Manual Planning Assumption.
- Analytical Forecast.
- Reconstructed Planning Context.
- Unstructured Planning Evidence.

This classification determines how the data may be migrated.

---

# 9.6 Product Identity Migration

Planning requires stable Product identity.

Migration must preserve:

- Product IDs.
- variants.
- Product families.
- lifecycle status.

A Forecast linked to the wrong Product is a critical defect.

---

# 9.7 Material Identity Migration

Material IDs must remain stable or permanently mapped.

Critical attributes may include:

- Material type.
- dimensions.
- thickness.
- unit of measure.
- variant/specification.

---

# 9.8 Unit-of-Measure Migration

Migration must preserve UOM meaning.

Example:

```text id="uom-migration"
Legacy:
Acrylic = 20

Unknown whether:
Sheets
Pieces
Square Feet

↓

Migration Blocked Until Semantics Resolved
```

Ambiguous units are unsafe for planning.

---

# 9.9 Supplier Identity Migration

Supplier records should preserve:

- Supplier identity.
- relevant Material relationships.
- Lead-Time history where available.
- supplier-status context.

---

# 9.10 Order History Migration

Historical demand analytics depend on reliable Orders.

Preserve:

- Order ID.
- Order Line.
- Product.
- quantity.
- Order date.
- relevant due/fulfillment dates.
- channel.
- cancellation status.

---

# 9.11 Demand History Reconciliation

Historical demand should reconcile against authoritative Order/transaction history.

Planning systems must not silently alter actual past demand to fit a model.

---

# 9.12 Demand Signal Migration

Where formal Demand Signals exist, preserve:

- Signal source.
- quantity.
- period.
- confidence.
- reference.
- timestamp.

---

# 9.13 Historical Demand Signal Limitation

If historical Demand Signals were never captured separately:

Do not infer a complete historical signal stream from final sales records.

---

# 9.14 Forecast Migration

Native historical Forecasts should preserve:

- Forecast ID.
- period.
- quantity.
- method.
- version.
- created-at.
- scope.

---

# 9.15 Forecast Version Integrity

A migration must not collapse:

- Forecast v1.
- Forecast v2.
- Forecast v3.

into only the latest value where historical evaluation matters.

---

# 9.16 Forecast Timestamp Integrity

A Forecast produced on 1 August must remain identifiable as information available on 1 August.

It must not be updated using information learned later.

---

# 9.17 Forecast Method Migration

Where available, preserve:

- Method name.
- version.
- model reference.
- assumptions.

If unavailable:

- Method = Not Historically Captured.

---

# 9.18 Forecast Adjustment Migration

Historical overrides should preserve:

- Baseline Forecast.
- adjusted quantity.
- reason.
- actor.
- date.

---

# 9.19 Adjustment Evidence Limitation

If only final adjusted Forecast is available:

Do not invent the original baseline or override reason.

---

# 9.20 Demand Plan Migration

Historical Demand Plans should preserve:

- Plan version.
- effective periods.
- committed demand.
- Forecast contribution.
- approved adjustments.
- final planned demand.

---

# 9.21 Plan Status Mapping

Legacy statuses must be mapped semantically.

Example:

```text id="plan-status-mapping"
Legacy:
Final

Target:
Approved?

Only if legacy "Final"
actually represented approval.
```

---

# 9.22 Plan Approval Migration

Where approvals exist, preserve:

- Approver.
- time.
- conditions.

If no formal approval existed, do not fabricate one.

---

# 9.23 Seasonal Profile Migration

Historical seasonal profiles may preserve:

- Event.
- Product scope.
- uplift.
- periods.
- version.

---

# 9.24 Promotion Planning Migration

Where historical campaign planning exists, preserve:

- Promotion.
- baseline.
- uplift assumption.
- actual dates.
- Product/channel.

---

# 9.25 B2B Opportunity Planning Migration

Historical opportunity-based demand should preserve:

- Opportunity.
- probability.
- quantity.
- expected date.
- conversion outcome.

---

# 9.26 B2B Double-Count Reconciliation

Ensure historical planning did not double count:

- Opportunity demand.
- Converted Order demand.

If a legacy defect existed, document it rather than silently reinterpret history.

---

# 9.27 Product Requirement Migration

Preserve where available:

- Product.
- quantity.
- Need-By.
- source Demand Plan.

---

# 9.28 Material Requirement Migration

Material Requirements should preserve:

- Material.
- quantity.
- need date.
- source Product Requirement.
- BOM version.
- wastage/yield.

---

# 9.29 BOM Migration

BOM migration is critical.

Preserve:

- BOM ID.
- version.
- effective dates.
- components.
- quantities.
- units.

---

# 9.30 Historical BOM Integrity

Historical requirements should remain linked to the BOM applicable at that time.

Do not recalculate historical Material Requirements using only the latest BOM.

---

# 9.31 Wastage Assumption Migration

Where formal assumptions exist:

Preserve:

- Percentage/fixed factor.
- Product/process.
- effective period.

# 9.32 Inventory History Migration

Planning continuity depends on trustworthy Inventory state.

Preserve:

- Stock movements.
- receipts.
- reservations.
- adjustments.
- write-offs.
- quarantine where available.

Domain 2 remains authoritative.

---

# 9.33 Inventory Planning Snapshot Migration

Historical planning snapshots may preserve:

- On-hand.
- allocated.
- inbound.
- projected balance.
- date.

These remain distinct from transactional Inventory truth.

# 9.34 Safety Stock Migration

Historical Safety Stock values should preserve:

- Item.
- value.
- policy/method.
- effective date.

# 9.35 No-Retroactive-Safety-Stock Rule

A new Safety Stock policy must not be applied retrospectively as though it governed historical Plans.

---

# 9.36 Reorder Point Migration

Preserve where available:

- Item.
- threshold.
- method.
- effective period.

---

# 9.37 Replenishment Requirement Migration

- status.

---

# 9.38 Procurement Requirement Migration

Preserve:

- Required quantity.
- Need-By.

- status.
- release reference.

```text id="procurement-migration-reconciliation"
↓

Receipt
```

**Confirmed inbound**

unless actual PO/supplier commitment exists.

# 9.41 Supplier Lead-Time Migration

- approval.

# 9.46 Production Requirement Migration

Preserve:

- Working hours.

- downtime.

where used for historical planning.

---

# 9.51 Capacity Availability Migration

Historical available capacity should not be reconstructed from today's staffing/machine availability.

---

# 9.52 Shortage Migration

Historical native Shortage records should preserve:

- Item/resource.
- quantity gap.
- detected date.
- expected impact date.
- severity.
- cause.
- outcome.

---

# 9.53 Historical Shortage Reconstruction Boundary

A past stockout may be known from transactions.

That does not mean a **Shortage Risk** was known beforehand.

Do not fabricate predictive detection.

---

# 9.54 Surplus Migration

Historical surplus records should preserve:

- Item.
- quantity.
- reason.
- period.
- resolution.

---

# 9.55 Allocation Migration

Where formal allocation decisions exist, preserve:

- Available quantity.
- demand lines.
- allocation.
- rationale.
- authority.

---

# 9.56 Reservation Reconciliation

Planning allocation should reconcile with actual Inventory reservations where available.

---

# 9.57 Planning Exception Migration

Preserve native exceptions such as:

- Material Shortage.
- Supplier Delay.
- Capacity Overload.
- Forecast Anomaly.

---

# 9.58 Exception History Integrity

Historical exceptions should preserve:

- Detection time.
- acknowledgment.
- action.
- closure/acceptance.

---

# 9.59 Scenario Migration

Historical scenarios used for decisions should preserve:

- Baseline.
- assumptions.
- result.
- decision linkage.
- owner.

---

# 9.60 Scenario Isolation Validation

Migrated scenarios must not be confused with:

- Active Plan.

---

# 9.61 Planning Decision Migration

Historical material decisions should preserve:

- Issue.
- options.
- chosen action.
- rationale.
- approver.
- outcome.

---

# 9.62 Risk Acceptance Migration

Where shortage or planning risk was explicitly accepted:

Preserve:

- Risk.
- scope.
- approver.
- date.
- mitigation.

---

# 9.63 Planning Recommendation Migration

Recommendations should remain distinct from actual decisions.

---

# 9.64 Planning Snapshot Migration

Snapshots may be used to reconstruct what the planner saw at a particular time.

They must be clearly separated from current state.

---

# 9.65 Forecast Accuracy Migration

Historical Forecast accuracy may only be computed if:

- Historical Forecast existed.
- timestamp/version are trustworthy.
- actual demand is available.

---

# 9.66 No-Reconstructed-Accuracy Rule

If no historical Forecast existed:

Do not create a synthetic historical Forecast and then present its accuracy as historical business performance.

---

# 9.67 AI Model Migration

If historical AI models existed, preserve where practical:

- Model.
- version.
- deployment dates.
- outputs.

---

# 9.68 AI Recommendation Migration

Preserve distinction among:

- AI recommendation.
- human decision.
- execution.

---

# 9.69 Planning Audit Migration

Historical audit should preserve material actions such as:

- Forecast override.
- Plan approval.
- Safety Stock change.
- shortage acceptance.
- requirement release.
- allocation decision.

# 9.70 Planning Reconciliation Framework

Canonical sequence:

```text id="planning-reconciliation-framework"
Certified Source State

↓

Migrated Planning State

↓

Compare

↓

Difference

↓

Classify

↓

Correct / Accept / Document

↓

Re-Test

↓

Certify
```

# 9.71 Reconciliation Difference Classes

- Exact Match.
- Expected Representation Difference.
- Approved Technical Transformation.
- Approved Business Correction.
- Legacy Defect.
- Historical Data Gap.
- Migration Defect.
- Unexplained Difference.

Material unexplained differences block certification.

# 9.89 Planning Test Architecture

The permanent testing model includes:

1. Master Data Tests.
2. Demand Signal Tests.
3. Forecast Tests.
4. Forecast Version Tests.
5. Demand Plan Tests.
6. BOM/Material Requirement Tests.
7. Inventory Projection Tests.
8. Safety Stock Tests.
9. Replenishment Tests.
10. Procurement Planning Tests.
11. Supplier/Lead-Time Tests.
12. Supply Plan Tests.
13. Production Requirement Tests.
14. Capacity Planning Tests.
15. Shortage/Surplus Tests.
16. Allocation Tests.
17. Scenario Tests.
18. Event Synchronization Tests.
19. AI Planning Tests.
20. Migration/Reconciliation Tests.
21. Business Acceptance Tests.

---

# 9.90 Product Master Testing

Validate:

- Product IDs.
- variants.
- lifecycle.
- mapping.

---

# 9.91 Material Master Testing

Validate:

- IDs.
- specifications.
- dimensions.
- UOM.

---

# 9.92 Supplier Master Testing

Validate Supplier/material relationships and permissions where relevant.

---

# 9.93 Demand Signal Testing

Test:

- Confirmed Order Signal.
- B2B Opportunity.
- Marketing promotion.
- duplicate Signal.

---

# 9.94 Demand Deduplication Testing

Controlled case:

```text id="demand-deduplication-test"
Corporate Opportunity:
500 units

Then Order Confirmed:
500 units

Expected:
500 committed demand

NOT:
1,000 demand
```

---

# 9.95 Forecast Generation Testing

Validate:

- Correct scope.
- period.
- method.
- quantity.
- confidence.
- version.

---

# 9.96 Forecast Reproducibility Testing

Where deterministic methodology applies:

Same source snapshot + same model/version should produce expected result within defined tolerance.

---

# 9.97 Forecast Version Testing

Generate v1 and v2.

Expected:

- v1 preserved.
- v2 current.
- no overwrite.

---

# 9.98 Forecast Override Testing

Validate:

- Baseline retained.
- adjustment.
- reason.
- expiry.
- audit.

---

# 9.99 Forecast Expiry Testing

Temporary promotion uplift should cease after configured period.

---

# 9.100 Demand Plan Testing

Validate:

- Committed Demand included.
- Forecast included correctly.
- no double counting.
- approvals.

---

# 9.101 Demand Cancellation Testing

Cancel Order.

Expected:

- Committed demand reduced.
- downstream requirements recalculated.
- existing POs not silently deleted.

---

# 9.102 BOM Explosion Testing

Controlled example:

```text id="bom-explosion-test"
100 Lamps

Each requires:
1 LED Base
0.2 Acrylic Sheet Equivalent

Expected:
100 LED Bases
20 Acrylic Sheet Equivalent
before wastage
```

---

# 9.103 BOM Version Testing

Future requirements must use correct effective BOM.

Historical requirements remain on historical BOM.

---

# 9.104 UOM Conversion Testing

Validate conversions where required.

Ambiguous conversion must fail safely.

---

# 9.105 Wastage/Yield Testing

Validate expected material requirement after:

- wastage.
- yield.

---

# 9.106 Inventory Projection Testing

Test:

```text id="inventory-projection-test"
Opening:
100

Inbound:
50

Demand:
120

Expected Projected Balance:
30
```

subject to reservation/Safety Stock rules.

---

# 9.107 Reservation Testing

Reserved Inventory should not be counted as freely available if policy excludes it.

---

# 9.108 Quarantine Testing

Quarantined stock should not satisfy planning demand where unusable.

---

# 9.109 Safety Stock Testing

Validate:

- Policy resolution.
- calculated buffer.
- effective date.
- override.

---

# 9.110 Safety Stock Override Testing

Temporary override should preserve:

- Original.
- override.
- expiry.
- authority.

---

# 9.111 Net Requirement Testing

Controlled example:

```text id="net-requirement-test"
Gross Requirement:
500

Usable Inventory:
200

Confirmed Inbound:
150

Safety Requirement:
50

Expected Net Requirement:
200
```

according to certified netting semantics.

---

# 9.112 Replenishment Testing

Projected Shortage should generate one appropriate open Replenishment Requirement.

---

# 9.113 Replenishment Idempotency Testing

Repeat same planning run.

Expected:

- no duplicate active requirement.

---

# 9.114 Procurement Requirement Testing

Validate:

- Net Requirement.
- Need-By.
- Supplier.
- MOQ.
- latest safe Order date.

---

# 9.115 MOQ Testing

Example:

```text id="moq-test"
Net Requirement:
42

MOQ:
50

Expected Recommended Purchase:
50

Expected Planned Surplus:
8
```

---

# 9.116 Supplier Lead-Time Testing

Validate correct back-scheduling from:

- Need-By.
- Lead Time.
- receiving time.

---

# 9.117 Supplier Delay Testing

Change ETA.

Expected:

- Projected balance recalculated.
- shortage risk updated.

---

# 9.118 Partial Receipt Testing

If PO 100 and only 40 received:

Expected:

- Inventory +40.
- Remaining inbound 60.
- not +100 stock.

---

# 9.119 Purchase Order Cancellation Testing

Cancelled PO must be removed from expected Supply.

---

# 9.120 Supply Plan Testing

Validate:

- Confirmed Supply.
- planned Supply.
- timing.
- gaps.

---

# 9.121 Planned-vs-Confirmed Supply Testing

A planned purchase must not appear as confirmed inbound.

---

# 9.122 Production Requirement Testing

Validate:

- Product.
- quantity.
- need date.
- source Demand Plan.

---

# 9.123 Production Release Idempotency

Repeated release must not create duplicate Production Jobs.

---

# 9.124 Capacity Requirement Testing

Example:

```text id="capacity-requirement-test"
300 Units

5 Minutes Laser Each

Expected:
1,500 Minutes
25 Hours
```

---

# 9.125 Capacity Calendar Testing

Scheduled maintenance should reduce Available Capacity.

---

# 9.126 Capacity Overload Testing

If required hours > available hours:

Expected:

- Capacity Overload Exception.
- affected demand visible.

---

# 9.127 Bottleneck Testing

With:

- Materials ready.
- Laser ready.
- QC overloaded.

Expected:

- QC identified as constraining resource.

---

# 9.128 Shortage Detection Testing

Validate:

- quantity gap.
- shortage date.
- source.
- impact.

---

# 9.129 Timing Shortage Testing

Supply arriving after need date should still create shortage even if total horizon supply is sufficient.

---

# 9.130 Surplus Detection Testing

Validate surplus after:

- demand cancellation.
- MOQ.
- promotion decline.

---

# 9.131 Allocation Testing

Constrained supply should allocate according to approved policy.

---

# 9.132 Allocation Audit Testing

Validate:

- who approved.
- reason.
- impacted demand.

---

# 9.133 Scenario Isolation Testing

Run:

- Demand +40%.

Expected:

- Scenario changes.
- active Plan unchanged.

---

# 9.134 Scenario Adoption Testing

When adopted:

- New Plan version created.
- assumptions preserved.
- old Plan remains historical.

---

# 9.135 Planning Exception Testing

Validate:

- Detection.
- ownership.
- acknowledgment.
- escalation.
- closure.

---

# 9.136 Risk Acceptance Testing

Accepted Shortage Risk must preserve:

- Authority.
- rationale.
- impact.

---

# 9.137 Event Deduplication Testing

Replay same OrderConfirmed event.

Expected:

- no duplicate demand.

---

# 9.138 Out-of-Order Event Testing

Deliver events out of sequence.

Expected:

- system reconciles current authoritative state.
- no invalid planning projection.

---

# 9.139 Event Replay Testing

Replay historical planning events.

Expected:

- projections rebuilt.
- no duplicate POs.
- no duplicate Production Jobs.

---

# 9.140 Planning Run Failure Testing

Simulate Forecast or Capacity engine failure.

Expected:

- Last valid Plan retained.
- stale/incomplete warning.
- no false approval.

---

# 9.141 Source-System Failure Testing

Simulate:

- Inventory unavailable.
- Supplier integration unavailable.
- Production unavailable.

Planning must show reduced confidence or stale state.

---

# 9.142 AI Forecast Testing

Validate:

- Grounding.
- model/version.
- no invented demand.
- uncertainty.

---

# 9.143 AI Recommendation Testing

AI recommendation must not automatically:

- issue PO.
- create Production Job.
- change Customer commitment.

---

# 9.144 AI Constraint Testing

Prompt AI to create Plan ignoring unavailable machine capacity.

Expected:

- Hard constraints preserved.

---

# 9.145 AI Hallucination Testing

Prompt for unavailable Supplier ETA.

Expected:

- AI reports missing data.

Not an invented date.

---

# 9.146 AI Scenario Testing

AI-generated Scenario should remain isolated until adopted.

---

# 9.147 Security Testing

Validate permissions for:

- Forecast modification.
- Plan approval.
- Safety Stock.
- Supplier information.
- scenario adoption.
- risk acceptance.
- requirement release.

---

# 9.148 Audit Testing

Validate material actions preserve:

- Actor/system.
- timestamp.
- previous state.
- new state.
- reason where required.

---

# 9.149 Planning Performance Testing

Test:

- Forecast calculation at expected scale.
- Material Requirement explosion.
- scenario calculation.
- exception queue.
- planner workspace.

Correctness remains primary.

- Festival Orders.
- marketplace import.
- large B2B Order.
- mass inventory update.

---

# 9.151 Event Storm Testing

# 9.152 Reconciliation Testing

- Order change.
- inventory receipt.
- Supplier ETA change.
- Production completion.

# 9.153 Planning Search Testing

- Forecast.
- Shortage.
- Supplier.
- Material.
- Scenario.

---

# 9.154 GiftHatke Acrylic Testing

- thickness.
- sheet size.
- yield.
- wastage.
- Supplier.

# 9.158 GiftHatke Laser Capacity Testing

# 9.159 GiftHatke QC Capacity Testing

# 9.177 Certification Gates

The permanent Planning Operational Certification Gates are:

## Gate 1 — Planning Data Inventory

Critical planning inputs identified.

## Gate 2 — Semantic Mapping

Source and target meanings validated.

## Gate 3 — Product/Material Identity Integrity

Planning entities map correctly.

## Gate 4 — Historical Forecast Integrity

Existing Forecasts preserved without hindsight contamination.

## Gate 5 — Demand/Supply Relationship Integrity

Requirements remain traceable.

## Gate 6 — Inventory/Procurement Integrity

Supply assumptions reconcile.

## Gate 7 — Capacity Integrity

Planning resource semantics preserved.

## Gate 8 — Exception/Scenario Integrity

Risks and alternatives remain traceable.

## Gate 9 — Authority, Security & Audit

Planning controls remain intact.

## Gate 10 — Business Acceptance

Operational users approve readiness.

---

# 9.178 Certification States

Possible outcomes:

- Fully Certified.
- Certified With Controlled Exceptions.
- Not Certified.

Material unexplained differences block full certification.

---

# 9.179 Controlled Exceptions

Examples may include:

- Historical Forecasts unavailable.
- old Lead-Time history missing.
- old capacity standards undocumented.
- seasonal planning existed only in spreadsheets.
- supplier capacity not historically captured.

Each exception requires:

- Description.
- scope.
- business impact.
- risk.
- treatment.
- owner.
- approval.

---

# 9.180 Legacy Planning Defects

Migration may expose:

- Duplicate demand.
- incorrect Lead Time.
- stale Safety Stock.
- wrong BOM.
- overcounted inbound supply.
- impossible capacity.

These should not be blindly reproduced without assessment.

---

# 9.181 Legacy Defect Treatment

Canonical process:

```text id="legacy-planning-defect-treatment"
Legacy Planning Defect

↓

Evidence Captured

↓

Impact Assessed

↓

Preserve Historical Record

and/or

Correct Current Planning State

↓

Governed Decision

↓

Audit
```

---

# 9.182 Active Planning Cutover

If native planning is active during migration:

Preserve:

- Current Forecast version.
- Demand Plan.
- Supply Plan.
- open Requirements.
- Shortages.
- scenarios.
- accepted Risks.

---

```text id="active-plan-cutover"

↓

Demand / Supply / Inventory References

↓

Target Plan Imported

↓

Open Exceptions Imported

↓

Requirement Links Validated

↓

Target Planner Acceptance
```

---

# 9.184 Active Procurement Requirement Protection

Open planning requirement already converted to PO must not generate a new PO after cutover.

---

# 9.185 Active Production Requirement Protection

Existing Production Job must remain linked to imported planning requirement where applicable.

---

# 9.186 Active Shortage Protection

Critical open Shortages must remain visible immediately after cutover.

---

# 9.187 Active Scenario Protection

If a Scenario is currently under decision review:

Its assumptions and status should migrate.

---

# 9.188 Dual-Planning Authority Risk

The enterprise must not operate two independent active Demand/Supply Plans during cutover without explicit governance.

---

# 9.189 Source-System Authority During Cutover

Each source domain needs one authoritative writer for:

- Orders.
- Inventory.
- Purchase Orders.
- Production.

---

# 9.190 Synchronization Cutover

Planning integrations should be switched in controlled sequence so the target does not miss:

- New Orders.
- Inventory movements.
- Supplier changes.
- Production events.

---

# 9.191 Planning Cutover Reconciliation

Immediately after cutover, reconcile:

- Committed Demand.
- Projected Supply.
- Inventory.
- POs.
- critical Shortages.
- Capacity.

---

# 9.192 Rollback Requirement

Rollback planning must protect any new post-cutover:

- Forecasts.
- Plan approvals.
- Procurement Requirements.
- Production Requirements.
- risk decisions.
- planning events.

---

# 9.193 Rollback Prohibition

Rollback cannot simply delete newly approved planning obligations.

They must be reconciled back into the authoritative operating environment.

---

# 9.194 SMP1 Mandatory Planning Assurance

Stage 9 is binding for **SMP1** wherever planning-relevant information is migrated.

SMP1 cannot declare Planning Readiness merely because:

- Orders migrated.
- inventory migrated.

It must ensure that the information required to create reliable future plans remains trustworthy.

# ENTERPRISE SUPPLY CHAIN PLANNING & DEMAND INTELLIGENCE CANON
## Stage 10 — Final Enterprise Supply Chain Planning & Demand Intelligence Certification Canon

---

# 10.1 Purpose

The **Enterprise Supply Chain Planning & Demand Intelligence Domain** is hereby consolidated into one final authoritative enterprise specification.

Stages 1–9 established:

- Domain foundation and planning scope.
- Demand, Supply, Inventory Planning, and Capacity entity architecture.
- Demand Planning lifecycle and Supply Balancing operating model.
- Planning services and execution architecture.
- Forecast authority and Planning Governance.
- planning events, synchronization, and orchestration.
- Planner Workspaces and Supply Chain Command Center.
- Demand Forecast Intelligence, predictive risk, and optimization.
- migration, reconciliation, testing, and operational certification.

Stage 10 formally certifies Domain 33 as the permanent GiftHatkeOS architecture for:

- Demand Planning.
- Demand Forecasting.
- Supply Planning.
- Inventory Planning.
- Replenishment Planning.
- Procurement Planning.
- Material Requirements Planning.
- Production Requirement Planning.
- Capacity Planning.
- Supplier Planning.
- shortage management.
- Surplus Management.
- allocation planning.
- Scenario Planning.
- Seasonal Planning.
- Promotional Planning.
- B2B Demand Planning.
- Supply Chain Intelligence.
- Predictive Risk.
- Prescriptive Planning.
- optimization.

The Domain exists to ensure that forward-looking enterprise decisions remain:

- Evidence-based.
- time-aware.
- constraint-aware.
- economically disciplined.
- operationally feasible.
- explainable.
- governed.
- auditable.
- technically portable.

---

# 10.2 Final Canon Mission

The permanent mission is:

> **Convert trusted demand signals into explainable, governed, and actionable supply plans so that the enterprise can satisfy customer demand while protecting working capital, operational feasibility, service levels, and supply-chain resilience.**

The Domain must enable the enterprise to answer:

- What demand is committed?
- What demand is forecast?
- When will demand occur?
- Which Products and materials will be required?
- What inventory will remain available?
- What supply is already confirmed?
- What supply is only planned?
- What material will become short?
- When will the shortage occur?
- Which Supplier is creating risk?
- What Production capacity is required?
- Which resource is the bottleneck?
- What inventory may become surplus?
- Which scenarios should management consider?
- What action is recommended?
- Who has authority to commit the action?
- What actually happened compared with the Plan?

---

# 10.3 Certified Permanent Principles

The Domain permanently follows:

- Demand before replenishment.
- committed demand before Forecast.
- source truth before planning projection.
- baseline Forecast before override.
- time before quantity alone.
- Gross Requirement before Net Requirement.
- Inventory Position before purchase recommendation.
- confirmed Supply before proposed Supply.
- Lead Time before shortage.
- capacity before customer promise.
- constraint before optimization.
- Scenario before major commitment.
- exception before crisis.
- service level and working capital together.
- probability before certainty.
- explanation before automated action.
- recommendation before execution.
- reconciliation before certification.
- human accountability before irreversible autonomous planning.

---

# 10.4 Certified Domain Boundary

Domain 33 permanently owns the planning meaning for:

- Demand Signals.
- Demand Forecasts.
- Forecast Versions.
- Demand Plans.
- Supply Plans.
- Product Requirements.
- Material Requirements.
- Inventory Planning projections.
- Safety Stock.
- Reorder Points.
- Replenishment Requirements.
- Procurement Requirements.
- Production Requirements.
- Capacity Requirements.
- Shortages.
- Surpluses.
- Allocation Plans.
- Planning Exceptions.
- Scenarios.
- Planning Recommendations.
- Planning Risk.
- Supply Chain Intelligence.

It does **not** replace:

- Order Management.
- Inventory & Procurement.
- Production & Manufacturing.
- Sales.
- Marketing.
- Commercial Governance.
- Product.
- Shipping.
- Finance.

Canonical relationship:

```text id="domain33-boundary"
Orders / Sales / Marketing / Product / Market Signals

↓

Domain 33
Demand & Supply Planning

↓

Inventory / Procurement / Production / Capacity Requirements

↓

Execution Domains

↓

Actual Results

↓

Planning Learning
```

---

# 10.5 Certified Relationship With Order Management

Order Management owns:

- Confirmed Order.
- Order Line.
- quantity.
- customer commitment.
- due date.

Domain 33 consumes this as:

**Committed Demand.**

Permanent distinction:

```text id="order-vs-forecast"
Confirmed Order
=
Committed Demand

Forecast
=
Expected Future Demand
```

Forecasts must never overwrite accepted customer commitments.

---

# 10.6 Certified Relationship With Inventory & Procurement

Domain 2 remains authoritative for:

- Physical inventory.
- inventory movements.
- reservations.
- Purchase Orders.
- supplier transactions.
- receipts.

Domain 33 owns forward-looking calculations such as:

- Projected Available Balance.
- Net Requirement.
- Replenishment Requirement.
- Procurement Requirement.
- Shortage Risk.

---

# 10.7 Certified Relationship With Production

Production owns:

- Production Jobs.
- manufacturing execution.
- work centers.
- actual completion.
- actual Production state.

Domain 33 owns:

- Production Requirement.
- Capacity Requirement.
- future load.
- capacity gap.
- bottleneck prediction.

Permanent distinction:

```text id="production-planning-boundary"
Production Requirement
=
Planning Need

Production Job
=
Executable Manufacturing Work
```

Sales contributes:

- expected quantity.
- probability.
- required date.

Sales pipeline remains probabilistic until converted to committed business demand.

# 10.17 Certified Demand Signal Principle

Every material demand input should preserve its origin where practical.

Potential sources:

- Confirmed Order.
- Sales Opportunity.
- Historical Demand.
- Marketing Campaign.
- Marketplace Forecast.
- Seasonal Event.
- Manual Planning Input.
- Statistical/AI Forecast.

# 10.18 Certified Demand Classification

Demand may be classified as:

- Committed.
- Highly Probable.
- Forecast.
- Promotional.
- Seasonal.
- Strategic.
- Exploratory.

The enterprise must not treat all demand signals as equally certain.

---

# 10.19 Certified Forecast Architecture

Every Forecast should preserve:

- Scope.
- Product/Material.
- period.
- quantity.
- method/model.
- version.
- confidence.
- generated time.

---

# 10.20 Certified Forecast Versioning

Permanent rule:

```text id="forecast-versioning"
Forecast v1

↓

Forecast v2

↓

Forecast v3
```

v1 and v2 remain historical evidence.

Forecast history must not be overwritten by current values.

---

# 10.21 Certified Forecast vs Actual

Permanent distinction:

```text id="forecast-vs-actual"
Forecast
=
What Was Expected

Actual
=
What Happened
```

Historical Forecasts must not be retrospectively changed to match actual demand.

---

# 10.22 Certified Forecast vs Target

Forecast and target remain different.

```text id="forecast-vs-target"
Target
=
Desired Business Outcome

Forecast
=
Expected Future Outcome
```

A Forecast must not be manipulated merely to equal target.

---

# 10.23 Certified Baseline Forecast

The baseline statistical/model Forecast remains visible even after:

- Sales override.
- Marketing adjustment.
- management intervention.

---

# 10.24 Certified Forecast Adjustment

A material manual Forecast change preserves:

- Baseline.
- adjustment.
- reason.
- actor.
- effective period.
- approval where required.

---

# 10.25 Certified Consensus Demand

Canonical model:

```text id="consensus-demand"
Baseline Forecast

+

Committed Demand

+

Approved Business Adjustments

↓

Consensus Demand Plan
```

Double counting must be prevented.

---

# 10.26 Certified B2B Probability Planning

A corporate Opportunity may contribute:

```text id="b2b-weighted-demand"
Expected Quantity

×

Probability

=

Probability-Weighted Demand
```

- probabilistic contribution is removed.
- confirmed Order becomes Committed Demand.

---

```text id="demand-plan-lifecycle"
Reviewed

↓

Approved

↓
```

```text id="seasonal-planning"
Current Growth
```

# 10.35 Certified Gross Requirement

---

# 10.36 Certified Net Requirement

```text id="net-requirement-final"
Gross Requirement

-

Usable Inventory

-

Confirmed Inbound

+

Required Safety Stock

=

Net Requirement
```

---

# 10.37 Certified Inventory Position

Planning Inventory Position may include:

- On-hand.
- usable.
- reserved.
- allocated.
- inbound.
- projected.

---

# 10.38 Certified Projected Available Balance

Canonical relationship:

```text id="projected-balance-final"
Opening Inventory

+

Expected Receipts

-

Requirements

=

Projected Available Balance
```

The balance should be time-phased.

---

# 10.39 Certified Safety Stock

Safety Stock protects uncertainty in:

- Demand.
- Lead Time.
- quality.
- Supplier reliability.
- Production.

It must remain governed and explainable.

---

# 10.40 Certified Safety Stock Tradeoff

Permanent relationship:

```text id="safety-stock-tradeoff"
Higher Safety Buffer

↓

Higher Service Protection

+

Higher Working Capital
```

The enterprise must consciously balance both.

---

# 10.41 Certified Reorder Point

Conceptually:

```text id="reorder-point-final"
Expected Demand During Lead Time

+

Safety Stock

=

Reorder Point
```

Implementation may use more advanced logic.

---

# 10.42 Certified Replenishment Requirement

A Replenishment Requirement is a planning need.

It is not an executed procurement or Production commitment.

---

# 10.43 Certified Procurement Requirement

Permanent distinction:

```text id="procurement-boundary-final"
Procurement Requirement
=
Planning Need

Purchase Order
=
Executed Procurement Commitment
```

---

# 10.44 Certified Supplier Lead-Time Architecture

Planning should distinguish where possible:

- Standard Lead Time.
- observed Lead Time.
- temporary Lead-Time override.
- Supplier ETA.

Average Lead Time alone may be insufficient where variability is high.

---

# 10.45 Certified Supplier Capacity

Known Supplier capacity constraints should remain visible.

Planning must not assume unlimited supply.

---

# 10.46 Certified Supply Plan

Supply Plan may combine:

- Current Inventory.
- confirmed inbound supply.
- proposed procurement.
- planned Production.

Supply certainty should remain explicit.

---

# 10.47 Certified Planned vs Confirmed Supply

Permanent distinction:

```text id="planned-confirmed-final"
Planned Purchase
≠
Confirmed PO

Confirmed PO
≠
Supplier Confirmed

Supplier Confirmed
≠
Inventory Received
```

---

# 10.48 Certified Production Requirement

Production Requirement is forward-looking manufacturing demand.

It becomes actual work only through Production release.

---

# 10.49 Certified Capacity Requirement

Capacity Planning may represent:

- Machine hours.
- labor hours.
- personalization/design hours.
- QC hours.
- packaging throughput.

---

# 10.50 Certified Available Capacity

Available Capacity considers:

- Work calendar.
- staffing.
- maintenance.
- existing load.
- downtime.

Theoretical maximum capacity must not automatically equal usable capacity.

---

# 10.51 Certified Capacity Balance

Canonical relationship:

```text id="capacity-balance-final"
Required Capacity

vs

Available Capacity

↓

Balanced
or
Overloaded
```

---

# 10.52 Certified Bottleneck

The limiting resource should be explicitly identifiable.

Examples:

- Material.
- laser.
- QC.
- packaging.
- Supplier.

---

# 10.53 Certified Shortage Architecture

A Shortage represents expected inability to satisfy requirement in time.

Potential types:

- Material.
- Product.
- Supplier.
- Production Capacity.
- Packaging.
- Shipping Capacity.

---

# 10.54 Certified Shortage Timing

Total future supply being sufficient does not eliminate a timing shortage.

```text id="timing-shortage"
Need:
Week 1

Supply:
Week 2

↓

Week 1 Shortage Exists
```

---

# 10.55 Certified Shortage Impact

Material shortages should identify:

- Affected Product.
- affected Orders.
- affected dates.
- quantity gap.
- mitigation window.

---

# 10.56 Certified Shortage Lifecycle

```text id="shortage-lifecycle-final"
Potential Risk

↓

Confirmed Planning Shortage

↓

Mitigation

↓

Execution

↓

Resolved
or
Risk Accepted
```

---

# 10.57 Certified Surplus Architecture

A Surplus represents materially excess projected supply.

Potential causes:

- Overforecast.
- cancelled demand.
- MOQ.
- Product decline.
- seasonal end.

---

# 10.58 Certified Allocation Architecture

Where supply is constrained:

```text id="allocation-final"
Available Supply

↓

Governed Allocation Policy

↓

Demand Allocation

↓

Unmet Demand
```

Allocation must remain explainable.

---

# 10.59 Certified Allocation Priority

Potential legitimate factors include:

- Confirmed commitment.
- contractual requirement.
- due date.
- event date.
- strategic B2B commitment.

---

# 10.60 Certified Planning Exception

A Planning Exception represents a condition requiring intervention.

Examples:

- Forecast Spike.
- Shortage.
- Supplier Delay.
- Capacity Overload.
- Surplus.
- stale Plan.
- missing BOM.
- missing Lead Time.

---

# 10.61 Certified Exception Lifecycle

```text id="exception-lifecycle-final"
Detected

↓

Acknowledged

↓

Investigated

↓

Action Planned

↓

Resolved
or
Risk Accepted
```

---

# 10.62 Certified Scenario Planning

Scenario Planning allows controlled evaluation of alternative futures.

Examples:

- Demand +40%.
- Supplier delay +7 days.
- machine downtime.
- large B2B Order.
- promotion surge.

---

# 10.63 Certified Scenario Isolation

Permanent rule:

```text id="scenario-isolation-final"
Scenario

≠

Active Plan
```

A Scenario alters active planning only after formal adoption.

---

# 10.64 Certified Scenario Comparison

Scenarios may compare:

- Demand.
- Inventory.
- Procurement.
- Shortage.
- capacity.
- customer risk.
- working-capital implication.

---

# 10.65 Certified Planning Decision

Material decisions should preserve:

- Problem.
- options.
- chosen action.
- rationale.
- authority.
- expected impact.

---

# 10.66 Certified Planning Recommendation

Permanent distinction:

```text id="recommendation-boundary-final"
Recommendation

≠

Approved Decision

≠

Executed Commitment
```

---

# 10.67 Certified Risk Acceptance

Management may consciously accept planning risk.

Acceptance requires:

- Scope.
- expected impact.
- rationale.
- authority.
- mitigation where relevant.

Silent risk is prohibited.

---

# 10.68 Certified Planning Lifecycle

The permanent lifecycle is:

```text id="planning-lifecycle-final"
Demand Signals

↓

Forecast

↓

Demand Review

↓

Demand Plan

↓

Requirements

↓

Inventory / Supply Netting

↓

Supply Plan

↓

Constraint Detection

↓

Scenario / Mitigation

↓

Plan Approval

↓

Execution Handoff

↓

Actuals

↓

Variance / Learning
```

---

# 10.69 Certified Planning Cycle

Planning may operate through:

- Daily exception review.
- weekly planning.
- monthly review.
- seasonal/event planning.
- emergency replanning.

---

# 10.70 Certified Rolling Planning

Planning should continuously refresh as:

- Orders change.
- Inventory moves.
- Supplier dates change.
- Production changes.
- campaigns evolve.

But the process must avoid unnecessary instability.

---

# 10.71 Certified Freeze Window

Near-term Plan periods may be protected from frequent changes.

Major exceptions may override the freeze through authority.

---

# 10.72 Certified Planning Nervousness Control

Small Forecast noise should not constantly trigger:

- PO changes.
- Production rescheduling.
- allocation changes.

Materiality and tolerance are permanent planning controls.

---

# 10.73 Certified Demand Review

Demand Review focuses on:

- Forecast.
- committed Orders.
- B2B pipeline.
- campaigns.
- seasonality.
- Product launches.

---

# 10.74 Certified Supply Review

Supply Review focuses on:

- Inventory.
- Purchase Orders.
- Suppliers.
- Material Requirements.
- Production Capacity.
- bottlenecks.

---

# 10.75 Certified Demand-Supply Reconciliation

The core management question is:

> **Can the current Supply Plan satisfy the governed Demand Plan at the required time?**

---

# 10.76 Certified S&OP-Style Planning

GiftHatkeOS may use an appropriately scaled integrated planning process:

```text id="sop-final"
Demand Review

↓

Supply Review

↓

Constraint Review

↓

Commercial / Finance Context

↓

Management Decision

↓

Agreed Plan
```

The process need not become bureaucratic to be governed.

---

The permanent service landscape includes:

- Demand Signal Service.

- Forecast Service.

- Forecast Adjustment Service.
- Demand Plan Service.

- Planning Recommendation Service.
- Planning Decision Service.
- Plan Approval Service.

- Planning Intelligence Service.
- Planning Audit Service.

Examples:

- GenerateForecast.

Planning releases requirements.

Execution domains create commitments.

```text id="plan-execution-boundary-final"

↓

Authorized Release

↓

Operational Domain

↓

Purchase Order / Production Job / Reservation
```

Planning must prevent duplicate:

- Demand Signals.
- Procurement Requirements.
- Production Requirements.
- release actions.
- planning exceptions.

```text id="safe-failure-final"
Incomplete / Stale / Low Confidence

NOT

Invent Feasibility
```

```text id="planning-event-topology-final"

↓

Planning Consumer

↓

Exception / Recommendation

Governed Action
```

# 10.85 Certified Event Idempotency

Repeated delivery must not duplicate:

- Demand.
- requirements.
- execution requests.

# 10.86 Certified Event Ordering

# 10.87 Certified Replay Safety

```text id="replay-safety-final"

≠

Repeat Procurement
or
Repeat Production Commitments
```

# 10.88 Certified Eventual Consistency

# 10.89 Certified Planning Governance Roles

Permanent roles include:

- Enterprise Planning Authority.

- Inventory Planner.
- Procurement Planner.
- Capacity Planner.
- Planning Approver.

# 10.90 Certified Authority Principle

# 10.91 Certified Separation of Duties

```text id="planning-sod-final"
↓

Approver

Execution Domain

↓

Auditor
```

# 10.94 Certified Allocation Authority

# 10.95 Certified Shortage Acceptance Authority

# 10.96 Certified Emergency Planning Authority

- accuracy.

# 10.103 Certified Capacity Experience

Capacity view should identify:

- Demand Intelligence.
- Forecast Accuracy.
- Forecast Bias.

- Channel Intelligence.

# 10.108 Certified Forecast Accuracy

Forecast quality should be assessed by:

- Product.
- channel.
- horizon.
- demand segment.
- method.

One universal accuracy expectation is not always appropriate.

# 10.109 Certified Forecast Bias

Persistent overforecasting and underforecasting should be identified separately.

---

The enterprise should evaluate whether:

- Sales overrides.
- Marketing adjustments.
- human judgment.
- AI models.

actually improve Forecast quality.

---

# 10.111 Certified Demand Driver Intelligence

Possible drivers:

- Seasonality.
- promotion.
- Product launch.
- marketplace activity.
- B2B conversion.
- price change.

Correlation must not automatically be presented as causation.

# 10.112 Certified Stockout Intelligence

The enterprise should understand:

- Future stockout date.
- quantity gap.
- cause.
- affected demand.
- warning lead time.

---

# 10.113 Certified Surplus Intelligence

Surplus should be analyzed by:

- Quantity.
- age.
- cause.
- seasonality.
- reuse.
- obsolescence risk.

---

# 10.114 Certified Supplier Intelligence

Planning should understand:

- Lead-Time variability.
- Supplier delays.
- capacity limits.
- critical-material dependence.

---

# 10.115 Certified Capacity Intelligence

Capacity Intelligence should distinguish:

- Machine.
- design.
- assembly.
- QC.
- packaging.

One aggregate Production percentage is insufficient where bottlenecks differ.

---

# 10.116 Certified Predictive Planning

Future predictive capability may estimate:

- Demand.
- Stockout Risk.
- Supplier delay.
- capacity overload.
- Promotion Risk.
- B2B feasibility.

# 10.117 Certified Prescriptive Planning

Future systems may recommend:

- Increase procurement.
- expedite Supplier.
- use alternate Supplier.
- increase temporary capacity.
- reallocate stock.
- reduce promotion.

Optimization must preserve:

- Physical constraints.
- Product rules.
- Supplier limits.
- customer commitments.
- authority.

Planning may balance:

```text id="multi-objective-final"
Customer Service Level

+

Working Capital

+

Supplier Risk

+

Capacity Feasibility

+

Commercial Priority
```

AI may assist with:

- Forecasting.
- demand segmentation.
- anomaly detection.
- shortage prediction.
- root-cause explanation.
- Scenario generation.
- replenishment recommendation.

# 10.121 Certified AI Grounding

- Orders.
- Inventory.
- Purchase Orders.
- Suppliers.
- BOM.
- Production.
- capacity.
- Plan versions.

# 10.122 Certified AI Authority Boundary

- Create binding Purchase Order.

- authorize capacity investment.
- promise customer delivery.
- rewrite planning history.

```text id="ai-recommendation-final"
≠

Approved Plan

≠

Executed Business Commitment
```

- prediction outcome.

# ENTERPRISE MANUFACTURING EXCELLENCE & INDUSTRIAL OPERATIONS CANON
## Stage 1 — Domain Foundation, Manufacturing Excellence Scope & Industrial Operations Architecture Canon

---

# 1.1 Purpose

The **Enterprise Manufacturing Excellence & Industrial Operations Domain** establishes the permanent architecture for how GiftHatkeOS measures, stabilizes, improves, and optimizes manufacturing execution after production demand has been released into the shop-floor environment.

This Domain sits above and around operational manufacturing execution.

It does not replace the existing **Production & Manufacturing Domain**.

Instead, it answers questions such as:

- Are we producing efficiently?
- Where are we losing capacity?
- Which work center is constraining throughput?
- Which Products take longer than expected?
- Where is rework increasing?
- How much time is lost to setup, waiting, breakdowns, quality failures, and missing inputs?
- Are Production standards realistic?
- Are machines being used effectively?
- Are rush Jobs destabilizing normal flow?
- Are replacements consuming hidden Production capacity?
- Which processes should be improved first?
- Are process improvements actually working?
- Is Production becoming more stable over time?

The permanent objective is:

> **Create a measurable, stable, continuously improving manufacturing system where throughput, quality, capacity, equipment, people, and process flow are managed as one coherent operational reality.**

---

# 1.2 Domain Mission

The permanent mission is:

> **Measure, control, and continuously improve how manufacturing work is executed so that customer demand is converted into reliable output with minimal avoidable delay, waste, rework, downtime, and operational instability.**

The Domain must help GiftHatke answer:

- What was planned to be produced?
- What was actually produced?
- How long did it take?
- What capacity was consumed?
- What was waiting?
- What failed?
- What was reworked?
- What was scrapped?
- Which machine or process constrained the flow?
- Which causes repeatedly create delay?
- Which improvement should be prioritized?
- What measurable result followed the improvement?

---

# 1.3 Manufacturing Excellence Philosophy

The Domain permanently follows:

---

## Flow Before Local Activity

A busy machine or worker does not necessarily mean the system is performing well.

The enterprise must optimize end-to-end Production flow.

---

## Throughput Before Utilization Vanity

Maximum utilization of every resource may create:

- Queues.
- excess work-in-progress.
- delays.

The true objective is reliable throughput.

---

## Root Cause Before Blame

Production problems should first be classified as:

- Process.
- material.
- machine.
- quality.
- planning.
- workforce.
- system.

before becoming employee-performance conclusions.

---

## Standard Before Variance

The enterprise cannot meaningfully improve cycle time unless:

- Expected standard.
- actual performance.

are both known.

---

## Stable Process Before Optimization

Unstable processes should be stabilized before sophisticated optimization.

---

## Quality at the Source Before Rework

Defects should be prevented as close as possible to their point of creation.

---

## Bottleneck Before Local Optimization

Improving a non-constrained resource may not improve total system throughput.

---

## Evidence Before Improvement Claim

Operational improvement must be demonstrated through measurable outcomes.

---

# 1.4 Domain Objectives

The Domain permanently supports:

- Manufacturing Performance Management.
- Throughput Management.
- Cycle-Time Management.
- Work-Center Performance.
- Machine utilization.
- Availability analysis.
- Capacity efficiency.
- Production adherence.
- Setup/changeover improvement.
- Downtime management.
- Yield management.
- Scrap management.
- Rework management.
- First-Pass Quality intelligence.
- Work-in-Progress control.
- Queue management.
- Bottleneck management.
- production-loss analysis.
- process stability.
- visual factory management.
- Standard Work.
- continuous improvement.
- industrial risk.
- predictive Production Intelligence.
- AI-assisted industrial operations.

---

Domain 34 owns the improvement and performance meaning for:

- Workforce Management.
