# ENTERPRISE AI AGENTS, AUTONOMOUS OPERATIONS & DIGITAL WORKFORCE CANON
## Stage 10 — Final Enterprise AI Agents, Autonomous Operations & Digital Workforce Certification Canon

---

# 10.1 Purpose

Stage 10 consolidates and formally certifies Domain 42 as the permanent GiftHatkeOS architecture for AI Agents, digital workers, bounded autonomy, human approval, tool execution, Agent governance, AI accountability, and future autonomous operations.

The objective is:

> **Ensure AI can extend GiftHatkeOS safely and usefully without replacing human authority, bypassing certified business rules, creating a shadow ERP, or becoming a prerequisite for standalone operation.**

---

# 10.2 Final Domain Mission

Domain 42 permanently defines:

- AI Agent identity
- Agent versions
- Agent ownership
- Agent purpose
- tool access
- AI permissions
- task scope
- Delegation
- human approval
- autonomous action
- Agent memory
- recommendations
- Drafts
- execution
- validation
- exceptions
- escalation
- multi-Agent coordination
- Digital Workforce governance
- Agent testing
- AI incidents
- Agent auditability

---

# 10.3 Core Architecture Doctrine

Permanent:

```text id="core-doctrine42"
Certified Business Architecture

↓

Controlled Business Services / APIs

↓

AI Agent Capability
```

Never:

```text id="invalid-ai-architecture42"
AI Agent

↓

Directly Redefines Business Rules
```

---

# 10.4 Fundamental Authority Rule

Permanent:

```text id="authority-final42"
AI Agent
≠
Business Authority
```

---

# 10.5 AI Dependency Rule

Permanent:

```text id="dependency-final42"
AI may depend on ERP

ERP must not depend on AI
```

Core ERP operations remain available when AI is unavailable.

---

# 10.6 SMP1 Boundary

For SMP1:

```text id="smp1-final42"
Required Production AI Agents:
NONE
```

This is deliberate architecture.

---

# 10.7 AI Optionality

Standalone v1.0 must remain fully functional without:

- AI Agents
- autonomous workflows
- Agent memory
- Agent orchestration
- model-provider dependency

---

# 10.8 AI Adoption Principle

AI should be introduced only where it creates measurable business value.

---

# 10.9 AI Agent Identity

Every Production Agent must have:

- Agent ID
- purpose
- owner
- version
- status
- permission profile

---

# 10.10 Agent vs Human

Permanent:

```text id="agent-human-final42"
AI Agent
≠
Human User
```

---

# 10.11 Agent Ownership

Every Production Agent requires accountable ownership.

---

# 10.12 Ownership Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="ownership-final42"
Agent Owner
≠
Universal Action Approver
```

---

# 10.13 Agent Purpose

Every Agent must have a bounded business purpose.

---

# 10.14 No Universal Super-Agent

Permanent:

> **GiftHatkeOS should not create one general AI Agent with unrestricted access across the enterprise simply because the underlying model is capable of reasoning broadly.**

---

# 10.15 Agent Version

Material Agent behavior is versioned.

Changes to:

- model
- system instruction
- tools
- permissions
- autonomy

may constitute a new Production behavior version.

---

# 10.16 Version Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="version-final42"
Agent Name
≠
Agent Behavior Version
```

---

# 10.17 Agent Capability

A model may technically perform many things.

Only approved Agent capabilities are relevant operationally.

---

# 10.18 Capability Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="capability-final42"
AI Can Do It
≠
AI Is Authorized to Do It
```

---

# 10.19 Agent Scope

Effective scope may include:

- Domain
- Company
- user
- records
- action class
- tool
- threshold

---

# 10.20 Effective Authority

Canonical:

```text id="effective-authority-final42"
Agent Permission

∩

Delegated / Service Authority

∩

Company Scope

∩

Task Scope

∩

Approval Policy

=
Effective AI Authority
```

---

# 10.21 Read vs Write

Permanent:

```text id="read-write-final42"
Can Read
≠
Can Write
```

---

# 10.22 Recommend vs Execute

Permanent:

```text id="recommend-execute-final42"
Can Recommend
≠
Can Execute
```

---

# 10.23 Draft vs Commit

Permanent:

```text id="draft-commit-final42"
AI Draft
≠
Business Commitment
```

---

# 10.24 Human Authority

Humans retain decision rights for material business actions unless explicit policy delegates bounded execution.

---

# 10.25 Human-in-the-Loop

Preferred initial execution model:

```text id="human-loop-final42"
AI Recommends / Drafts

↓

Human Reviews

↓

Human Approves

↓

Certified Service Executes
```

---

# 10.26 Human-on-the-Loop

Appropriate later for:

- low-risk
- reversible
- predictable

automation.

---

# 10.27 Human-out-of-the-Loop

Permitted only for:

- tightly bounded
- low-risk
- validated
- auditable

actions.

---

# 10.28 Progressive Autonomy

Canonical:

```text id="progressive-autonomy-final42"
Read

↓

Recommend

↓

Draft

↓

Human-Approved Execution

↓

Limited Autonomous Execution

↓

Higher Autonomy Only When Proven
```

---

# 10.29 More AI ≠ More Autonomy

Permanent:

```text id="more-ai-final42"
Improved AI Capability
≠
Requirement for Increased Autonomy
```

- Supplier commitment
- Customer commitment
- Inventory state
- Production
- Shipping
- permissions
- Legal position
- Compliance

# 10.31 Material Action Governance

Higher business impact requires stronger control.

# 10.32 Action Risk Classes

Recommended:

- LOW
- MODERATE
- HIGH
- PROHIBITED

---

# 10.33 Contextual Risk

Risk may increase due to:

- monetary amount
- batch size
- irreversibility
- Company

# 10.34 Batch Risk

Permanent:

```text id="batch-risk-final42"
Safe for One Record

Safe for 10,000 Records
```

# 10.35 Monetary Risk

---

# 10.36 Tool Architecture

Agents act through controlled tools/services.

```text id="tool-architecture-final42"
AI Agent

↓

Tool Gateway / Permission Enforcement

↓

Certified Domain Service

↓

Business Validation
```

# 10.37 No Generic Database Authority

Production Agents should not receive unrestricted:

- SQL execution
- arbitrary table updates
- arbitrary record deletion

# 10.38 Tool Publication

- inputs
- outputs
- Risk
- permission
- approval requirement

# 10.40 Tool Gateway Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="tool-gateway-final42"
Tool Gateway
≠
Business Rule Engine
```

# 10.41 Double Validation

Material action may require:

```text id="double-validation-final42"
AI Authorization Validation

+

Business Domain Validation
```

---

# 10.42 No Business Rule Bypass

Permanent:

```text id="rule-bypass-final42"
AI Says Proceed
≠
Certified Workflow Allows Proceed
```

---

# 10.43 Delegation

Human users may delegate bounded authority.

---

# 10.44 Delegation Limit

Permanent:

```text id="delegation-final42"
Delegated Authority
≤
Delegator Authority
```

---

# 10.45 Delegation Scope

May restrict:

- task
- Domain
- Company
- amount
- time
- records

---

# 10.46 Service Agents

System-operated Agents require explicit service authority.

They are not default superusers.

---

# 10.47 Company Context

Domain 40 applies to all Company-owned AI operations.

---

# 10.48 Cross-Company Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="company-final42"
Authorized in Company A
≠
Authorized in Company B
```

---

# 10.49 Task Model

AI activity occurs within a valid Task.

---

# 10.50 Task Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="task-final42"
Agent Exists
≠
Agent May Act Without Valid Task Context
```

---

# 1.1 Purpose

Domain 43 defines how GiftHatkeOS may safely expand beyond internal users and internal modules into a controlled external ecosystem of Partners, integration providers, service providers, extensions, applications, and future marketplace capabilities.

The objective is:

> **Enable GiftHatkeOS to connect with external Partners and future extensions without giving external actors uncontrolled access to certified business architecture, data, permissions, or operational authority.**

```text id="ecosystem-core43s1"
External Partner
≠
Internal Business Authority
```

```text id="ecosystem-priority43s1"
Future Ecosystem Capability
≠
Current SMP1 Requirement
```

A partner marketplace is **not required**.

- current integrations
- current suppliers/service providers
- certified business operations
- clean API boundaries

Domain 43 exists to define future architecture for:

- Partner identity

- Partner types

- extensions

- partner data access

- commercial arrangements

# 1.22 Extension Types

Potential:

- Integration Connector
- UI Extension
- Workflow Extension
- Reporting Extension
- Automation Extension

---

# 1.23 Extension Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="extension-boundary43s1"
Extension
≠
Permission to Modify Core Arbitrarily
```

---

# 1.24 Extension Point

An Extension Point is a controlled place where external functionality may connect.

Examples:

- API
- webhook/event
- approved UI slot
- workflow callback

---

# 1.25 Extension Point Ownership

Each Extension Point must belong to an owning Domain or platform capability.

---

# 1.26 No Open-Core Mutation

Third-party code should not gain unrestricted access to:

- internal database
- server filesystem
- private service internals

without a deliberate controlled architecture.

---

# 1.27 API-First Boundary

Preferred:

```text id="api-first43s1"
External Capability

↓

Approved API / Event / Extension Point

↓

Certified Domain Service
```

---

# 1.28 Domain Authority

Domain 13 remains authoritative for:

- APIs
- integration contracts
- external connectivity

Domain 43 governs broader ecosystem participation.

---

# 1.29 Security Authority

Domain 28 remains authoritative for:

- authentication
- authorization
- identity
- credentials
- trust

---

# 1.30 Data Governance Authority

Domain 29 governs:

- data disclosure
- privacy
- retention
- external sharing

---

# 1.31 Partner Access Principle

Partner access should follow:

- least privilege
- purpose limitation
- Environment scope
- Company scope

where applicable.

---

# 1.32 Partner Membership Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="partner-membership43s1"
Partner Approved
≠
Access to All GiftHatkeOS Data
```

---

# 1.33 Partner Permission

- APIs
- records
- Company
- operation
- Environment

---

# 1.34 Read vs Write

```text id="partner-readwrite43s1"
Partner Can Read
≠
Partner Can Write
```

---

# 1.35 Data Scope

A Partner should receive only data required for the approved capability.

---

# 1.36 Company Scope

```text id="partner-company43s1"
Partner Access in Company A
≠
Access in Company B
```

---

# 1.37 Environment Scope

- Production

credentials where practical.

---

# 1.38 Production Boundary

```text id="partner-prod43s1"
Sandbox Approval
≠
Production Approval
```

---

# 1.39 Partner Credentials

- application/service credentials

not shared human passwords.

---

# 1.40 Credential Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="partner-credential43s1"
Partner Credential
≠
Internal Administrator Credential
```

---

# 1.41 Credential Revocation

---

# 1.42 API Permissions

Each external application may have explicit:

- write scope

- Sync Marketplace Orders

# 1.44 Capability Boundary

```text id="capability-boundary43s1"
≠
```

A future marketplace may list approved:

- integrations

- services

# 1.47 Marketplace Boundary

```text id="marketplace-boundary43s1"
Listed in Marketplace
≠
Trusted Without Limits
```

GiftHatke does not need to launch a public app marketplace unless ecosystem scale justifies it.

---

# 1.49 Private Partner Catalog

without public marketplace functionality.

```text id="ecosystem-maturity43s1"
↓
```

- revenue share

- support

# 1.54 Technical Approval vs Commercial Approval

Permanent:

```text id="technical-commercial43s1"
Technical Integration Approved
≠
Commercial Agreement Approved
```

---

# 1.55 Partner Contract

---

# 1.56 Financial Settlement

Revenue share, Partner fees, commissions, and payouts remain governed by Domain 6/31 as relevant.

---

# 1.57 Partner Owner

Each important Partner should have an internal accountable owner.

---

# 1.58 Owner Responsibilities

Potential:

- relationship
- access review
- issue escalation
- renewal
- termination

---

# 1.59 Owner Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="partner-owner43s1"
Partner Owner
≠
Security Administrator
```

---

# 1.60 Partner Support

External applications may require:

- support contact
- operational contact
- escalation contact

---

# 1.61 Service Level

Future Partner arrangements may define:

- uptime
- response

---

# 1.62 SLA Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="partner-sla43s1"
Partner SLA
≠
GiftHatke Business Continuity Guarantee
```

Domain 38 remains resilience authority.

---

# 1.63 Partner Eventing

Partners may consume or produce approved events.

---

# 1.64 Event Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="partner-event43s1"
External Event
≠
Authoritative Business State
```

until owning Domain validates/processes it.

---

# 1.65 Webhook

Webhook may notify Partners of approved events.

---

# 1.66 Webhook Security

Should use:

- authentication/signing
- retry
- replay protection

where implemented.

---

# 1.67 Retry Safety

Partner retries must not duplicate:

- Orders
- payments
- shipments
- other material effects

---

# 1.68 Idempotency

External write operations should support idempotency where duplicate requests could create material business effects.

---

# 1.69 Partner Rate Limits

External applications may be subject to:

- request limits
- concurrency
- quotas

---

# 1.70 Rate Limit Boundary

Rate limits protect platform resources.

They should not silently corrupt business synchronization.

---

# 1.71 Partner Failure

External service failure must be visible where it affects business operations.

---

# 1.72 Core ERP Independence

Permanent:

```text id="partner-outage43s1"
One Partner Service Down
≠
Entire ERP Down
```

where architecture can reasonably isolate dependency.

---

# 1.73 Critical Partner Dependency

Some Partners may be essential for:

- payments
- shipping
- marketplace operations

Their failure requires Domain 14/38 visibility.

---

# 1.74 Fallback

Where practical, important business operations should have:

- manual fallback
- alternate provider
- queue/retry

according to real Risk.

---

# 1.75 Partner Data Ownership

External Partner data should not silently become authoritative business truth.

---

# 1.76 Data Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="partner-data43s1"
Partner Says Record = X
≠
GiftHatkeOS Must Accept X
```

Owning Domain validates.

---

# 1.77 Data Synchronization

Integration should define:

- source authority
- destination
- direction
- conflict handling

---

# 1.78 Source of Truth

Every integrated object should have an explicit authoritative source.

---

# 1.79 Sync Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="sync-boundary43s1"
Two Systems Contain Same Data
≠
Both Are Authoritative
```

---

# 1.80 Conflict Resolution

Conflicts should follow predefined:

- source authority
- timestamps
- business rules
- human review

where needed.

---

# 1.81 Partner Audit

- Partner
- Application
- credential/user
- operation
- time
- result

---

# 1.82 Audit Boundary

Partner logs provide Evidence.

Domain 39 remains assurance authority.

---

# 1.83 Partner Monitoring

Monitor important integrations for:

- authentication failure
- API errors
- synchronization failures
- latency
- availability

---

# 1.84 Observability Authority

Domain 14 remains monitoring/incident authority.

---

# 1.85 Partner Suspension

A Partner or Application may be suspended due to:

- Security Risk
- repeated failures
- contractual issue
- data misuse
- business decision

---

# 1.86 Suspension Effect

Potential:

- new API calls rejected
- existing pending operations handled according to policy
- history retained

---

# 1.87 Partner Revocation

Revocation should terminate:

- credentials
- access
- subscriptions/webhooks
- active permissions

---

# 1.88 Revocation Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="revocation43s1"
Partner Revoked
≠
Historical Business Records Deleted
```

---

# 1.89 Extension Suspension

---

# 1.90 Marketplace Removal

Removing a listing does not automatically revoke existing installed/approved applications unless policy says so.

---

# 1.91 Extension Versioning

External Extensions should have identifiable versions.

---

# 1.92 Version Compatibility

GiftHatkeOS may define:

- supported API versions
- compatibility windows

---

# 1.93 Breaking Change

External interfaces should avoid uncontrolled breaking changes.

---

# 1.94 API Deprecation

```text id="api-deprecation43s1"
New Version Available

↓

Deprecation Notice

↓

Migration Window

↓

Old Version Retirement
```

where external dependency exists.

---

# 1.95 No Infinite Compatibility

GiftHatkeOS does not need to support obsolete external API versions forever.

---

# 1.96 Partner Sandbox

Future external developers may receive:

- sandbox/test Environment
- sample data
- limited credentials

---

# 1.97 Sandbox Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="sandbox-boundary43s1"
Sandbox Access
≠
Production Data Access
```

---

- API documentation
- authentication
- examples
- errors
- version policy

---

# 1.99 Certification

High-impact Extensions may require technical certification before Production use.

---

# 1.100 Certification Depth

Certification should match Risk.

- payment
- Inventory mutation
- Production control

integration.

---

Potential:

- LOW
- MODERATE
- HIGH
- PROHIBITED

---

# 1.102 Low-Risk Extension

Example:

- read-only reporting/export.

---

# 1.103 Moderate-Risk Extension

Example:

- Customer communication connector.

---

# 1.104 High-Risk Extension

Examples:

- payment processing
- Inventory write
- Order creation
- shipping commitment

---

# 1.105 Prohibited Extension

Capability that violates core:

- Security
- data governance
- business integrity

may be prohibited.

---

# 1.106 Extension Isolation

Extension failure should have limited blast radius where practical.

---

# 1.107 No Extension Superuser

```text id="extension-superuser43s1"
Installed Extension
≠
Administrator of GiftHatkeOS
```

---

---

# 1.109 UI Trust

- GiftHatke core
- approved third-party extension

where material.

---

# 1.110 Workflow Extensions

Third-party capability may participate in workflow through:

- controlled action
- event
- callback

---

# 1.111 Finance Extensions

Third-party Finance capability must not bypass Domain 6 controls.

---

# 1.112 Security Extensions

No Extension may override Domain 28 authorization policy.

---

# 1.113 Data Extensions

No Extension may escape Domain 29 data rules.

---

# 1.114 AI Extensions

Future Agent/AI extensions remain governed by Domain 42.

---

# 1.115 Platform Extensions

Runtime/deployment extensions remain subject to Domain 41 controls.

---

# 1.116 Ecosystem Growth

Expansion should follow actual needs.

Canonical:

```text id="ecosystem-growth43s1"
Current Integration

↓

Reusable Integration Model

↓

Partner Network

↓

Extension Ecosystem

↓

Marketplace Only If Valuable
```

---

# 1.117 No Marketplace-First Strategy

Permanent:

> **Do not build a public marketplace before GiftHatke has enough Partners, Extensions, or external demand to justify operating one.**

---

# 1.118 SMP1 Required Ecosystem Capability

For standalone v1.0:

Minimum:

- existing critical integrations
- stable API architecture
- service credentials
- access control
- integration audit
- failure visibility

---

# 1.119 SMP1 Non-Requirements

Do not build during SMP1:

- public app marketplace
- Partner developer portal
- Extension SDK
- Partner billing system
- revenue-share engine
- app review board
- Partner certification platform
- Extension marketplace UI

---

# 1.120 SMP1 Existing Partners

Existing services such as:

- marketplaces
- shipping
- communication
- payment/other providers

should be migrated only as required by current operations.

---

# 1.121 SMP1 Integration Priority

Priority is:

```text id="smp1-integration-priority43s1"
Current Business-Critical Integration

before

Future Ecosystem Platform
```

---

# 1.122 ERP9 Reuse

ERP9 may strengthen:

- Partner/Company configuration
- integration settings
- external business master data

where required.

---

# 1.123 ERP10 Reuse

ERP10 may improve:

- integration administration
- external service UX
- Partner visibility

---

# 1.124 Version 1.1 Reuse

Version 1.1 may introduce selected reusable integration/Partner capabilities if real demand exists.

---

# 1.125 Future Marketplace Trigger

Consider a true marketplace only when:

- multiple third-party apps exist
- repeated onboarding occurs
- external developers request access
- governance burden justifies standardization

---

# 1.126 Advanced Ecosystem Capabilities That Can Wait

Do not block roadmap for:

- public app marketplace
- developer monetization
- app ratings/reviews
- Partner tiers
- Extension discovery engine
- app subscription billing
- cross-company app federation
- public developer community platform
- certification badge ecosystem

---

# 1.127 Anti-Duplication Rule

Permanent:

> **Domain 43 governs external participation and Extension capability. It does not replace Domain 13 integrations, Domain 23 Supplier/Partner business relationships, Domain 24 contracts, Domain 28 Security, Domain 29 data governance, or the business Domains themselves.**

---

# 1.128 Anti-Platform-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **GiftHatkeOS must not drift from being a business operating system into becoming an ecosystem marketplace company unless the business itself later chooses that strategy.**

---

# 1.129 Anti-Overengineering Rule

Permanent:

> **Build the integration or Partner capability needed for the next real external relationship. Do not build a platform economy before there is an ecosystem to operate.**

---

# 1.130 Critical Domain Invariants

1. External Partner ≠ internal business authority.
2. Future ecosystem capability ≠ SMP1 requirement.
3. Platform Partner ≠ Supplier ≠ Customer.
4. External Application ≠ Partner organization.
5. Extension ≠ permission to rewrite core.
6. External capability should use approved interfaces.
7. Partner approved ≠ access to all data.
8. Read access ≠ write access.
9. Company A Partner access ≠ Company B access.
10. Sandbox approval ≠ Production approval.
11. Partner credential ≠ internal admin credential.
12. Technical approval ≠ commercial approval.
13. External Event ≠ authoritative business state.
14. Retry must not duplicate business effects.
15. Partner data ≠ authoritative ERP truth without validation.
16. Two systems containing same data ≠ dual authority.
17. Partner revocation ≠ deletion of business history.
18. Installed Extension ≠ GiftHatkeOS administrator.
19. Public marketplace is optional future maturity.
20. SMP1 must prioritize current critical integrations over ecosystem infrastructure.

---

Stage 1 permanently establishes the implementation-grade foundation for:

- external ecosystem scope
- Partner identity
- Partner/Application separation
- Partner types/status
- Extensions
- Extension Points
- API-first integration
- Partner permissions
- Company/Environment scope
- credentials
- capabilities
- marketplace optionality

- support/SLAs
- events/webhooks
- retries/idempotency
- data synchronization/source authority
- Audit/Monitoring
- suspension/revocation
- versioning/deprecation
- sandbox/developer documentation
- Extension Risk/isolation
- UI/workflow/Finance/Security/Data/AI boundaries
- SMP1 minimum/non-requirements
- ERP9/ERP10/Version 1.1 reuse
- anti-duplication
- anti-platform-drift
- anti-overengineering

This is sufficient to establish future external ecosystem architecture without turning GiftHatkeOS into a marketplace platform or delaying standalone migration.

# ENTERPRISE ECOSYSTEM MARKETPLACE, PARTNER NETWORK & PLATFORM EXPANSION CANON
## Stage 2 — Partner, Application, Extension, Capability, Credential, Permission, Subscription, Installation & Marketplace Listing Entity Model Canon

---

# 2.1 Purpose

Stage 2 defines the permanent entity model required to represent external Partners, applications, extensions, credentials, permissions, subscriptions, installations, capabilities, marketplace listings, and Partner operational relationships.

The objective is:

> **Create a durable ecosystem data model that allows external parties and applications to connect with GiftHatkeOS through explicit identities, scopes, permissions, lifecycle states, and commercial relationships without duplicating core ERP entities.**

---

# 2.2 Core Entity Set

Future-capable entities include:

- Ecosystem Partner
- Partner Type
- Partner Contact
- Partner Owner
- Partner Status
- External Application
- Application Version
- Extension
- Extension Version
- Extension Type
- Capability
- Capability Version
- Extension Point
- API Scope
- Partner Permission
- Application Permission
- Credential Reference
- Environment Binding
- Company Binding
- Installation
- Subscription
- Webhook Subscription
- Marketplace Listing
- Listing Version
- Commercial Plan
- Partner Agreement Reference
- Support Profile
- Certification Record
- Partner Audit Record

---

# 2.3 Ecosystem Partner

Represents the external organization participating in the GiftHatkeOS ecosystem.

Minimum fields:

- Partner ID
- legal/business name
- Partner Type
- status
- internal owner
- primary contact
- created time

---

# 2.4 Partner Identity Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="partner-identity43s2"
Ecosystem Partner
≠
Supplier Master
≠
Customer
```

One real organization may hold multiple roles, but each role remains independently governed.

---

# 2.5 Partner Type

Potential values:

- Technology
- Integration
- Logistics
- Marketplace
- Payment
- Service
- Developer

Only actual types should be configured.

---

Recommended:

```text id="partner-status43s2"
DRAFT
UNDER REVIEW
ACTIVE
SUSPENDED
REVOKED
RETIRED
```

# 2.7 Partner Status Boundary

ACTIVE means Partner identity is approved.

It does not imply every application or capability is approved.

---

Stores operational/business contacts.

Potential roles:

- Technical
- Commercial
- Security
- Support

---

# 2.9 Partner Owner

Represents the internal GiftHatke owner responsible for the relationship.

---

# 2.10 Partner Owner Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="partner-owner43s2"
Partner Owner
≠
Security Administrator
≠
Commercial Approver
```

---

Minimum:

- Application ID
- Partner ID
- name
- purpose
- status
- current version

---

# 2.12 Application Identity Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="application-identity43s2"
One Partner
may operate
Many Applications
```

---

# 2.13 Application Status

Potential:

```text id="application-status43s2"
DEVELOPMENT
UNDER REVIEW
ACTIVE
SUSPENDED
REVOKED
RETIRED
```

---

# 2.14 Application Purpose

Every Production application should have explicit business purpose.

---

# 2.15 Application Version

Minimum:

- Version ID
- Application ID

# 2.16 Application Version Boundary

```text id="application-version43s2"

≠

```

Minimum:

- Extension ID
- Partner
- name

# 2.18 Extension Type

- Integration
- UI
- Reporting
- Workflow
- Automation

---

# 2.19 Extension Boundary

```text id="extension-entity43s2"
External Application
≠
Extension
```

# 2.20 Extension Version

# 2.25 Capability Version

# 2.26 Capability Risk

- MODERATE
- HIGH
- PROHIBITED

```text id="readwrite43s2"
READ
≠
```

```text id="installation-status43s2"
PENDING
ACTIVE
```

# 2.121 Anti-Duplication Rule

Permanent:

> **Ecosystem entities represent external participation, technical access, installation, and commercial context. They must not duplicate Suppliers, Customers, Orders, Contracts, Finance records, or other authoritative business entities.**

---

# 2.122 Anti-Overengineering Rule

Permanent:

> **Create only the ecosystem entities needed by real integrations and Partner relationships. A complete marketplace data model is future-capable architecture, not a requirement to implement all entities now.**

---

# 2.123 Critical Entity Invariants

1. Partner ≠ Supplier ≠ Customer.
2. Partner Active ≠ all Applications approved.
3. External Application ≠ Partner organization.
4. Extension ≠ Application.
5. Capability declared ≠ capability certified.
6. Extension Point ≠ unrestricted internal access.
7. Partner eligibility ≠ Application permission granted.
8. READ ≠ WRITE.
9. Company A Installation ≠ Company B Installation.
10. Sandbox binding ≠ Production binding.
11. Credential metadata ≠ credential secret.
12. Listing exists ≠ Extension installed.
13. Subscription active ≠ unlimited technical permission.
14. Agreement signed ≠ Production access enabled.
15. Webhook Event access ≠ unrestricted record access.
16. Partner certified once ≠ every Version certified forever.
17. External ID ≠ internal GiftHatkeOS ID.
18. Uninstallation ≠ deletion of historical business records.
19. Installed ≠ compatible forever.
20. SMP1 needs only current-integration entities, not a marketplace database.

---

- external identifiers
- revocation/uninstallation
- compatibility/deprecation
- SMP1 minimal integration model
- ERP9/ERP10/Version 1.1 reuse
- anti-duplication
- anti-overengineering

This is sufficient to support future structured Partner and marketplace operations without requiring GiftHatkeOS to implement a marketplace during standalone migration.

# ENTERPRISE ECOSYSTEM MARKETPLACE, PARTNER NETWORK & PLATFORM EXPANSION CANON
## Stage 3 — Partner Lifecycle, Application Onboarding, Extension Review, Installation, Access Granting, Suspension, Revocation & Ecosystem Operating Model Canon

---

# 3.1 Purpose

Stage 3 defines how external Partners, applications, extensions, credentials, permissions, installations, and marketplace participation should move through their operational lifecycle.

The objective is:

> **Ensure every external ecosystem participant is intentionally onboarded, appropriately scoped, safely activated, continuously governable, and cleanly removable without compromising certified GiftHatkeOS business architecture or historical business records.**

---

# 3.2 Core Operating Principle

Permanent:

```text id="ecosystem-operating43s3"
External Access
must follow

Identity
+
Purpose
+
Review
+
Scope
+
Permission
+
Validation
+
Activation
```

---

# 3.3 Partner Lifecycle

Canonical:

```text id="partner-lifecycle43s3"
Requested

↓

Identity Established

↓

Business Purpose Reviewed

↓

Security / Data Review

↓

Approved

↓

Active

↓

Periodic Review

↓

Suspended / Retired / Revoked
```

---

# 3.4 Partner Request

A Partner relationship may begin from:

- internal business need
- existing vendor integration
- Partner request
- marketplace/platform opportunity

---

# 3.5 Business Need First

Permanent:

> **External Partner onboarding should begin from a real business or platform need, not from a desire to populate a Partner ecosystem.**

---

# 3.6 Partner Identification

Confirm:

- legal/business identity
- operating contact
- technical contact
- relevant service/product

---

# 3.7 Identity Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="partner-identity-operating43s3"
Known Company Name
≠
Verified Partner Identity
```

---

# 3.8 Partner Purpose

Define why GiftHatkeOS needs the Partner.

Examples:

- shipping
- marketplace sales
- payment processing
- communication
- analytics
- external Extension

---

# 3.9 Purpose Boundary

Partner access should not materially exceed the defined purpose.

---

# 3.10 Partner Review

Review depth should depend on:

- access requested
- data involved
- operational criticality
- business impact

---

# 3.11 Low-Risk Partner

Example:

- read-only analytics provider using non-sensitive data.

---

# 3.12 High-Risk Partner

Examples:

- payment provider
- marketplace order write integration
- shipping commitment provider
- provider processing sensitive data

---

# 3.13 Risk-Proportional Review

Permanent:

```text id="partner-review-risk43s3"
Higher External Authority
=
Stronger Review
```

---

# 3.14 Partner Approval

Approval may cover:

- organization
- intended relationship
- general trust status

It does not automatically approve every application.

---

# 3.15 Partner Activation

ACTIVE Partner may submit or operate approved applications according to policy.

---

# 3.16 Partner Activation Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="partner-activation-boundary43s3"
Partner Active
≠
Every Partner Application Active
```

---

# 3.17 Application Lifecycle

Canonical:

```text id="application-lifecycle43s3"
Register

↓

Define Purpose

↓

Configure

↓

Review Permissions

↓

Test

↓

Production Approve

↓

Activate

↓

Monitor

↓

Suspend / Upgrade / Revoke / Retire
```

---

# 3.18 Application Registration

Each application requires distinct identity.

---

# 3.19 No Shared Application Identity

Avoid using one generic external credential for unrelated Partner applications.

---

# 3.20 Application Purpose

Must identify:

- what it does
- which Domain it interacts with
- which data it needs

---

# 3.21 Requested Permissions

Application may request:

- API scopes
- Event subscriptions
- Company access
- read/write capabilities

---

# 3.22 Permission Review

Requested permission should be evaluated against:

- business purpose
- least privilege
- Risk

---

# 3.23 Excess Permission

If application requests unnecessary authority:

- reduce scope before activation.

---

# 3.24 Permission Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="requested-granted43s3"
Permission Requested
≠
Permission Granted
```

---

# 3.25 Development Environment

New integration should normally begin in:

- Development/Test/Sandbox

where feasible.

---

# 3.26 Sandbox Credentials

Should remain separate from Production credentials.

---

# 3.27 Sandbox Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="sandbox-production43s3"
Works in Sandbox
≠
Approved for Production
```

---

# 3.28 Integration Testing

Test:

- authentication
- permissions
- input validation
- output mapping
- retries
- error handling
- authoritative state handling

---

# 3.29 Negative Testing

Also test:

- unauthorized API
- wrong Company
- malformed request
- revoked credential
- duplicate request

---

# 3.30 Production Approval

Production approval should confirm:

- identity
- permissions
- credentials
- Environment
- Company scope
- tested business flow

---

# 3.31 Production Activation

Only approved application configuration enters Production.

---

# 3.32 Activation Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="app-activation43s3"
Application Installed
≠
Application Authorized
```

unless installation includes explicit approved authorization.

---

Canonical:

```text id="extension-lifecycle43s3"

↓

↓

↓

Approved

↓

↓

Operated

↓
```

# 3.34 Extension Review

Review should consider:

- Extension Points used
- requested permissions
- data access
- UI impact
- Business Domain impact

---

# 3.35 Extension Boundary Review

Verify Extension cannot:

- bypass Domain services
- bypass permissions
- modify arbitrary core data

---

# 3.36 UI Extension Review

Check external UI does not:

- impersonate trusted core action
- hide third-party origin where material
- bypass normal authorization

---

# 3.37 Workflow Extension Review

Domain 11 rules remain authoritative.

---

# 3.38 Finance Extension Review

Domain 6 remains financial authority.

---

# 3.39 AI Extension Review

Domain 42 remains AI Agent/autonomy authority.

---

# 3.40 Installation Request

Installation should identify:

- Application/Extension
- Company
- Environment
- requested permissions
- installer/requester

---

# 3.41 Installation Approval

Installation may require approval based on:

- risk
- Company
- access
- capability

---

# 3.42 Self-Service Installation

May eventually be allowed for low-risk certified extensions.

Not required initially.

---

# 3.43 Installation Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="installation-operating43s3"
User Can Discover Extension
≠
User May Install It
```

---

# 3.44 Installation Execution

On approved installation:

- create Installation record
- bind Environment/Company
- grant defined scopes
- activate required webhooks/config

---

# 3.45 Installation Verification

After install confirm:

- authentication works
- permissions match approval
- no unexpected scopes
- initial health succeeds

---

# 3.46 Failed Installation

If setup fails:

- mark FAILED/PARTIAL
- do not present as active
- clean up unsafe credentials/access

---

# 3.47 Access Granting

Access is granted to:

- Application identity

not merely to Partner organization.

---

# 3.48 Least Privilege

Permanent:

```text id="least-privilege43s3"
Grant
minimum authority
needed for approved capability
```

---

# 3.49 Read Access

Should not imply:

- write
- delete
- administrative control

---

# 3.50 Event Access

Webhook/event subscription does not automatically grant API access.

---

# 3.51 Company Access

Each applicable Company scope should be explicit.

---

# 3.52 Cross-Company Access

Requires deliberate authorization.

---

# 3.53 Access Start

Permission may have:

- effective start

where useful.

---

# 3.54 Access Expiry

Temporary integrations may have:

- expiry

to prevent forgotten persistent access.

---

# 3.55 Credential Provisioning

Credentials should be issued only after appropriate authorization.

---

# 3.56 Secret Delivery

Secret values should use secure delivery/storage mechanisms.

---

# 3.57 Credential Rotation

Rotation should:

- create new credential
- transition safely
- revoke previous credential

---

# 3.58 Rotation Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="rotation-boundary43s3"
Credential Rotated
≠
Application Identity Changed
```

---

# 3.59 Credential Expiry

Expired credential must fail authentication.

---

# 3.60 Credential Revocation

Revocation should block future use promptly.

---

# 3.61 Permission Change

Material permission increase should follow review.

---

# 3.62 Permission Reduction

May normally be applied without full re-onboarding.

---

# 3.63 New Domain Access

Granting access to a new Business Domain may require new Risk review.

---

# 3.64 New Write Permission

Permanent:

```text id="new-write43s3"
Existing Read Integration
+
New Write Scope
=
Material Authority Change
```

---

# 3.65 Application Version Upgrade

Upgrade may be:

- compatible minor change
- material behavioral change

---

# 3.66 Upgrade Review

Material changes to:

- permissions
- write behavior
- data handling
- Extension Points

may require revalidation.

---

# 3.67 Version Rollout

Canonical:

```text id="version-rollout43s3"
New Version

↓

Test

↓

Approve

↓

Deploy

↓

Verify

↓

Retire Old Version
```

---

# 3.68 Rollback

Where feasible, maintain ability to return to prior known-compatible version.

---

# 3.69 Marketplace Listing Lifecycle

Future:

```text id="listing-lifecycle43s3"
Draft

↓

Review

↓

Publish

↓

Maintain

↓

Suspend / Remove
```

---

# 3.70 Listing Review

Potential review:

- accurate description
- Partner identity
- compatibility
- permissions
- Risk
- support information

---

# 3.71 Listing Approval Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="listing-approval43s3"
Marketplace Listing Approved
≠
Every Installation Automatically Approved
```

---

# 3.72 Listing Updates

Material capability or permission claims should be reviewed where required.

---

# 3.73 Marketplace Removal

May occur due to:

- unsupported application
- security issue
- Partner request
- policy violation
- business decision

---

# 3.74 Existing Installations After Removal

Handling should be deliberate.

Possible:

- continue supported
- block new installs
- suspend existing installs
- require upgrade/removal

---

# 3.75 Partner Monitoring

Operational monitoring may cover:

- API errors
- sync failures
- authentication failures
- webhook failures
- uptime

---

# 3.76 Business Outcome Monitoring

For critical integration, monitor actual business effect.

Example:

```text id="shipping-monitor43s3"
Shipping API Available
≠
Shipping Labels Successfully Flowing
```

---

# 3.77 Integration Health

Potential:

- HEALTHY
- DEGRADED
- FAILED
- DISABLED

---

# 3.78 Degraded Integration

May continue limited operation while issue is visible.

---

# 3.79 External Dependency Failure

Should trigger:

- retry/queue
- fallback
- human escalation

as appropriate.

---

# 3.80 Partner Incident

Potential:

- data exposure
- unauthorized access
- invalid mass write
- prolonged outage
- duplicate transaction creation

---

# 3.81 Partner Incident Flow

Canonical:

```text id="partner-incident43s3"
Detect

↓

Contain

↓

Suspend Credential / Application if Needed

↓

Preserve Evidence

↓

Assess Business Impact

↓

Reconcile

↓

Correct

↓

Revalidate
```

---

# 3.82 Narrow Containment

Prefer suspending:

- one credential
- one Application
- one Extension

before entire Partner where safe.

---

# 3.83 Emergency Suspension

Authorized operators should be able to stop risky external access quickly.

---

# 3.84 Suspension Effect

Application suspension should prevent:

- new authenticated operations
- new webhook delivery if relevant
- new scheduled executions

according to architecture.

---

# 3.85 Suspension Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="suspension-history43s3"
Application Suspended
≠
Historical Business Records Removed
```

---

# 3.86 Partner Suspension

If entire Partner is suspended:

All active Partner applications may be blocked according to policy.

---

# 3.87 Revocation

Revocation represents stronger termination than temporary suspension.

---

# 3.88 Application Revocation

Should revoke:

- credentials
- API scopes
- webhooks
- execution capability

---

# 3.89 Partner Revocation

May revoke all:

- applications
- credentials
- installations
- access

while preserving historical Evidence.

---

# 3.90 Revocation Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="revocation-history43s3"
External Access Revoked
≠
Erase Transactions Previously Created
```

---

# 3.91 Uninstallation

Removing an installed Extension/Application should:

- terminate active integration where appropriate
- revoke associated access
- stop jobs/webhooks
- retain Audit/history

---

# 3.92 Data After Uninstall

Business records created during integration remain governed by owning Domains.

---

# 3.93 External Stored Data

If Partner retains GiftHatke data after termination:

Domain 29/24 rules govern retention/deletion obligations.

---

---

```text id="smp1-lifecycle43s3"

↓

Define Purpose

↓

Define Credentials / Permissions

↓

Migrate

↓

Test

↓

Activate

↓

Monitor
```

during SMP1.

---

Do not block the roadmap for:

- self-service Partner onboarding
- automated marketplace publishing
- developer approval pipelines
- Partner tier promotion
- automated commercial settlement
- public Extension moderation
- mass third-party certification
- multi-tenant Partner administration

---

# 3.130 Anti-Duplication Rule

Permanent:

> **Domain 43 manages external Partner and Application lifecycle. It does not replace Domain 13 integration contracts, Domain 23 business Partner relationships, Domain 24 contracts, Domain 28 Security, Domain 29 data governance, or owning Domain business workflows.**

---

# 3.131 Anti-Overengineering Rule

Permanent:

> **Operate each external integration with enough identity, access control, monitoring, and lifecycle discipline to keep it safe. Do not create a marketplace operating bureaucracy until there is an actual marketplace to operate.**

---

# 3.132 Critical Operating Invariants

1. External access requires explicit identity and purpose.
2. Higher external authority requires stronger review.
3. Partner Active ≠ every Partner Application Active.
4. Permission requested ≠ permission granted.
5. Sandbox success ≠ Production approval.
6. Application installed ≠ application authorized.
7. Discoverable Extension ≠ installable by every user.
8. Access should follow least privilege.
9. New write scope is a material authority change.
10. Listing approved ≠ every installation approved.
11. External API availability ≠ business process success.
12. Application suspension ≠ deletion of historical records.
13. Revocation must terminate active access while preserving business history.
14. Subscription cancellation ≠ verified technical access revocation.
15. Critical Partner removal requires dependency awareness.
16. Unknown Production credential is a governance defect.
17. External authenticated request still requires business validation.
18. External retries must not duplicate business effects.
19. SMP1 needs only lifecycle control for current critical integrations.
20. Marketplace operating processes must wait until marketplace demand exists.

---

# 3.133 Stage 3 Certification

Stage 3 permanently establishes the implementation-grade operating model for:

- Partner lifecycle
- Partner identity/purpose
- risk-proportional review
- Application lifecycle
- permission requests/reviews
- Sandbox/Production separation
- integration testing
- Extension review
- Installation
- access granting
- Company scope
- credential provisioning/rotation/revocation
- permission changes
- Application Version upgrades
- marketplace listing lifecycle
- integration monitoring
- external dependency incidents
- narrow containment
- suspension/revocation
- uninstallation
- commercial/technical closure
- Partner retirement
- dependency transition
- periodic access review
- orphaned credentials
- Audit
- incoming/outgoing synchronization
- retries/replay protection
- Security/Data/Compliance/Operations escalation
- SMP1 minimal lifecycle
- ERP9/ERP10/Version 1.1 reuse
- anti-duplication
- anti-overengineering

This is sufficient to govern real external integrations and future ecosystem participation without turning SMP1 into an ecosystem-platform implementation programme.

# ENTERPRISE ECOSYSTEM MARKETPLACE, PARTNER NETWORK & PLATFORM EXPANSION CANON
## Stage 4 — Partner Registry, Developer/API Gateway, Extension Registry, Installation, Credential, Webhook, Certification & Marketplace Service Architecture Canon

---

# 4.1 Purpose

Stage 4 defines the future service architecture required to manage external Partners, applications, extensions, credentials, permissions, installations, webhooks, certification, and marketplace participation.

The objective is:

> **Provide controlled ecosystem services that let external applications connect to GiftHatkeOS through explicit identities, permissions, contracts, and lifecycle controls without exposing internal platform internals or creating a second business system.**

---

# 4.2 Core Service Landscape

Future-capable ecosystem services may include:

- Partner Registry Service
- Application Registry Service
- Extension Registry Service
- Capability Registry Service
- Partner Access Service
- API Gateway
- Credential Service
- Installation Service
- Environment Binding Service
- Company Binding Service
- Webhook Service
- Certification Service
- Compatibility Service
- Marketplace Catalog Service
- Subscription Service
- Partner Audit Service
- Partner Health Service
- Partner Incident Service

Not all are required initially.

# 4.119 Existing Integrations First

SMP1 architecture priority:

```text id="existing-integration-priority43s4"
Current Business-Critical Integration

↓

Stable Standalone Contract

↓

Secure Production Operation

before

Future Ecosystem Services
```

---

# 4.120 First Reusable Ecosystem Step

When multiple integrations require common governance, introduce:

- Application Registry
- Credential Service
- Permission/Scope model
- Audit

first.

---

# 4.121 Second Maturity Step

If third-party Extensions appear, add:

- Extension Registry
- Installation Service
- certification/compatibility

---

# 4.122 Third Maturity Step

Only with meaningful ecosystem demand add:

- Developer Portal
- Marketplace Catalog
- Subscription/Commercial Services

---

# 4.123 ERP9 Reuse

ERP9 may improve:

- Company configuration
- Partner master references
- external service configuration

that these services can consume.

---

# 4.124 ERP10 Reuse

ERP10 may improve:

- Integration administration
- error handling
- permission review
- operational visibility

---

# 4.125 Version 1.1 Reuse

Version 1.1 may add a small Application Registry or integration administration service if current integration count justifies it.

---

# 4.126 Advanced Services That Can Wait

Do not block roadmap for:

- public app store infrastructure
- developer monetization platform
- automated partner payouts
- partner rating/review service
- extension dependency resolver
- application recommendation engine
- public SDK distribution platform
- partner tier engine
- marketplace advertising service
- automated third-party certification platform

---

# 4.127 Anti-Duplication Rule

Permanent:

> **Domain 43 ecosystem services control external identities, applications, permissions, installations, and marketplace participation. They do not replace Domain 13 integration contracts, Domain 28 Security, Domain 29 data governance, Domain 41 infrastructure, or business Domain services.**

---

# 4.128 Anti-Platform-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **The existence of reusable integration services must not turn GiftHatkeOS into a public platform business unless that becomes an explicit commercial strategy.**

---

# 4.129 Anti-Overengineering Rule

Permanent:

> **Implement shared ecosystem services only when repeated external integration needs justify them. One shipping provider and one marketplace connector do not require building an app marketplace.**

---

# 4.130 Critical Service Invariants

1. Ecosystem Service Layer ≠ parallel business platform.
2. Partner Registry ≠ Supplier/Customer Master.
3. Partner approved ≠ Application approved.
4. Application registered ≠ Extension installed.
5. Capability registered ≠ capability trusted.
6. API Gateway ≠ Business Rule Engine.
7. Valid credential ≠ authorized operation.
8. Test credential ≠ Production credential.
9. External application must not infer Company authority.
10. Internal Event ≠ automatically externally publishable Event.
11. Partner Event ≠ authoritative business state.
12. Synchronization service cannot arbitrarily choose business truth.
13. Idempotency must protect material external writes.
14. Marketplace Catalog ≠ Security trust store.
15. Commercial entitlement ≠ technical authorization.
16. Developer self-service ≠ Production self-approval.
17. Partner API healthy ≠ business integration healthy.
18. Permission unknown ≠ allow.
19. SMP1 requires only current business-critical integration services.
20. Advanced ecosystem services must follow real Partner/platform demand.

---

# 4.131 Stage 4 Certification

Stage 4 permanently establishes the implementation-grade service architecture for:

- Partner Registry
- Application Registry
- Extension Registry
- Capability Registry
- Extension Points
- external access resolution
- API Gateway
- Credential Service
- Environment/Company bindings
- Installation Service
- Webhooks
- incoming external Events
- identifier mapping
- synchronization
- idempotency/correlation
- rate limiting
- certification
- compatibility
- Marketplace Catalog
- subscriptions
- developer portal
- API documentation
- Partner Audit
- Partner Health
- Partner incidents
- revocation
- Domain 13/28/29/41 integration
- business Domain routing
- SMP1 minimum/non-requirements
- maturity sequencing
- ERP9/ERP10/Version 1.1 reuse
- anti-duplication
- anti-platform-drift
- anti-overengineering

This is sufficient to define a controlled future ecosystem service layer while keeping the current standalone programme focused entirely on the integrations actually required by the business.

# ENTERPRISE ECOSYSTEM MARKETPLACE, PARTNER NETWORK & PLATFORM EXPANSION CANON
## Stage 5 — Partner Governance, External Trust, Application Permissions, Extension Risk, Data Access, Commercial Authority & Ecosystem Accountability Canon

---

# 5.1 Purpose

Stage 5 defines how GiftHatkeOS governs external Partners, applications, extensions, permissions, data access, trust, risk, commercial authority, and accountability.

The objective is:

> **Ensure external ecosystem participation is explicitly authorized, risk-proportional, least-privilege, auditable, revocable, and incapable of silently acquiring internal business authority.**

---

# 5.2 Governance Philosophy

Permanent principles:

- external identity does not create trust automatically.
- trust does not create unlimited access.
- Partner approval and Application approval are separate.
- commercial relationship and technical authority are separate.
- data access must follow purpose and permission.
- high-impact Extensions require stronger controls.
- external access must be revocable.
- Partner accountability must remain attributable.
- business Domains retain business authority.
- ecosystem governance must remain proportional to actual Risk.

---

# 5.3 Governance Layers

Canonical:

```text id="ecosystem-governance43s5"
Enterprise Governance

↓

Partner Relationship Governance

↓

Application / Extension Governance

↓

Permission & Data Scope

↓

Installation / Execution

↓

Business Domain Validation
```

---

# 5.4 External Trust Model

Trust should be established through:

- verified Partner identity
- approved business purpose
- Security review where needed
- data review
- technical validation
- operational history

---

# 5.5 Trust Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="trust-boundary43s5"
Known Brand / Vendor
≠
Automatically Trusted Application
```

---

# 5.6 Partner Approval

Partner approval confirms:

- identity
- intended relationship
- acceptable organizational trust

It does not grant unrestricted Production access.

---

# 5.7 Application Approval

Application approval is separate and should evaluate:

- purpose
- requested scopes
- Environment
- Company access
- behavior
- Risk

---

# 5.8 Partner vs Application Approval

Permanent:

```text id="partner-app-approval43s5"
Partner Approved
≠
Application Approved
```

---

# 5.9 Extension Approval

An Extension may require independent review even when its Application is approved.

---

# 5.10 Version Approval

Materially changed versions may require revalidation.

---

# 5.11 Trust Is Scoped

Trust may be specific to:

- capability
- Company
- Environment
- data type
- operation

---

# 5.12 No Universal Trust

Permanent:

```text id="universal-trust43s5"
Trusted for Shipping Labels
≠
Trusted for Finance Data
```

---

# 5.13 Partner Owner

Each material Partner relationship should have an internal owner.

---

# 5.14 Partner Owner Responsibilities

Potential:

- relationship oversight
- purpose validation
- access review
- escalation
- lifecycle decision

---

# 5.15 Owner Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="owner-boundary43s5"
Partner Owner
≠
Security Approver
≠
Finance Approver
≠
Legal Approver
```

---

# 5.16 External Application Owner

Important applications may also have an internal technical/business owner.

---

# 5.17 Accountability Chain

Canonical:

```text id="accountability-chain43s5"
Partner

↓

Application

↓

Internal Owner

↓

Permissions

↓

Business Operation

↓

Audit
```

---

# 5.18 Permission Governance

Permissions should follow:

- least privilege
- purpose limitation
- explicit scope
- revocability

---

# 5.19 Permission Dimensions

Potential:

- API
- read/write
- Company
- Environment
- data category
- record type
- operation

---

# 5.20 Permission Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="permission-boundary43s5"
Application Has Credential
≠
Application Has Permission
```

---

# 5.21 Read Authority

Read access should be separately granted.

---

# 5.22 Write Authority

Write access is materially stronger and should receive additional review where appropriate.

---

# 5.23 Delete Authority

External deletion capabilities should be highly restricted.

---

# 5.24 Administrative Authority

Third-party applications should not receive broad internal administrative authority by default.

---

# 5.25 New Write Scope

Permanent:

```text id="new-write-scope43s5"
Existing Read Integration
+
New Write Permission
=
Material Authority Expansion
```

---

# 5.26 Company Scope

Domain 40 governs multi-company authority.

---

# 5.27 Company Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="company-boundary43s5"
Application Authorized in Company A
≠
Application Authorized in Company B
```

---

# 5.28 Environment Scope

Production authority must remain distinct from:

- Development
- Test
- Sandbox

---

# 5.29 Production Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="production-boundary43s5"
Sandbox Credential
≠
Production Credential
```

---

# 5.30 External Data Access

Applications should receive only the data necessary for approved purpose.

---

# 5.31 Data Purpose

Potential purposes:

- fulfillment
- payment
- analytics
- communication
- marketplace synchronization

---

# 5.32 Purpose Limitation

Permanent:

```text id="purpose-limitation43s5"
Data Available
≠
Data May Be Used for Any Purpose
```

---

# 5.33 Sensitive Data

Sensitive data access may require:

- stronger approval
- narrower scope
- specific provider controls

---

# 5.34 Data Minimization

Prefer:

- required fields only

over full-record disclosure.

---

# 5.35 Data Disclosure Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="disclosure-boundary43s5"
Can Read Record
≠
Can Export / Redistribute Record
```

---

# 5.36 External Data Retention

Domain 29/24 govern:

- retention
- deletion
- contractual handling
- privacy

---

# 5.37 Data Residency

If future legal/operational requirements arise:

Data residency constraints may apply.

Do not implement multi-region complexity without real need.

---

# 5.38 Credential Governance

Credentials should be:

- application-specific
- Environment-specific
- revocable
- rotated where appropriate

---

# 5.39 Shared Credential Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="shared-credential43s5"
One Shared Credential for Many Unrelated Integrations
=
Poor Governance
```

---

# 5.40 Secret Governance

Secret values should not be exposed through ordinary administrative screens or logs.

---

# 5.41 Credential Rotation

Rotation should preserve continuity without creating uncontrolled simultaneous access.

---

# 5.42 Credential Revocation

Security-critical revocation must be prompt.

---

# 5.43 Orphaned Credential

Production credential without clear owner/application/purpose is a governance defect.

---

# 5.44 Extension Risk Model

Recommended:

- LOW
- MODERATE
- HIGH
- PROHIBITED

---

# 5.45 Low-Risk Extension

Examples:

- read-only reporting
- non-sensitive export

---

# 5.46 Moderate-Risk Extension

Examples:

- communication connector
- workflow task creation

---

# 5.47 High-Risk Extension

Examples:

- Order creation
- Inventory write
- Payment initiation
- shipping commitment

---

# 5.48 Prohibited Extension

Examples:

- authorization bypass
- unrestricted DB mutation
- Secret extraction
- hidden background data export

---

# 5.49 Contextual Risk

Risk also depends on:

- batch size
- record sensitivity
- financial amount
- Company scope
- irreversibility

---

# 5.50 Risk Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="risk-boundary43s5"
Low-Risk Capability
at Small Scale
≠
Low-Risk Capability at Unlimited Scale
```

---

# 5.51 Installation Governance

Installation authority should depend on:

- Extension Risk
- Company
- requested scopes
- user Role

---

# 5.52 Self-Service Installation

May be allowed only for sufficiently low-risk certified extensions.

---

# 5.53 Installation Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="installation-boundary43s5"
Visible in Catalog
≠
Safe for Automatic Installation
```

---

# 5.54 Permission Consent

Where useful, installation should show requested scopes in plain language.

---

# 5.55 Scope Transparency

Example:

```text id="scope-transparency43s5"
This application can:

✓ Read Orders
✓ Create Shipping Labels

It cannot:

✕ Change Prices
✕ Access Finance
```

---

# 5.56 No Hidden Scope Increase

Updates that materially add permissions should require review.

---

# 5.57 Extension Update Governance

Material changes may include:

- new permissions
- new data access
- new write operations
- changed external destination

---

# 5.58 Automatic Update Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="auto-update-boundary43s5"
Extension Update Available
≠
Safe to Auto-Grant New Authority
```

---

# 5.59 API Scope Governance

API scopes should remain:

- understandable
- bounded
- versioned where needed

---

# 5.60 Scope Granularity

Avoid both extremes:

- one giant admin scope
- thousands of unusably tiny scopes

---

# 5.61 External Event Governance

Applications receive only approved event categories.

---

# 5.62 Event Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="event-boundary43s5"
Can Receive Order Event
≠
Can Read Every Order Field
```

---

# 5.63 Webhook Endpoint Governance

External endpoints should be:

- registered
- authenticated
- reviewable
- disableable

---

# 5.64 Incoming External Events

Incoming Event must be authenticated and validated.

---

# 5.65 Incoming Event Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="incoming-event-boundary43s5"
Partner Reports State X
≠
GiftHatkeOS Must Accept State X
```

---

# 5.66 Commercial Governance

Partner commercial arrangements may include:

- fees
- usage charges
- commissions
- revenue share
- subscription

---

# 5.67 Commercial Authority

Domain 6/31 remain financial/commercial truth authorities.

---

# 5.68 Commercial Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="commercial-boundary43s5"
Technical Access Approved
≠
Commercial Terms Approved
```

---

# 5.69 Legal Authority

Domain 24 governs:

- contracts
- liability
- terms
- data-processing obligations

---

# 5.70 Legal Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="legal-boundary43s5"
Application Works Technically
≠
Legal Relationship Is Approved
```

---

# 5.71 Marketplace Governance

If a marketplace exists, listing review may assess:

- publisher identity
- capability claims
- permissions
- support
- compatibility
- Risk

---

# 5.72 Marketplace Trust Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="marketplace-trust43s5"
Published in Marketplace
≠
GiftHatke Guarantees Every Business Outcome
```

---

# 5.73 Certification Labels

If certification labels are used:

They should communicate clearly what was actually reviewed.

---

# 5.74 No Overstated Certification

Do not imply:

- Security
- business quality
- legal compliance
- uptime

were certified if they were not.

---

# 5.75 Marketplace Ranking

Future listing ranking should not override Security or compliance controls.

---

# 5.76 Paid Promotion Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="promotion-boundary43s5"
Partner Paid for Promotion
≠
Partner Gains More Technical Trust
```

---

# 5.77 Partner Tier

Future Partner tiers may represent:

- commercial relationship
- support level
- certification depth

but not hidden Security privilege.

---

# 5.78 Partner Tier Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="tier-boundary43s5"
Gold / Premium Partner
≠
Administrator
```

---

# 5.79 Support Governance

Material Partners should identify:

- operational support
- escalation contact

---

# 5.80 SLA Governance

Formal SLA exists only where explicitly agreed.

---

# 5.81 SLA Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="sla-boundary43s5"
Good Historical Uptime
≠
Contractual SLA
```

---

# 5.82 External Dependency Governance

Critical dependencies should be identified.

Examples:

- payment
- shipping
- marketplace sync

---

# 5.83 Criticality Classification

Potential:

- NON-CRITICAL
- IMPORTANT
- CRITICAL

---

# 5.84 Criticality Boundary

Not every integration should be labeled critical.

---

# 5.85 Business Continuity

Domain 38 governs continuity requirements for critical external dependencies.

---

# 5.86 Failure Isolation

Where practical:

One external provider failure should not collapse unrelated ERP capabilities.

---

# 5.87 External Incident Governance

Material external incidents may include:

- credential compromise
- unauthorized access
- bad bulk writes
- data leakage
- duplicate transactions
- prolonged critical outage

---

# 5.88 Incident Containment

Potential controls:

- credential revoke
- Application suspend
- Installation suspend
- Partner suspend

---

# 5.89 Narrow Containment Principle

Prefer the smallest safe blast-radius containment.

---

# 5.90 Emergency Authority

Security/Platform authorized Roles may suspend external access immediately when required.

---

# 5.91 Incident Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="incident-boundary43s5"
Partner Incident
≠
Automatic Deletion of Partner Business Records
```

---

# 5.92 Business Reconciliation

Owning Domain determines correction of affected business state.

---

# 5.93 External Auditability

Material external operations should identify:

- Partner
- Application
- credential/service identity
- Company
- action
- result
- timestamp

---

# 5.94 Accountability Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="accountability-boundary43s5"
"Third Party Did It"
≠
Untraceable Action
```

---

# 5.95 Audit vs Assurance

Domain 39 remains formal assurance authority.

---

# 5.96 Periodic Access Review

Material Production integrations should periodically verify:

- still needed
- scopes still appropriate
- credentials controlled
- owner still valid

---

# 5.97 Review Frequency

Risk-based, not bureaucratic.

---

# 5.98 Dormant Application

Unused Production Application should be reviewed for:

- suspension
- retirement
- credential revocation

---

# 5.99 Dormant Access Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="dormant-access43s5"
Not Used Recently
≠
Safe to Leave Privileged Forever
```

---

# 5.100 Partner Termination

Termination should distinguish:

- commercial termination
- technical revocation
- data obligations
- operational dependency transition

---

# 5.101 Technical Closure

Verify:

- credentials revoked
- API scopes disabled
- webhooks disabled
- scheduled jobs stopped

---

# 5.102 Data Closure

Verify retention/deletion obligations where applicable.

---

# 5.103 Business Continuity Closure

Critical dependency replacement should be handled before irreversible shutdown where necessary.

---

# 5.104 Historical Integrity

Permanent:

```text id="history-integrity43s5"
Partner Relationship Ended
≠
Historical Transactions Removed
```

---

# 5.105 External Developer Governance

If future developer self-service exists:

Developers may:

- register
- build
- test

but not self-approve Production authority.

---

# 5.106 Developer Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="developer-boundary43s5"
Developer Account
≠
Production Access
```

---

# 5.107 Extension SDK Governance

Future SDKs should expose controlled supported interfaces.

---

# 5.108 SDK Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="sdk-boundary43s5"
SDK Capability
≠
Access to Internal Unsupported APIs
```

---

# 5.109 Partner Certification Governance

High-impact integrations may require formal technical certification.

---

# 5.110 Certification Depth

Certification should match actual Risk.

---

# 5.111 Recertification

May be required after material:

- version
- permission
- Security
- data-handling

change.

---

# 5.112 No Permanent Certification

Permanent:

```text id="certification-permanence43s5"
Certified Version A
≠
Version B Automatically Certified
```

---

# 5.113 Security Authority

Domain 28 remains authoritative for:

- external authentication
- authorization
- credential lifecycle
- privilege enforcement

---

# 5.114 Data Authority

Domain 29 remains authoritative for:

- external data sharing
- privacy
- retention
- classification

---

# 5.115 Integration Authority

Domain 13 remains authoritative for:

- API contracts
- integration patterns
- connectivity

---

# 5.116 Business Domain Authority

External applications cannot redefine:

- Orders
- Inventory
- Production
- Finance
- Shipping
- other certified Domain semantics

---

# 5.117 Workflow Authority

Domain 11 remains workflow authority.

---

# 5.118 AI Extensions

Domain 42 governs AI Agent/autonomy behavior supplied by ecosystem Extensions.

---

# 5.119 Platform Authority

Domain 41 governs Production runtime/infrastructure.

Third parties do not gain platform-admin authority merely because they integrate.

---

# 5.120 SMP1 Governance Requirement

For SMP1:

```text id="smp1-governance43s5"
Required Ecosystem Governance:
Only What Current Production Integrations Need
```

---

# 5.121 SMP1 Minimum Controls

For each critical current integration:

- known Application identity
- purpose
- credentials
- permissions
- Company/Environment context
- operational owner
- Audit
- revocation capability

---

# 5.122 SMP1 Non-Requirements

Do not establish:

- Partner governance board
- public marketplace policies
- Partner tiers
- Extension certification department
- developer approval programme
- ecosystem revenue-share governance

---

# 5.123 First Future Governance Step

When reusable Partner governance becomes necessary:

Start with:

- Partner/Application registry
- permission review
- credential lifecycle
- ownership
- revocation

---

# 5.124 Marketplace Governance Trigger

Only build marketplace governance when:

- multiple third-party listings exist
- repeated submissions occur
- user discovery/install becomes real

---

# 5.125 ERP9 Reuse

ERP9 may strengthen:

- Company
- configuration
- Partner references
- role/authority data

used by ecosystem governance.

---

# 5.126 ERP10 Reuse

ERP10 may improve:

- access review
- integration administration
- audit visibility
- suspension controls

---

# 5.127 Version 1.1 Reuse

Version 1.1 may formalize Application governance if external integration growth justifies it.

---

# 5.128 Advanced Governance That Can Wait

Do not block roadmap for:

- public marketplace governance board
- Partner reputation engine
- developer trust scores
- automated legal-contracting portal
- partner tier automation
- marketplace dispute system
- app moderation workforce
- ecosystem fraud scoring
- global developer certification framework

---

# 5.129 Anti-Duplication Rule

Permanent:

> **Domain 43 governs external ecosystem trust, access, Partner/application authority, and Extension Risk. It does not replace Security, Data Governance, Contracts, Finance, Integration architecture, or Business Domain authority.**

---

# 5.130 Anti-Platform-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **Govern external participation only to the level required by real integrations and ecosystem activity. GiftHatkeOS remains a business platform first.**

---

# 5.131 Anti-Overengineering Rule

Permanent:

> **A current shipping connector needs clear identity, credentials, permissions, ownership, monitoring, and revocation. It does not need a marketplace governance bureaucracy.**

---

# 5.132 Critical Governance Invariants

1. External identity ≠ automatic trust.
2. Trust ≠ unlimited access.
3. Partner approval ≠ Application approval.
4. Trust for one capability ≠ trust for all Domains.
5. Application credential ≠ permission.
6. READ ≠ WRITE ≠ DELETE ≠ ADMIN.
7. Company A authority ≠ Company B authority.
8. Sandbox credential ≠ Production credential.
9. Data available ≠ data usable for every purpose.
10. Can read ≠ can redistribute.
11. Shared privileged credentials are poor governance.
12. Low-risk at small scale ≠ low-risk at unlimited scale.
13. Catalog visibility ≠ installation authority.
14. Extension update ≠ automatic new permission approval.
15. Incoming Partner Event ≠ accepted business truth.
16. Technical approval ≠ commercial or Legal approval.
17. Marketplace promotion ≠ increased technical trust.
18. Partner tier ≠ administrative privilege.
19. Third-party action must remain attributable.
20. SMP1 implements only governance needed by current real integrations.

---

# 5.133 Stage 5 Certification

Stage 5 permanently establishes the implementation-grade governance architecture for:

- external trust
- Partner/Application/Extension approval
- ownership/accountability
- permission governance
- read/write/delete/admin separation
- Company/Environment scope
- external-data access
- data minimization/retention
- credential governance
- Extension Risk
- installation permissions
- permission transparency
- Extension updates
- API scopes
- Event/webhook governance
- commercial authority
- Legal authority
- marketplace trust
- certification labels
- Partner tiers
- external dependency criticality
- incidents/containment
- access reviews
- termination/closure
- developer/SDK governance
- certification/recertification
- Domain 11/13/28/29/41/42 boundaries
- SMP1 minimum controls
- ERP9/ERP10/Version 1.1 reuse
- anti-duplication
- anti-platform-drift
- anti-overengineering

This is sufficient to govern future external ecosystem authority safely while keeping current GiftHatkeOS execution focused only on integrations the business actually needs.

**Stage 5 Status: ✅ CERTIFIED**

**Enterprise Canon Position: Domain 43 — IN PROGRESS (5/10 stages certified).**

# ENTERPRISE ECOSYSTEM MARKETPLACE, PARTNER NETWORK & PLATFORM EXPANSION CANON
## Stage 6 — Partner Events, Application Installation Automation, Webhook Orchestration, External Synchronization, Certification Routing, Suspension & Ecosystem Incident Escalation Canon

---

# 6.1 Purpose

Stage 6 defines how Partner events, application installations, webhook delivery, external synchronization, certification routing, access changes, incidents, suspensions, and escalations should be orchestrated.

The objective is:

> **Allow external ecosystem activity to move through predictable, traceable workflows while ensuring that external automation never bypasses permissions, business validation, Company scope, or certified Domain authority.**

---

# 6.2 Core Orchestration Principle

Permanent:

```text id="ecosystem-orchestration43s6"
External Event / Request

↓

Identity

↓

Authorization

↓
```

# 6.128 Anti-Duplication Rule

---

# 6.129 Anti-Platform-Drift Rule

Permanent:

---

Permanent:

> **The first reusable ecosystem automation should solve repeated integration problems—authentication, webhook reliability, reconciliation, and access control—not create a generalized marketplace orchestration platform.**

---

# 6.131 Critical Orchestration Invariants

1. Ecosystem Event ≠ Business Domain Event.
2. Partner activation ≠ Application activation.
3. Permission approval ≠ unlimited application trust.
4. Installation script completed ≠ integration proven operational.
5. System must not invent missing permission.
6. Webhook retry ≠ repeat business transaction.
7. Authenticated incoming event ≠ accepted business state.
8. Bidirectional sync ≠ dual authority.
9. Sync job finished ≠ records reconciled.
10. Partner retry must not duplicate material business effect.
11. Certification completed ≠ Production access automatically granted.
12. Application update ≠ permission expansion approval.
13. Suspension ≠ invalidation of historical business records.
14. Status revocation ≠ verified technical closure until access is actually disabled.
15. Uninstall requires dependency awareness.
16. Partner outage ≠ loss of ERP business truth.
17. Dead-lettered work ≠ resolved work.
18. Billing state ≠ Security authorization state.
19. SMP1 requires orchestration only for current critical integrations.
20. Marketplace automation waits for actual marketplace activity.

---

- SMP1 minimum/non-requirements

This is sufficient to orchestrate current and future external ecosystem activity safely without introducing a generalized marketplace platform before the business has one.

# ENTERPRISE ECOSYSTEM MARKETPLACE, PARTNER NETWORK & PLATFORM EXPANSION CANON
## Stage 7 — Partner Administration, Application Installation, Permission Consent, Integration Health, Marketplace Discovery, Certification, Incident & Audit UX Canon

---

# 7.1 Purpose

Stage 7 defines the user experience required to administer external Partners, applications, extensions, credentials, permissions, installations, integration health, certification, incidents, and future marketplace discovery.

The objective is:

> **Make external ecosystem access visible, understandable, controllable, and easy to revoke while keeping ordinary business users focused on business operations rather than integration infrastructure.**

---

# 7.2 UX Philosophy

Permanent principles:

- users should know which external application is acting.
- permissions should be understandable in business language.
- installation must not hide requested authority.
- Production and Sandbox must be visibly distinct.
- integration failures should show business impact.
- suspension and revocation must be easy for authorized users.
- external and internal functionality should remain distinguishable where material.
- marketplace UX is optional future maturity.
- ecosystem administration should not become a second ERP.

---

# 7.3 Core Future Workspaces

Potential:

- Partner Registry
- Partner Detail
- Application Registry
- Application Detail
- Extension Catalog
- Installation Workspace
- Permission Review
- Credential Administration
- Integration Health
- Sync/Reconciliation Queue
- Webhook Administration
- Certification Workspace
- Partner Incident Workspace
- Ecosystem Audit
- Marketplace Discovery

---

# 7.4 Partner Registry

Should answer:

- Which Partners exist?
- What type are they?
- Which are active?
- Who owns each relationship?
- Are any suspended?

---

# 7.130 Anti-Duplication Rule

Permanent:

> **Ecosystem UX should expose external capability inside the relevant business and administrative workflows. It must not create duplicate Partner-owned versions of Orders, Shipping, Inventory, Finance, CRM, or other certified modules.**

---

# 7.131 Anti-Platform-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **Do not make GiftHatkeOS look like an app marketplace before ecosystem scale makes marketplace discovery a real user need.**

---

# 7.132 Anti-Overengineering Rule

Permanent:

> **For current integrations, users mainly need four things: configure it, know whether it works, understand what access it has, and disable it safely. Everything beyond that must earn its place.**

---

# 7.133 Critical UX Invariants

1. Partner Active ≠ every Application Active.
2. Application identity should be visible separately from Partner identity.
3. Sandbox must remain distinguishable from Production.
4. Company access must be understandable.
5. Catalog visibility ≠ Installation.
6. Certification label must not imply unlimited trust.
7. Installation must disclose material requested permissions.
8. Software update ≠ permission expansion approval.
9. Setup complete ≠ integration operational.
10. Credential metadata visible ≠ Secret visible.
11. API healthy ≠ business integration healthy.
12. Sync finished ≠ records reconciled.
13. Conflict must not be silently overwritten where source authority is material.
14. Dead-lettered work ≠ resolved.
15. Suspension should preserve historical business records.
16. Partner online again ≠ integration fully recovered.
17. Marketplace discoverable ≠ recommended or installed.
18. Paid subscription ≠ technical authorization.
19. SMP1 needs only current integration administration UX.
20. Ecosystem UX must solve operational needs before marketplace presentation.

---

# 7.134 Stage 7 Certification

Stage 7 permanently establishes the implementation-grade UX architecture for:

- Partner Registry
- Partner/Application identity
- Environment/Company visibility
- Extension Catalog
- certification labels

- permission consent
- permission deltas

- conflict handling
- retries/duplicate protection
- webhook administration
- dead-letter queues
- certification review
- suspension/revocation
- dependency warnings
- uninstallation
- Partner incidents
- recovery
- external Audit/attribution
- future marketplace discovery
- commercial plan/subscription UX
- Application updates/deprecation
- role-based views
- manual fallback
- contextual integration panels
- SMP1 practical scope
- ERP9/ERP10/Version 1.1 reuse
- anti-duplication
- anti-platform-drift
- anti-overengineering

This is sufficient to make current and future external integrations understandable and controllable without building marketplace-heavy UI before a genuine ecosystem exists.
