# ENTERPRISE ECOSYSTEM MARKETPLACE, PARTNER NETWORK & PLATFORM EXPANSION CANON
## Stage 8 — Partner Performance, Integration Reliability, Ecosystem Risk, Adoption, Commercial Value, Support Quality & Marketplace Intelligence Canon

---

# 8.1 Purpose

Stage 8 defines how GiftHatkeOS should measure whether external Partners, applications, extensions, integrations, and future marketplace capabilities are reliable, useful, safe, commercially sensible, and operationally worth maintaining.

The objective is:

> **Evaluate ecosystem capability by real business reliability, operational value, Risk, support quality, adoption, and commercial impact rather than by the number of Partners, integrations, or marketplace listings.**

---

# 8.2 Intelligence Philosophy

Permanent principles:

- business reliability before ecosystem scale.
- operational value before Partner count.
- critical integration health before marketplace growth.
- adoption does not equal value.
- Partner uptime does not equal business success.
- API success does not equal synchronization success.
- commercial revenue does not override Security or data governance.
- support quality matters for operational dependencies.
- external Risk must remain visible.
- metrics must remain proportional to actual ecosystem maturity.

---

# 8.3 Core Intelligence Areas

Future-capable measurement may include:

- Partner Activity
- Application Usage
- Integration Reliability
- API Success
- Webhook Delivery
- Synchronization Health
- Reconciliation Quality
- Incident Frequency
- Security/Access Risk
- Partner Support Quality
- Adoption
- Installation Activity
- Extension Usage
- Commercial Value
- Cost
- Dependency Criticality
- Certification Quality
- Marketplace Discovery
- Retention
- Ecosystem Growth

---

# 8.4 Partner Activity

Potential:

- active Partners
- active Applications
- active Installations
- suspended Applications
- retired relationships

---

# 8.5 Partner Count Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="partner-count43s8"
More Partners
≠
Stronger Ecosystem
```

A few high-value reliable Partners may be better than many unused ones.

---

# 8.6 Application Activity

Track where useful:

- requests
- sync jobs
- business transactions supported
- active users/Companies

---

# 8.7 Activity Boundary

```text id="application-activity43s8"

≠

```

---

# 8.8 Integration Reliability

Measure whether integration performs the required business function reliably.

Potential:

- backlog

---

```text id="api-success43s8"
/

```

---

# 8.10 API Success Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="api-success-boundary43s8"
HTTP/API Success
≠
Business Process Success
```

---

# 8.11 Business Integration Success

For a shipping connector, a meaningful metric is:

- labels successfully created

not merely:

- API calls completed.

---

# 8.12 Webhook Delivery Quality

Potential:

- successful deliveries
- retries
- dead-lettered events
- delivery latency

---

# 8.13 Webhook Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="webhook-quality43s8"
Webhook Delivered
≠
Partner Processed Event Correctly
```

unless acknowledgment semantics prove it.

---

# 8.14 Synchronization Reliability

Track:

- expected records
- processed
- failed
- skipped
- conflicted

---

# 8.15 Sync Success Rate

Potential:

```text id="sync-success43s8"
Successfully Reconciled Records
/
Expected Sync Population
```

where applicable.

---

# 8.16 Sync Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="sync-job-boundary43s8"
Sync Job Completed
≠
All Records Correctly Reconciled
```

---

# 8.17 Reconciliation Quality

Measure differences such as:

- external vs internal Order count
- Inventory quantity mismatch
- shipping status mismatch
- payment status mismatch

---

# 8.18 Reconciliation Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="reconciliation-boundary43s8"
No Detected Difference
≠
Integration Proven Correct
```

if monitoring coverage is incomplete.

---

# 8.19 Data Freshness

For time-sensitive integration, measure:

- last successful sync
- age of oldest pending item

---

# 8.20 Freshness Boundary

Not every integration requires real-time synchronization.

---

# 8.21 Backlog

Track pending:

- outbound requests
- imports
- webhook deliveries
- reconciliation work

---

# 8.22 Backlog Age

Age may matter more than raw count.

---

# 8.23 Backlog Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="backlog-boundary43s8"
10 Pending for 2 Minutes
may be healthier than
1 Pending for 3 Days
```

---

# 8.24 Integration Latency

Measure where delay affects:

- fulfillment
- Customer experience
- payment
- Inventory availability

---

# 8.25 Latency Boundary

Do not optimize every background integration for real-time performance without business need.

---

# 8.26 Retry Intelligence

Track:

- retries by reason
- successful retry
- exhausted retry
- duplicate protection events

---

# 8.27 Retry Boundary

High retry success may still indicate an unstable Partner service.

---

# 8.28 Dead-Letter Intelligence

Track:

- records/events entering dead-letter queue
- age
- resolution time

---

# 8.29 Dead-Letter Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="deadletter-intelligence43s8"
Moved to Dead Letter
≠
Handled
```

---

# 8.30 Integration Failure Classification

Useful categories:

- Authentication
- Authorization
- Validation
- Partner API
- Network
- Mapping
- Business Rule
- Data Conflict
- Internal Platform

---

# 8.31 Failure Ownership

Failure classification should help identify:

- GiftHatke
- Partner
- configuration
- business data

responsibility.

---

# 8.32 Partner Availability

Potential:

- uptime
- outage duration
- degraded periods

for important services.

---

# 8.33 Availability Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="partner-availability43s8"
Partner Uptime 99.9%
≠
GiftHatke Integration Uptime 99.9%
```

Local integration defects may exist.

---

# 8.34 Critical Dependency Health

For critical Partners monitor:

- availability
- transaction success
- backlog
- fallback readiness

---

# 8.35 Criticality Boundary

Not all external services deserve 24/7 operational metrics.

---

# 8.36 Incident Frequency

Track material Partner/integration incidents.

Examples:

- credential compromise
- duplicate transactions
- sync corruption
- prolonged outage
- unauthorized access

---

# 8.37 Incident Severity

Use existing Domain 14/39 models where possible.

---

# 8.38 Incident Trend

Repeated incidents from same Partner/Application may trigger:

- access reduction
- remediation
- alternative provider review
- suspension

---

# 8.39 Near-Miss

Examples:

- unauthorized API attempt blocked
- malformed bulk request rejected
- expired credential used

---

# 8.40 Near-Miss Value

Near-misses can reveal:

- weak Partner configuration
- integration defects
- attempted abuse
- misunderstood scope

---

# 8.41 Access Risk Intelligence

Potential:

- excessive permissions
- unused privileged scopes
- dormant credentials
- cross-Company access
- failed authorization attempts

---

# 8.42 Permission Utilization

A granted scope that is never used may be unnecessary.

---

# 8.43 Permission Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="permission-usage43s8"
Granted Permission Exists
≠
Permission Still Needed
```

---

# 8.44 Dormant Application

Potential indicator:

- no Production activity for defined period

with active credential.

---

# 8.45 Dormant Boundary

Dormancy should trigger review, not automatic deletion.

---

# 8.46 Credential Health

Track:

- active
- expiring
- overdue rotation
- revoked
- orphaned

---

# 8.47 Credential Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="credential-health43s8"
Credential Has Not Failed
≠
Credential Governance Is Healthy
```

---

# 8.48 Security Risk

Potential signals:

- unusual request volume
- repeated forbidden access
- access from unexpected source
- abnormal data extraction

Domain 28 owns Security interpretation.

---

# 8.49 Data Governance Risk

Potential:

- excessive data fields shared
- unnecessary retention
- sensitive data access
- unauthorized export

Domain 29 owns final data-governance interpretation.

---

# 8.50 Partner Support Quality

For operationally important Partners, measure:

- response time
- resolution time
- escalation effectiveness
- communication quality

---

# 8.51 Support Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="support-boundary43s8"
Fast First Reply
≠
Fast Resolution
```

---

# 8.52 Support Escalation Quality

Assess whether Partner provides:

- correct technical owner
- useful updates
- clear resolution

---

# 8.53 SLA Measurement

Where formal SLA exists:

Measure against contractual definition.

---

# 8.54 SLA Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="sla-metric43s8"
Internal Expectation
≠
Contractual SLA
```

---

# 8.55 Partner Reliability Profile

A practical view may include:

- integration success
- incident history
- support performance
- criticality

without creating a single artificial score.

---

# 8.56 No Universal Partner Score

Permanent:

> **Do not compress Security, reliability, commercial value, support, and business criticality into one opaque Partner score.**

---

# 8.57 Application Adoption

Future metrics may include:

- installations
- active Companies
- usage
- retained installations

---

# 8.58 Adoption Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="adoption-boundary43s8"
Installed
≠
Used
≠
Valuable
```

---

# 8.59 Active Installation

Define meaningful activity before calling an Installation active.

---

# 8.60 Extension Usage

Potential:

- active users
- transactions supported
- workflow actions
- reports generated

---

# 8.61 Usage Boundary

High usage may reflect necessity rather than satisfaction.

---

# 8.62 Marketplace Discovery

If marketplace exists, measure:

- searches
- listing views
- installation starts
- completed installs

---

# 8.63 Discovery Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="discovery-boundary43s8"
Listing Viewed
≠
Application Needed
```

---

# 8.64 Installation Conversion

Potential:

```text id="install-conversion43s8"
Completed Installations
/
Qualified Installation Starts
```

---

# 8.65 Conversion Boundary

Do not optimize conversion by hiding permissions or Risk warnings.

---

# 8.66 Uninstallation Rate

May indicate:

- poor value
- technical issues
- changed need
- duplicated capability

---

# 8.67 Uninstall Reason

Where useful classify:

- no longer needed
- poor reliability
- cost
- permission concern
- replaced
- technical incompatibility

---

# 8.68 Retention

A retained application may indicate value, but critical legacy dependency can also create forced retention.

---

# 8.69 Marketplace Reviews

Only meaningful if enough real users participate.

---

# 8.70 Review Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="review-boundary43s8"
High Rating
≠
Security Certification
```

---

# 8.71 Certification Intelligence

Track:

- Applications reviewed
- pass/fail/conditions
- recertifications
- expired certifications

---

# 8.72 Certification Failure Trend

Repeated issues may reveal:

- weak Partner engineering
- unclear standards
- poor integration design

---

# 8.73 Certification Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="certification-quality43s8"
Certification Pass
≠
Future Versions Automatically Safe
```

---

# 8.74 Compatibility Intelligence

Track:

- incompatible versions
- deprecated APIs
- upcoming retirement deadlines
- unsupported Installations

---

# 8.75 Compatibility Risk

Unsupported integration in Production should remain visible.

---

# 8.76 Deprecation Risk

Measure number/importance of integrations still using retiring interfaces.

---

# 8.77 Commercial Value

If ecosystem monetization exists, potential:

- subscription revenue
- Partner fees
- revenue share
- cost avoidance
- operational savings

---

# 8.78 Commercial Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="commercial-value-boundary43s8"
Revenue Generated
≠
Partner Is Safe or Strategically Valuable
```

---

# 8.79 Cost of Integration

True cost may include:

- Partner fees
- API usage
- internal support
- engineering maintenance
- incident handling

---

# 8.80 Total Cost

Potential:

```text id="integration-cost43s8"
External Fees
+
Infrastructure
+
Engineering Maintenance
+
Support
+
Incident Cost
```

---

# 8.81 Value Calculation

For useful integration:

```text id="integration-value43s8"
Business Value / Work Saved

-

Total Integration Cost

=
Net Integration Value
```

where meaningful.

---

# 8.82 Cost Boundary

Cheap integration can still be costly if:

- unreliable
- manually reconciled
- frequently broken

---

# 8.83 Partner Revenue Share

If future marketplace exists:

Financial truth remains with Domain 6/31.

---

# 8.84 Commercial Adoption

Track only if actual ecosystem business model exists.

Not required for current GiftHatkeOS.

---

# 8.85 Business Dependency Value

Some integrations create value by being necessary infrastructure rather than direct revenue.

Examples:

- Shipping
- Payment

---

# 8.86 Replacement Risk

For critical Partner, evaluate:

- availability of alternative
- migration difficulty
- data portability
- switching effort

---

# 8.87 Concentration Risk

Potential:

```text id="concentration-risk43s8"
Critical Business Capability
depends on
Single External Provider
```

This may warrant resilience attention.

---

# 8.88 Concentration Boundary

Single provider is not automatically unacceptable.

Decision depends on:

- business impact
- alternatives
- cost
- complexity

---

# 8.89 Partner Performance Trend

Compare performance over time:

- reliability
- failures
- support
- cost

---

# 8.90 Version Performance

Where relevant compare Integration Versions for:

- failure rate
- latency
- reconciliation

---

# 8.91 Regression Detection

Material decline after upgrade should trigger review.

---

# 8.92 Change Attribution

Do not blame Partner automatically when failure begins after:

- GiftHatke API change
- internal mapping change
- configuration change

---

# 8.93 Integration Owner Metrics

Useful:

- current health
- backlog
- incidents
- credential expiry
- deprecation
- unresolved conflicts

---

# 8.94 Business User Metrics

Useful:

- Orders waiting
- labels failed
- sync backlog
- manual work required

---

# 8.95 Executive Metrics

Only material:

- critical dependency outage
- major incidents
- high integration cost
- strategic Partner Risk
- clear commercial value

---

# 8.96 Security Metrics

Potential:

- blocked unauthorized calls
- dormant privileged credentials
- compromised credentials
- scope violations

Domain 28 remains Security authority.

---

# 8.97 Compliance Metrics

Potential:

- expired certification
- overdue Partner review
- unresolved control exception

Domain 39 remains assurance authority.

---

# 8.98 No Vanity Marketplace Metrics

Avoid emphasizing:

- total listings
- Partner registrations
- API calls
- developer signups

unless they support real strategic decisions.

---

# 8.99 Metric Lineage

Material ecosystem metrics should identify:

- Partner/Application
- Company
- period
- calculation/source

---

# 8.100 Missing Data

If measurement is incomplete:

Use:

- UNKNOWN
- INSUFFICIENT DATA

rather than false precision.

---

# 8.101 Missing Evidence Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="missing-evidence43s8"
No Recorded Partner Incident
≠
Partner Proven Low-Risk
```

---

# 8.102 Business Outcome Attribution

If integration introduced and outcome improved:

Do not automatically claim the integration caused all improvement.

---

# 8.103 Value Review

Periodically ask:

- Is this integration still needed?
- Is it reliable enough?
- Is manual overhead acceptable?
- Is the cost justified?
- Is a simpler alternative available?

---

# 8.104 Retirement Candidate

Application may become retirement candidate when:

- unused
- unreliable
- duplicated
- unsupported
- too costly

---

# 8.105 Retirement Boundary

Metric signal should trigger review.

It should not automatically disconnect critical integration.

---

# 8.106 Ecosystem Growth

Growth may be measured through:

- useful integrations
- reusable capabilities
- external demand

not raw Partner count.

---

# 8.107 Ecosystem Maturity

Practical progression:

```text id="ecosystem-maturity43s8"
Reliable Critical Integrations

↓

Reusable Integration Governance

↓

Multiple External Extensions

↓

Partner Network

↓

Marketplace Only If Valuable
```

---

# 8.108 Marketplace Readiness Indicators

A true marketplace may become justified when:

- multiple external Applications exist
- repeated onboarding occurs
- discovery is difficult
- users request Extensions
- commercial opportunity exists

---

# 8.109 Marketplace Readiness Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="marketplace-readiness43s8"
Technology Can Support Marketplace
≠
Business Needs Marketplace
```

---

# 8.110 Partner Benchmarking

Compare Partners only for comparable capabilities.

Example:

- two Shipping carriers

not:

- Shipping provider vs analytics provider.

---

# 8.111 Benchmark Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="partner-benchmark43s8"
Better API Latency
≠
Better Overall Partner
```

---

# 8.112 Partner Selection Intelligence

Future Partner selection may consider:

- business capability
- reliability
- cost
- support
- Security
- integration effort

---

# 8.113 AI-Assisted Ecosystem Analysis

Domain 42 AI may summarize:

- integration failures
- Partner performance
- reconciliation backlog

but authoritative metrics remain deterministic.

---

# 8.114 AI Analysis Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="ai-ecosystem-boundary43s8"
AI Says Partner Is Best
≠
Partner Selection Authority
```

---

# 8.115 SMP1 Requirement

For SMP1:

```text id="smp1-intelligence43s8"
Required Ecosystem Intelligence:
Only Operational Measures for Current Critical Integrations
```

---

# 8.116 SMP1 Minimum Metrics

For current important integrations:

- health
- last success
- failures
- backlog
- reconciliation state

are sufficient.

---

# 8.117 SMP1 Non-Requirements

Do not build:

- Partner scorecards
- marketplace conversion analytics
- Partner revenue analytics
- Extension adoption dashboards
- developer-growth dashboards
- ecosystem benchmark engine

---

# 8.118 First Reusable Intelligence Step

When integrations grow:

Create one simple Integration Health view.

---

# 8.119 Second Maturity Step

When multiple Applications/Partners exist:

Add:

- reliability trends
- credential/deprecation Risk
- Partner incidents

---

# 8.120 Third Maturity Step

Only when marketplace/commercial ecosystem exists:

Add:

- adoption
- retention
- marketplace conversion
- Partner commercial value

---

# 8.121 ERP9 Reuse

ERP9 configuration and master data can provide clean ownership/context for future Partner metrics.

---

# 8.122 ERP10 Reuse

ERP10 may strengthen:

- health
- reconciliation
- operational reporting

for external integrations.

---

# 8.123 Version 1.1 Reuse

Version 1.1 may introduce a unified current-integration health dashboard if justified by actual operations.

---

# 8.124 Advanced Intelligence That Can Wait

Do not block roadmap for:

- Partner ranking algorithms
- marketplace recommendation analytics
- developer funnel analytics
- Partner lifetime-value models
- ecosystem network-effect scoring
- extension recommendation engine
- Partner churn prediction
- public marketplace benchmarking
- ecosystem revenue forecasting platform

---

# 8.125 Anti-Metric-Gaming Rule

Permanent:

> **Do not optimize Partners or marketplace operations for API volume, listing count, installs, or commercial conversion at the expense of reliability, Security, transparency, or business value.**

---

# 8.126 Anti-Duplication Rule

Permanent:

> **Domain 43 measures ecosystem reliability, external operational value, Partner Risk, and adoption. Domain 14 owns operational observability, Domain 28 Security, Domain 29 data governance, Domain 39 assurance, Domain 6/31 financial truth, and business Domains own business-performance metrics.**

---

# 8.127 Anti-Platform-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **Ecosystem metrics must not create pressure to turn GiftHatkeOS into a marketplace business simply because marketplace-style growth metrics are measurable.**

---

# 8.128 Anti-Overengineering Rule

Permanent:

> **For current GiftHatkeOS integrations, the most useful questions are simple: Is it working? Are business records synchronized? Is it safe? How much manual work does it create? Is the provider still worth using?**

---

# 8.129 Critical Intelligence Invariants

1. More Partners ≠ stronger ecosystem.
2. More API calls ≠ more business value.
3. API success ≠ business-process success.
4. Webhook delivery ≠ Partner processing success.
5. Sync job completed ≠ reconciliation complete.
6. No detected difference ≠ correctness proven when coverage is incomplete.
7. Backlog age may matter more than backlog count.
8. Partner uptime ≠ GiftHatke integration uptime.
9. Permission granted ≠ permission still needed.
10. Credential not failing ≠ credential governance healthy.
11. Fast support reply ≠ fast issue resolution.
12. Installed ≠ used ≠ valuable.
13. High marketplace rating ≠ Security certification.
14. Certification pass ≠ future Versions automatically safe.
15. Revenue generated ≠ Partner safe or strategically valuable.
16. Cheap external service ≠ low total operating cost.
17. Single-provider dependence ≠ automatically unacceptable, but Risk must be visible.
18. Technology readiness ≠ marketplace business need.
19. SMP1 needs only operational metrics for current critical integrations.
20. Ecosystem intelligence must support real operational decisions, not vanity platform growth.

---

# 8.130 Stage 8 Certification

Stage 8 permanently establishes the implementation-grade intelligence architecture for:

- Partner/Application activity
- API reliability
- webhook delivery
- synchronization
- reconciliation
- freshness/backlog
- retries/dead letters
- failure classification
- Partner availability
- incidents/near-misses
- permission/access Risk
- credential health
- Security/Data Risk
- Partner support
- SLA measurement
- Application adoption
- Extension usage
- marketplace discovery/conversion
- uninstallation/retention
- certification/compatibility
- commercial value
- total integration cost
- dependency/concentration Risk
- Partner trends/regression
- audience-specific reporting
- metric lineage
- value reviews
- ecosystem maturity
- marketplace readiness
- SMP1 operational minimum
- ERP9/ERP10/Version 1.1 reuse
- anti-metric-gaming
- anti-duplication
- anti-platform-drift
- anti-overengineering

This is sufficient to evaluate external ecosystem performance and value without creating an enterprise marketplace analytics programme before GiftHatke actually operates a meaningful external marketplace.

**Stage 8 Status: ✅ CERTIFIED**

**Enterprise Canon Position: Domain 43 — IN PROGRESS (8/10 stages certified).**

# ENTERPRISE ECOSYSTEM MARKETPLACE, PARTNER NETWORK & PLATFORM EXPANSION CANON
## Stage 9 — Partner Testing, API & Permission Validation, Extension Safety, Synchronization Reconciliation, Certification, Incident Simulation & Production Readiness Canon

---

# 9.1 Purpose

Stage 9 defines how external Partners, applications, extensions, credentials, permissions, webhooks, synchronization flows, marketplace capabilities, and critical external dependencies must be tested before Production use.

The objective is:

> **Prove that every external integration can perform its intended business function, stay inside its approved authority, fail safely, reconcile correctly, remain attributable, and be revoked without compromising the certified GiftHatkeOS core.**

---

# 9.2 Testing Philosophy

Permanent principles:

- test intended behavior.
- test prohibited behavior.
- test permission boundaries.
- test wrong Company and wrong Environment.
- test retries and duplicate protection.
- test synchronization accuracy.
- test external failure.
- test suspension and revocation.
- test business reconciliation.
- test operational fallback.
- certification depth must match actual Risk.

---

# 9.3 Production Readiness Scope

A Production external integration should be validated across:

- Partner identity
- Application identity
- version
- purpose
- Environment
- Company scope
- credentials
- permissions
- API behavior
- business validation
- webhooks
- synchronization
- idempotency
- reconciliation
- monitoring
- incident containment
- revocation
- fallback

as relevant.

---

# 9.4 Integration Inventory

Before testing record:

- Partner
- Application
- Application Version
- Extension if applicable
- owner
- business purpose
- Environment
- Company
- API scopes
- credentials
- criticality

---

# 9.5 No Unknown Production Integration

Permanent:

```text
Unknown Application Identity
+
Production Access
=
FAIL
```

---

# 9.6 Partner Identity Validation

Confirm Production Application maps to:

- known Partner
- approved relationship
- accountable internal owner

---

# 9.7 Partner Status Test

Suspended/revoked Partner should not receive new Production authority.

---

# 9.8 Application Identity Validation

Every API call should be attributable to the correct Application identity.

---

# 9.9 Shared Identity Negative Test

Two unrelated applications should not silently operate under one generic identity where independent control is required.

---

# 9.10 Purpose Validation

Confirm granted access supports the documented business purpose.

---

# 9.11 Purpose Negative Test

Application attempts unrelated capability.

Expected:

- rejected.

---

# 9.12 Version Validation

Confirm exact tested Application/Extension Version matches Production candidate.

---

# 9.13 Version Boundary

Permanent:

```text
Version A Certified
≠
Version B Automatically Certified
```

---

# 9.14 Compatibility Test

Verify Application Version works with the supported:

- GiftHatkeOS API Version
- Extension Points
- relevant platform version

---

# 9.15 Incompatible Version Test

Expected:

- installation/activation blocked
- clear compatibility error.

---

# 9.16 Environment Validation

Verify:

- Sandbox credentials cannot access Production
- Production credentials are not casually reused in Test.

---

# 9.17 Environment Boundary

Permanent:

```text
Sandbox Success
≠
Production Readiness
```

---

# 9.18 Company Scope Test

Application authorized for Company A attempts Company B access.

Expected:

- denied.

---

# 9.19 Ambiguous Company Test

Request lacks Company where context is required.

Expected:

- reject/require explicit Company
- never guess.

---

# 9.20 Credential Validation

Test:

- valid credential
- invalid credential
- expired credential
- revoked credential

---

# 9.21 Credential Revocation Test

After revocation:

- new requests must fail.

---

# 9.22 Credential Rotation Test

Verify:

- replacement credential works
- old credential is revoked at correct point
- no unplanned outage where continuity matters.

---

# 9.23 Secret Exposure Test

Confirm secrets are not exposed in:

- UI
- logs
- API errors
- Audit output.

---

# 9.24 Authentication Boundary

Permanent:

```text
Successfully Authenticated
≠
Authorized Business Operation
```

---

# 9.25 Permission Inventory

For each Application document:

- read scopes
- write scopes
- event scopes
- administrative capability

---

# 9.26 Read Permission Test

Read-only Application accesses allowed records only.

---

# 9.27 Write Negative Test

Read-only Application attempts business mutation.

Expected:

- rejected.

---

# 9.28 Delete Negative Test

Application without delete authority attempts deletion.

Expected:

- rejected.

---

# 9.29 Cross-Domain Permission Test

Shipping Application attempts Finance operation.

Expected:

- rejected unless explicitly approved.

---

# 9.30 Permission Expansion Test

New Application Version requests additional scope.

Expected:

- new permission review
- not automatically inherited.

---

# 9.31 Least-Privilege Review

Check whether every granted privileged scope is actually required.

---

# 9.32 Dormant Privilege Test

Identify:

- unused privileged permissions
- unused Production credentials.

---

# 9.33 API Contract Testing

For every business-critical API validate:

- required fields
- optional fields
- data types
- error responses
- version contract

---

# 9.34 Malformed Request Test

Submit:

- invalid JSON/structure
- wrong data type
- missing required field
- invalid identifier

Expected:

- deterministic rejection.

---

# 9.35 Unknown Field Test

Unexpected fields should not silently create unintended behavior.

---

# 9.36 Invalid Business State Test

Example:

- Partner attempts shipping action for cancelled Order.

Expected:

- owning Domain rejects it.

---

# 9.37 Business Rule Boundary

Permanent:

```text
External Application Says Action Is Valid
≠
GiftHatkeOS Business Rule Accepts It
```

---

# 9.38 Direct Database Access Test

Normal external integration must not possess unrestricted direct business database mutation.

---

# 9.39 Internal Endpoint Negative Test

Application attempts undocumented/private internal service.

Expected:

- rejected.

---

# 9.40 API Rate-Limit Test

Verify rate limiting behaves as designed.

---

# 9.41 Rate-Limit Safety

Throttling must not silently discard business-critical requests.

---

# 9.42 Idempotency Test

Repeat same material request.

Expected:

```text
One Intended Business Effect
```

not duplicates.

---

# 9.43 Duplicate Order Test

Send identical external Order-create request twice with same idempotency reference.

Expected:

- second request reuses/reports existing result.

---

# 9.44 Duplicate Payment/Shipment Test

Where applicable verify duplicates cannot arise from network retry.

---

# 9.45 Timeout After Commit Test

Simulate timeout after possible business commit.

Expected:

- query/reconcile authoritative state before retry.

---

# 9.46 Timeout Boundary

Permanent:

```text
Timeout
≠
Transaction Definitely Failed
```

---

# 9.47 Retry Test

Transient dependency failure should:

- retry according to policy
- remain bounded.

---

# 9.48 Non-Retryable Test

Business validation or permission rejection should not be endlessly retried.

---

Future Production integration evidence should include:

- Partner/Application identity
- purpose
- owner
- Version
- Company/Environment
- permission matrix
- credential model
- API contract tests
- negative permission tests
- idempotency tests
- sync/reconciliation tests
- failure/recovery tests
- suspension/revocation test
- Security/data tests
- Audit evidence

# 9.118 Certification Outcomes

Use:

- PASS
- PASS WITH CONTROL
- FAIL

under Domain 39 governance.

---

# 9.119 PASS

Means:

- intended capability works
- prohibited access blocked
- data scope correct
- business validation preserved
- retries safe
- reconciliation reliable
- revocation works
- no critical unresolved Risk.

---

# 9.120 PASS WITH CONTROL

Acceptable only for non-blocking issue with:

- owner
- treatment
- accepted Risk.

---

# 9.121 FAIL

Examples:

- credential/permission bypass
- cross-Company access
- unauthorized data exposure
- direct uncontrolled DB mutation
- duplicate material transactions
- inability to reconcile critical sync
- ineffective revocation
- critical Partner outage taking down entire ERP unnecessarily.

---

# 9.122 Critical Certification Blockers

Minimum:

1. Unknown Production Application identity.
2. Authentication bypass.
3. Authorization bypass.
4. Company isolation failure.
5. Production/Sandbox separation failure.
6. unrestricted external database mutation.
7. material data exposure.
8. duplicate transaction protection failure.
9. critical synchronization cannot be reconciled.
10. revocation cannot actually stop access.

---

# 9.123 Retesting

After material defect correction:

Re-run:

- affected positive tests
- negative tests
- regression tests
- reconciliation checks.

---

# 9.124 No Evidence Erasure

Previous FAIL remains historical certification Evidence.

---

- API behavior
- permissions
- data handling
- Company scope
- Extension behavior
- criticality.

---

- limited record population
- controlled operational window

where practical.

- Audit

---

- correct credentials
- correct endpoint
- correct Company
- correct Environment
- correct Version
- monitoring active.

---

# 9.129 Post-Cutover Reconciliation

After first Production runs:

Validate actual business records against expected results.

---

```text
Testing Scope
=
Only Current Business-Critical Integrations
```

---

- configuration
- credential
- permissions
- connectivity

- error handling

- monitoring.

---

- public marketplace testing

- marketplace security laboratory
- app review automation
- Partner scoring tests

unless these capabilities are actually implemented.

---

# 9.133 ERP9 Reuse

ERP9's stronger configuration/master data should improve external integration testing and validation.

---

# 9.134 ERP10 Reuse

ERP10 may strengthen:

- administration
- monitoring

- operational acceptance.

---

# 9.135 Version 1.1 Reuse

---

# 9.136 Advanced Testing That Can Wait

Do not block roadmap for:

- ecosystem-wide penetration laboratory
- public Extension certification factory
- automated third-party code analysis platform
- global Partner chaos engineering
- marketplace fraud simulation
- developer reputation validation
- multi-Partner failover laboratory
- mass app compatibility farm.

---

# 9.137 Anti-Duplication Rule

Permanent:

> **Domain 43 tests external participation and integration behavior. Domain 13 owns API contracts, Domain 28 Security, Domain 29 data governance, Domain 14/41 operational reliability, Domain 38 resilience, Domain 39 formal assurance, and business Domains own transaction correctness.**

---

# 9.138 Anti-Platform-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **Do not build marketplace certification infrastructure before GiftHatke has a marketplace requiring certification at scale. Test the integrations that actually run the business.**

---

# 9.139 Anti-Overengineering Rule

Permanent:

> **A real shipping or marketplace integration must be tested thoroughly for identity, permissions, business correctness, retries, reconciliation, failure, and revocation. It does not require an enterprise app-store testing platform.**

---

# 9.140 Critical Testing Invariants

1. Unknown Production integration ≠ acceptable.
2. Partner approved ≠ all Versions approved.
3. Sandbox success ≠ Production readiness.
4. Authentication ≠ authorization.
5. Read permission ≠ write permission.
6. External request still requires business validation.
7. Direct uncontrolled DB mutation is prohibited.
8. Rate limiting must not silently lose critical business work.
9. Duplicate retries must not duplicate business effect.
10. Timeout ≠ definite failure.
11. Partner Event ≠ accepted business state.
12. Bidirectional sync ≠ dual authority.
13. Sync completed ≠ reconciled.
14. Installation finished ≠ integration operational.
15. Revocation status ≠ access actually closed until verified.
16. Uninstall ≠ delete historical business records.
17. Partner outage should not collapse unrelated ERP capability.
18. Recovery ≠ full reconciliation until backlog/state is verified.
19. SMP1 testing applies only to current required integrations.
20. Production external access must be certified by Evidence, not by Partner reputation.

---

# 9.141 Stage 9 Certification

Stage 9 permanently establishes the implementation-grade testing and acceptance architecture for:

- Partner/Application identity
- Version/compatibility
- Environment/Company scope
- credential lifecycle
- permissions
- API contracts
- malformed requests
- business validation
- rate limits
- idempotency
- webhooks
- data minimization
- synchronization
- mapping/source authority
- reconciliation
- Installation/uninstallation
- suspension/revocation
- Extension safety
- marketplace listing/subscription boundaries
- monitoring
- external outages
- recovery/fallback
- incident simulations
- Audit
- certification package
- PASS/PASS WITH CONTROL/FAIL
- recertification
- SMP1 critical-integration acceptance
- ERP9/ERP10/Version 1.1 reuse
- anti-duplication
- anti-platform-drift
- anti-overengineering

This is sufficient to certify external integrations safely without creating marketplace-scale testing infrastructure before a genuine ecosystem exists.

# ENTERPRISE ECOSYSTEM MARKETPLACE, PARTNER NETWORK & PLATFORM EXPANSION CANON
## Stage 10 — Final Enterprise Ecosystem Marketplace, Partner Network & Platform Expansion Certification Canon

---

# 10.1 Purpose

Stage 10 consolidates and formally certifies Domain 43 as the permanent GiftHatkeOS architecture for external Partners, applications, extensions, credentials, permissions, installations, marketplace participation, external synchronization, ecosystem governance, and platform expansion.

The objective is:

> **Enable GiftHatkeOS to grow safely beyond internal operations without allowing external parties, applications, or marketplace activity to compromise certified business architecture, internal authority, data governance, or business-first execution priorities.**

---

# 10.2 Final Domain Mission

Domain 43 permanently defines:

- Partner identity
- Application identity
- Extension identity
- capabilities
- Extension Points
- API permissions
- Company/Environment scope
- credentials
- installations
- subscriptions
- Partner onboarding
- Application onboarding
- certification
- marketplace listings
- Webhooks
- synchronization
- external source authority
- Partner incidents
- revocation
- ecosystem performance
- marketplace maturity

---

# 10.3 Core Architecture Doctrine

Permanent:

```text id="core-ecosystem-doctrine43"
Certified GiftHatkeOS Core

↓

Controlled APIs / Events / Extension Points

↓

External Applications & Partners
```

Never:

```text id="invalid-ecosystem43"

↓

```

Permanent:

```text id="external-authority43"
External Partner
≠

```

# 10.74 Core Independence

Permanent:

```text id="external-outage-final43"
Partner Service Down
≠
Entire GiftHatkeOS Down
```

where architecture reasonably permits isolation.

---

# 10.75 Business Truth Independence

External provider outage must not erase or invalidate GiftHatkeOS authoritative business records.

---

# 10.76 Fallback

Critical integrations may have:

- queue
- manual fallback
- alternate provider

according to actual business Risk.

---

# 10.77 Partner Monitoring

Useful signals include:

- last success
- errors
- backlog
- authentication failures
- reconciliation state

---

# 10.78 Monitoring Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="monitoring-final43"
Partner API Healthy
≠
Business Integration Healthy
```

---

# 10.79 Business Health

Integration health should ultimately reflect business outcomes.

---

# 10.80 Partner Incident

Material incidents may include:

- credential compromise
- unauthorized data access
- duplicate business transactions
- synchronization corruption
- prolonged critical outage

---

# 10.81 Incident Flow

Canonical:

```text id="incident-final43"
Detect

↓

Contain

↓

Suspend / Revoke

↓

Preserve Evidence

↓

Assess Business Impact

↓

Reconcile

↓

Correct

↓

Revalidate
```

---

# 10.82 Narrow Containment

Prefer smallest safe control:

```text id="containment-final43"
Credential
→
Installation
→
Application
→
Partner
```

as Risk demands.

---

# 10.83 Suspension

Temporary suspension stops relevant new external activity.

---

# 10.84 Suspension Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="suspension-final43"
Application Suspended
≠
Historical Records Invalid
```

---

# 10.85 Revocation

Revocation must actually close technical access.

---

# 10.86 Revocation Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="revocation-final43"
Status = REVOKED
≠
Access Proven Closed
```

Technical verification is required.

---

# 10.87 Uninstallation

Uninstallation should stop integration capability while preserving business history.

---

# 10.88 Historical Integrity

Permanent:

```text id="history-final43"
Partner / Extension Removed
≠
Historical Transactions Deleted
```

---

# 10.89 Dependency Awareness

Before disabling critical external service:

Understand what business workflow depends on it.

---

# 10.90 No Blind Uninstall

Permanent:

```text id="blind-uninstall-final43"
Uninstall Requested
≠
Safe to Immediately Disconnect Critical Provider
```

---

# 10.91 Data Governance

Domain 29 remains authoritative for:

- external data disclosure
- privacy
- retention
- data classification

---

# 10.92 Purpose Limitation

External data may be used only according to approved purpose and policy.

---

# 10.93 Data Availability Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="data-purpose-final43"
Data Accessible
≠
Data May Be Used for Any Purpose
```

---

# 10.94 Data Redistribution

Read permission does not automatically permit external redistribution.

---

# 10.95 Security Authority

Domain 28 remains authoritative for:

- authentication
- authorization
- credentials
- privilege control

---

# 10.96 Integration Authority

Domain 13 remains authoritative for:

- API contracts
- integration patterns
- event contracts
- external connectivity

---

# 10.97 Workflow Authority

Domain 11 retains Workflow authority.

External integrations cannot force invalid workflow states.

---

# 10.98 Finance Authority

Domain 6 remains authoritative for financial truth.

---

# 10.99 AI Extension Authority

Domain 42 governs AI Agent/autonomy capability exposed by external ecosystem Extensions.

---

# 10.100 Platform Authority

Domain 41 governs:

- runtime
- infrastructure
- networking
- Secrets
- deployment

---

# 10.101 Business Relationship Authority

Domain 23 remains authoritative for Supplier/Partner business relationship semantics where relevant.

---

# 10.102 Contract Authority

Domain 24 governs:

- Partner contracts
- legal obligations
- liability
- data agreements

---

# 10.103 Commercial Entitlement

Future marketplace Subscription may determine entitlement to use an Application.

---

# 10.104 Commercial Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="commercial-final43"
Commercial Entitlement
≠
Technical Authorization
```

---

# 10.105 Marketplace

---

# 10.106 Marketplace Purpose

May eventually support:

- discovery
- installation
- commercial subscriptions
- Extension publication

---

# 10.107 Marketplace Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="marketplace-final43"
Listed in Marketplace
≠
Installed
≠
Unlimited Trust
```

---

# 10.108 Marketplace Certification

Certification should communicate exact scope.

---

# 10.109 Certification Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="certification-final43"
Certified Version
≠
Every Future Version Certified
```

---

# 10.110 Marketplace Ratings

User ratings, if ever introduced, remain separate from:

- Security
- certification
- legal/compliance approval

---

# 10.111 Rating Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="rating-final43"
Five-Star Rating
≠
Security Certification
```

---

# 10.112 Partner Tiers

Future commercial tiers must not create hidden technical privilege.

---

# 10.113 Partner Tier Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="tier-final43"
Premium Partner
≠
Platform Administrator
```

---

# 10.114 Developer Self-Service

Future developers may:

- register
- develop
- test

through controlled interfaces.

---

# 10.115 Production Self-Approval

Permanent:

```text id="self-approval-final43"
Developer Self-Service
≠
Production Self-Approval
```

---

# 10.116 Developer Portal

Future developer portal is optional administration convenience.

It is not a runtime dependency for core integrations.

---

# 10.117 Extension SDK

Future SDK should expose only supported interfaces.

---

# 10.118 SDK Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="sdk-final43"
SDK Available
≠
Internal Private API Supported
```

---

# 10.119 Partner Performance

Useful measures include:

- business integration success
- reconciliation
- outages
- incidents
- support quality
- cost

---

# 10.120 No Vanity Ecosystem Metrics

Permanent:

```text id="vanity-final43"
More Partners
More Listings
More API Calls
More Installs

≠

More Business Value
```

---

# 10.121 Adoption

Permanent:

```text id="adoption-final43"
Installed
≠
Used
≠
Valuable
```

---

If ecosystem monetization emerges:

Measure value alongside:

- reliability
- maintenance
- support
- Security
- operating cost

---

# 10.123 Cost

True integration cost may include:

- external fees
- engineering
- support
- reconciliation
- incidents

---

# 10.124 Critical Dependency

Some external providers may be operationally critical.

---

# 10.125 Concentration Risk

Single-provider dependency should be visible where material.

It is not automatically unacceptable.

---

# 10.126 Ecosystem Maturity

Canonical:

```text id="maturity-final43"
Reliable Current Integrations

↓

Reusable Integration Governance

↓

Multiple External Applications

↓

Partner Network

↓

Extension Ecosystem

↓

Marketplace Only If Needed
```

---

# 10.127 Marketplace Readiness

Marketplace becomes justified only when real evidence exists:

- repeated Partner onboarding
- multiple Extensions
- user demand
- discovery problem
- commercial opportunity

---

# 10.128 Technology vs Business Need

Permanent:

```text id="marketplace-business-final43"
Technology Can Support Marketplace
≠
Business Should Build Marketplace
```

---

# 10.129 Testing Doctrine

Production external integration testing must validate:

- intended capability
- prohibited capability
- authentication
- permissions
- Company/Environment
- retries
- reconciliation
- failure
- revocation

---

# 10.130 Negative Testing

Production acceptance should test:

- unauthorized scope
- wrong Company
- wrong Environment
- revoked credential
- duplicate request
- malformed payload
- invalid business state

---

# 10.131 More External Authority = More Evidence

Permanent:

```text id="evidence-final43"
Higher External Authority
=
Higher Certification Burden
```

---

# 10.132 Critical Integration Acceptance

High-impact integrations require stronger:

- end-to-end business testing
- idempotency
- reconciliation
- outage/fallback
- revocation testing

---

# 10.133 Certification Outcomes

Use:

- PASS
- PASS WITH CONTROL
- FAIL

consistent with Domain 39.

---

# 10.134 Critical FAIL Examples

- authentication bypass
- authorization bypass
- Company isolation failure
- uncontrolled database mutation
- material data exposure
- duplicate transactions
- unreconcilable critical synchronization
- revocation failure

---

# 10.135 SMP1 Explicit Requirements

For current business-critical external integrations, standalone v1.0 should provide:

- Application identity
- secure authentication
- permissions
- correct Company/Environment
- business API contract
- errors/retries
- idempotency where needed
- monitoring
- reconciliation
- revocation capability

---

# 10.136 SMP1 Explicit Non-Requirements

Standalone v1.0 does **not** require:

- public Partner portal
- public developer portal
- public marketplace
- app store
- app rating/reviews
- Partner tiers
- revenue-share platform
- Extension SDK ecosystem
- automated certification platform
- Partner analytics suite

---

# 10.137 No SMP1 Ecosystem Drift

Permanent:

> **Domain 43 must not expand SMP1 from a standalone ERP migration into a platform-marketplace programme.**

---

# 10.138 ERP9 Reuse

ERP9 may strengthen:

- Settings
- Company configuration
- external Partner references
- integration settings
- master data

that ecosystem capabilities can later reuse.

---

# 10.139 ERP10 Reuse

ERP10 may improve:

- external integration administration
- permission visibility
- health
- reconciliation
- operational polish

---

# 10.140 Version 1.1 Reuse

Version 1.1 may introduce:

- unified integration administration
- reusable Application Registry
- selected extension capability

only when current operational demand justifies it.

---

# 10.141 Anti-Duplication Certification

Domain 43 explicitly rejects duplicate external-owned versions of:

- Orders
- Inventory
- Production
- Shipping
- Finance
- CRM
- Workflow
- Security
- Customer/Supplier Master Data

---

# 10.142 Anti-Platform-Drift Certification

Permanent:

> **GiftHatkeOS remains a business operating platform first. External ecosystem capability is an expansion option, not the platform's primary purpose unless business strategy later explicitly changes.**

---

# 10.143 Anti-Marketplace-First Certification

Permanent:

> **Do not build a marketplace and then search for Partners. Build reliable Partner integrations first; marketplace capability comes only after actual ecosystem demand exists.**

---

# 10.144 Anti-Overengineering Certification

Permanent:

> **Current external integrations need clear identity, credentials, permissions, business validation, monitoring, reconciliation, and revocation. They do not need a public ecosystem platform.**

---

# 10.145 Critical Domain Invariants

The following are permanently certified:

1. External Partner ≠ internal business authority.
2. Future ecosystem capability ≠ current business priority.
3. Partner ≠ Supplier ≠ Customer.
4. Partner approved ≠ every Application approved.
5. External Application ≠ Partner organization.
6. Extension ≠ authority to modify core.
7. External capability must use approved interfaces.
8. API Gateway ≠ Business Rule Engine.
9. Authentication ≠ authorization.
10. READ ≠ WRITE ≠ ADMIN.
11. Company A access ≠ Company B access.
12. Sandbox approval ≠ Production approval.
13. Credential possession ≠ unlimited authority.
14. Installation ≠ global authorization.
15. Software update ≠ permission expansion approval.
16. Internal Event ≠ automatically publishable external Event.
17. Partner Event ≠ accepted business truth.
18. Two systems containing same record ≠ dual authority.
19. External ID ≠ internal GiftHatkeOS ID.
20. Sync completed ≠ reconciliation PASS.
21. Partner retry must not duplicate business effect.
22. Timeout ≠ definite transaction failure.
23. Dead-lettered ≠ resolved.
24. Partner API healthy ≠ business integration healthy.
25. Suspension ≠ historical business record invalidation.
26. Revoked status ≠ verified access closure until tested.
27. Uninstall ≠ delete historical business records.
28. Commercial entitlement ≠ technical authorization.
29. Marketplace listing ≠ installation or unlimited trust.
30. Marketplace rating ≠ Security certification.
31. Premium Partner ≠ administrator.
32. Developer self-service ≠ Production self-approval.
33. More Partners/API calls/installs ≠ more business value.
34. SMP1 requires only current critical integration capability.
35. Marketplace/platform expansion must follow real business demand.

# ENTERPRISE KNOWLEDGE OPERATING SYSTEM & ORGANIZATIONAL MEMORY CANON
## Stage 1 — Knowledge Foundation, Organizational Memory, Authority, Provenance, Ownership & Business Architecture Preservation Canon

---

# 1.1 Purpose

Domain 44 defines how GiftHatkeOS should preserve, govern, retrieve, and reuse enterprise knowledge across people, processes, systems, documents, decisions, and future AI capabilities.

The objective is:

> **Create a durable organizational memory that helps people and systems understand how GiftHatke operates without confusing documentation, guidance, or learned knowledge with authoritative transactional business truth.**

---

# 1.2 Core Principle

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-core44s1"
Knowledge
≠
Transactional System of Record
```

---

# 1.3 Priority Principle

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-priority44s1"
Knowledge Platform Expansion
≠
SMP1 Critical-Path Requirement
```

---

# 1.4 Domain Mission

Domain 44 defines future architecture for:

- enterprise knowledge
- business documentation
- policies
- procedures
- operating instructions
- decision memory
- institutional memory
- lessons learned
- reusable expertise
- Knowledge ownership
- provenance
- validation
- lifecycle
- retrieval
- human reuse
- AI retrieval
- organizational continuity

---

# 1.5 Knowledge vs Business Data

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-data44s1"
Knowledge Explains Business

Business Systems Record Business
```

---

# 1.6 Examples of Business Truth

Authoritative business truth includes:

- Order status
- Current Stock
- Accounts payable
- Customer record
- Production status
- Shipment status

These remain in owning Domains.

---

# 1.7 Examples of Knowledge

Knowledge may include:

- how to process a return
- how Inventory Reorder works
- why a policy exists
- how to troubleshoot a machine
- how to onboard a new team member
- approved operating procedures

---

# 1.8 Knowledge Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-boundary44s1"
Article Says Order Is Shipped
≠
Order Is Shipped
```

---

# 1.9 Organizational Memory

Organizational memory represents information that should survive:

- employee turnover
- system migration
- management change
- time

---

# 1.10 Memory Purpose

Organizational memory should preserve:

- how work is done
- why important decisions were made
- what was learned
- which policies govern behavior

---

# 1.11 Memory Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="memory-boundary44s1"
Organizational Memory
≠
Personal Memory of One Employee
```

---

# 1.12 Knowledge Classes

Potential:

- Policy
- Procedure
- Work Instruction
- Standard Operating Procedure
- Guide
- Reference
- Troubleshooting Note
- Decision Record
- Lesson Learned
- FAQ
- Training Material

---

# 1.13 Knowledge Classification

Classification should be practical.

Do not create dozens of categories without need.

---

# 1.14 Policy

Represents mandatory organizational rule.

---

# 1.15 Procedure

Defines expected method to perform business process.

---

# 1.16 Work Instruction

Provides detailed task-level instructions.

---

# 1.17 Guide

Provides explanatory or advisory information.

---

# 1.18 Decision Record

Captures an important decision and its rationale.

---

# 1.19 Lesson Learned

Captures reusable learning from:

- incident
- project
- operational experience

---

# 1.20 Knowledge Authority

Not all knowledge has equal authority.

---

# 1.21 Authority Levels

Potential:

- OFFICIAL
- APPROVED
- DRAFT
- INFORMAL
- ARCHIVED

---

# 1.22 Authority Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="authority-boundary44s1"
Knowledge Exists
≠
Knowledge Is Approved
```

---

# 1.23 Official Knowledge

Represents formally approved organizational guidance.

---

# 1.24 Draft Knowledge

May support collaboration but must not be presented as binding guidance.

---

# 1.25 Informal Knowledge

Examples:

- useful note
- team tip
- temporary observation

Should remain distinguishable from approved procedure.

---

# 1.26 Archived Knowledge

Retained for historical reference but should not normally guide current work.

---

# 1.27 Knowledge Owner

Every material official knowledge asset should have accountable ownership.

---

# 1.28 Owner Responsibilities

Potential:

- accuracy
- approval
- review
- update
- retirement

---

# 1.29 Ownership Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="owner-boundary44s1"
Knowledge Author
≠
Knowledge Owner
```

---

# 1.30 Knowledge Author

Creates or substantially updates content.

---

# 1.31 Knowledge Approver

Confirms content is acceptable for its intended authority level.

---

# 1.32 Approver Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="approver-boundary44s1"
Can Edit Article
≠
Can Approve Policy
```

---

# 1.33 Domain Ownership

Knowledge about a Business Domain should remain aligned to that Domain's authority.

Example:

```text id="domain-knowledge44s1"
Finance Procedure
→
Finance Domain Ownership
```

---

# 1.34 No Knowledge Override

Permanent:

> **A Knowledge Base article cannot override a certified business rule, permission, state machine, or accounting rule.**

---

# 1.35 Business Architecture Preservation

Canonical:

```text id="knowledge-business-architecture44s1"
Certified Business Architecture

↓

Official Knowledge Explains It
```

not:

```text id="knowledge-redesign44s1"
Documentation
→
Silently Redesigns Business Process
```

---

# 1.36 Knowledge Source

Knowledge should identify source where material.

Potential:

- certified business process
- approved policy
- legal requirement
- operating experience
- management decision
- vendor manual

---

# 1.37 Provenance

Provenance means knowing:

- where knowledge came from
- who authored it
- who approved it
- when it became valid

---

# 1.38 Provenance Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="provenance-boundary44s1"
Confidently Written Article
≠
Trusted Provenance
```

---

# 1.39 Knowledge Version

Material official knowledge should support versioning.

---

# 1.40 Version Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-version44s1"
Same Article Title
≠
Same Instructions Forever
```

---

# 1.41 Effective Date

Policies/procedures may have:

- effective from
- expiry/review date

---

# 1.42 Historical Version

Old versions may remain available for:

- Audit
- historical explanation
- dispute/investigation

---

# 1.43 Current Version

Only one approved current version should normally guide operations.

---

# 1.44 Knowledge Status

Recommended:

```text id="knowledge-status44s1"
DRAFT
IN REVIEW
APPROVED
PUBLISHED
SUPERSEDED
ARCHIVED
```

---

# 1.45 Knowledge Lifecycle

Canonical:

```text id="knowledge-lifecycle44s1"
Identify Need

↓

Create

↓

Review

↓

Approve

↓

Publish

↓

Use

↓

Review / Update

↓

Supersede / Archive
```

---

# 1.46 Knowledge Need

Knowledge should exist because users need:

- guidance
- continuity
- training
- reference
- explanation

not because every possible topic must be documented.

---

# 1.47 Publishing Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="publishing-boundary44s1"
Draft Saved
≠
Official Knowledge Published
```

---

# 1.48 Review Frequency

Review should depend on:

- business Risk
- change frequency
- legal significance
- operational impact

---

# 1.49 No Review Bureaucracy

Low-risk reference material does not need the same review process as:

- Finance policy
- Security procedure
- Legal/compliance instruction

---

# 1.50 Knowledge Scope

May apply to:

- Enterprise
- Company
- Business Unit
- Department
- Role
- Domain
- Process

---

# 1.51 Company Scope

Domain 40 applies.

Permanent:

```text id="company-scope44s1"
Knowledge Approved for Company A
≠
Automatically Applicable to Company B
```

---

# 1.52 Role Scope

Some Knowledge may be:

- general
- manager-only
- administrator-only
- specialized team material

---

# 1.53 Access Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-access44s1"
Can Read Knowledge
≠
Can Edit / Approve Knowledge
```

---

# 1.54 Confidential Knowledge

Potential:

- Security procedures
- privileged operational details
- legal strategy
- sensitive internal documentation

Access should be controlled.

---

# 1.55 Public Knowledge

Some future content may be suitable for:

- Customers
- Partners
- external developers

but remains separate from internal Knowledge.

---

# 1.56 Internal vs External Knowledge

Permanent:

```text id="internal-external44s1"
Internal Procedure
≠
External Help Article
```

---

# 1.57 Knowledge Reference

Knowledge may link to authoritative business entities.

Examples:

- Inventory procedure → Inventory module
- Finance policy → financial configuration
- Shipping SOP → carrier workflow

---

# 1.58 Reference Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="reference-boundary44s1"
Knowledge Links to Record
≠
Knowledge Owns Record
```

---

# 1.59 Embedded Knowledge

Future UI may surface relevant guidance directly inside a business workflow.

Example:

```text id="embedded-knowledge44s1"
Purchase Order Screen

↓

"How Approval Works"
```

---

# 1.60 Embedded Knowledge Boundary

Embedded guidance should not block ordinary work unless the business rule itself requires action.

---

# 1.61 Searchability

Knowledge should be retrievable by:

- title
- topic
- Domain
- role
- keywords
- natural-language search

when scale justifies it.

---

# 1.62 Search Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="search-boundary44s1"
Search Result Ranked First
≠
Most Authoritative Knowledge
```

Authority and freshness matter.

---

# 1.63 Knowledge Retrieval

A retrieval system should prioritize:

- relevance
- authority
- current version
- user access

---

# 1.64 Current vs Archived

Current approved knowledge should rank above archived versions by default.

---

# 1.65 Knowledge Relationships

Potential:

- Related To
- Replaces
- Supersedes
- Depends On
- Applies To
- Derived From

---

# 1.66 Supersession

When new official instruction replaces old:

Old knowledge should be clearly marked superseded.

---

# 1.67 Supersession Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="supersession44s1"
Old Document Still Exists
≠
Old Document Still Governs Operations
```

---

# 1.68 Knowledge Conflict

If two official sources conflict:

- surface conflict
- identify owners
- resolve

Do not leave users guessing.

---

# 1.69 Conflict Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-conflict44s1"
Two Approved Articles Disagree
≠
User Should Choose Arbitrarily
```

---

# 1.70 Decision Memory

Potential:

- decision
- date
- context
- rationale
- owner
- affected Domains

---

# 1.71 Decision Record Boundary

```text id="decision-record44s1"
Decision Record
explains
Why

but
does not replace
Current Business Configuration
```

---

# 1.72 Architecture Memory

GiftHatkeOS may preserve:

- certified architectural decisions
- migration decisions
- TITAN LOCK directives
- historical baselines

as organizational memory.

---

# 1.73 Historical Baseline

Apps Script v1.0 may remain documented as:

- certified reference architecture

after standalone cutover.

---

# 1.74 Historical Baseline Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="historical-baseline44s1"
Historical Reference
≠
Current Production Runtime
```

---

# 1.75 Migration Knowledge

- legacy field meaning
- workflow semantics
- reconciliation
- cutover decisions

---

# 1.76 Migration Knowledge Boundary

Migration documentation supports migration.

It does not redefine certified business meaning.

---

# 1.77 Knowledge Capture

Useful knowledge may be captured from:

- business owner
- team experience
- project
- incident
- vendor documentation
- existing certified docs

---

# 1.78 No Automatic Truth Capture

Permanent:

```text id="capture-boundary44s1"
Someone Said It
≠
Official Enterprise Knowledge
```

---

# 1.79 Tacit Knowledge

Domain 44 should support converting valuable tacit knowledge into reusable form.

---

# 1.80 Tacit Knowledge Boundary

Do not attempt to document every individual preference or trivial working habit.

---

# 1.81 Knowledge Validation

Material knowledge should be checked against:

- current business architecture
- current policy
- authoritative owner
- current platform behavior

---

# 1.82 Knowledge Freshness

Knowledge may become stale after:

- ERP release
- workflow change
- legal change
- supplier/process change

---

# 1.83 Stale Knowledge

Should be:

- marked stale
- superseded
- archived

depending on situation.

---

# 1.84 Staleness Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="stale-knowledge44s1"
Document Was Correct When Written
≠
Document Is Correct Today
```

---

# 1.85 Knowledge Change Trigger

Potential triggers:

- certified ERP release
- business process change
- policy update
- incident learning
- organizational change

---

# 1.86 Documentation Synchronization

Where certified functionality changes:

Relevant official documentation should be reviewed.

---

# 1.87 Documentation Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="documentation-sync44s1"
Software Released
≠
Documentation Automatically Accurate
```

Validation remains necessary.

---

# 1.88 Knowledge Quality

Good enterprise knowledge should be:

- accurate
- concise
- current
- actionable
- attributable
- searchable

---

# 1.89 Quality Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="quality-boundary44s1"
Longer Document
≠
Better Knowledge
```

---

# 1.90 Knowledge Duplication

Avoid multiple competing articles for the same official procedure.

---

# 1.91 Canonical Knowledge

Where appropriate, designate one:

- canonical article/procedure

with supporting references beneath it.

---

# 1.92 Duplicate Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="duplicate-knowledge44s1"
More Documents
≠
More Organizational Knowledge
```

---

# 1.93 Knowledge Fragmentation

Avoid spreading one operational procedure across many disconnected documents unless structure requires it.

---

# 1.94 Knowledge Discoverability

Users should be able to find answers without already knowing:

- exact document title
- storage location

---

# 1.95 Knowledge Feedback

Users may report:

- incorrect
- outdated
- unclear
- missing

knowledge.

---

# 1.96 Feedback Boundary

User feedback should trigger review.

It does not directly change official knowledge.

---

# 1.97 Knowledge Improvement

Approved feedback may result in:

- edit
- new version
- clarification
- retirement

---

# 1.98 Training Relationship

Training content may derive from official knowledge.

---

# 1.99 Training Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="training-boundary44s1"
Training Slide
≠
Authoritative Policy
```

---

# 1.100 AI Knowledge Retrieval

Domain 42 Agents may retrieve Domain 44 Knowledge.

---

# 1.101 AI Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="ai-knowledge44s1"
AI Retrieved Knowledge
≠
AI Gained Business Authority
```

---

# 1.102 AI Source Priority

AI should prefer:

1. authoritative ERP data for current transactional facts
2. current approved Knowledge for guidance
3. lower-authority/reference material as appropriate

---

# 1.103 AI Memory Boundary

Domain 42 Agent memory remains separate from Domain 44 organizational knowledge.

---

# 1.104 Organizational Knowledge vs AI Memory

Permanent:

```text id="org-vs-ai-memory44s1"
Organizational Knowledge
=
Governed Shared Knowledge

AI Memory
=
Agent Context
```

---

# 1.105 AI-Generated Knowledge Draft

AI may assist with:

- summarization
- first Draft
- formatting
- extraction

---

# 1.106 AI Publication Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="ai-publish44s1"
AI Generated Draft
≠
Approved Enterprise Knowledge
```

---

# 1.107 Knowledge Approval Remains Human/Governed

Material official Knowledge requires appropriate owner/approver even when AI created the Draft.

---

# 1.108 Knowledge Access Control

Domain 28 governs permissions.

---

# 1.109 Knowledge Data Governance

Domain 29 governs:

- privacy
- retention
- classification
- sensitive information

---

# 1.110 Knowledge Documents

Domain 10 remains authority for:

- Document/file lifecycle
- digital asset handling

Domain 44 owns knowledge meaning and governance.

---

# 1.111 Document vs Knowledge

Permanent:

```text id="document-knowledge44s1"
Document
=
Container / Asset

Knowledge
=
Governed Meaning
```

---

# 1.112 Search Authority

Domain 17 provides enterprise search/retrieval architecture.

Domain 44 defines knowledge content and authority.

---

# 1.113 Workflow Authority

Domain 11 may route:

- review
- approval
- publication

but Domain 44 defines knowledge lifecycle semantics.

---

# 1.114 Compliance Knowledge

Domains 24/39 may own official compliance/audit guidance.

---

# 1.115 Human Capital Integration

Domain 25 may consume Knowledge for:

- onboarding
- role training
- workforce development

---

# 1.116 Incident Learning

Domain 14/38 incidents may generate:

- Lesson Learned
- troubleshooting guidance
- recovery procedure improvements

---

# 1.117 Incident Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="incident-learning44s1"
Incident Closed
≠
Organizational Learning Captured
```

where a reusable lesson exists.

---

# 1.118 Knowledge Continuity

Knowledge should reduce dependence on individual people.

---

# 1.119 Key-Person Risk

Critical operating knowledge known only to one person is an organizational continuity Risk.

---

# 1.120 Knowledge Preservation

Important knowledge should survive:

- employee departure
- workstation change
- runtime migration
- provider change

---

# 1.121 SMP1 Requirement

For SMP1:

```text id="smp1-knowledge44s1"
Required Knowledge Platform:
NONE
```

No dedicated Knowledge Operating System is required.

---

# 1.122 SMP1 Documentation Requirement

SMP1 should preserve only knowledge necessary for:

- migration
- deployment
- operation
- support
- reconciliation
- business handover

---

# 1.123 SMP1 Existing Documentation

Existing certified documentation should be:

- preserved
- mapped
- updated only where runtime behavior requires it

---

# 1.124 No SMP1 Knowledge Platform Workstream

Do not build during SMP1:

- enterprise wiki platform
- AI knowledge graph
- semantic knowledge lake
- complex ontology
- knowledge recommendation engine
- organizational memory service

---

# 1.125 SMP1 Principle

Permanent:

```text id="smp1-principle44s1"
Preserve Critical Knowledge

before

Building Knowledge Platform
```

---

# 1.126 First Future Knowledge Step

When needed, begin with:

- official documentation repository
- owner
- status
- version
- search
- review date

---

# 1.127 Second Maturity Step

Later add:

- embedded help
- stronger relationships
- structured decision records
- lessons learned

---

# 1.128 Third Maturity Step

Only when knowledge scale justifies it:

- AI-assisted retrieval
- semantic relationships
- organizational memory intelligence

---

# 1.129 ERP9 Reuse

ERP9 business configuration/master data changes should trigger relevant Knowledge review where documentation exists.

---

# 1.130 ERP10 Reuse

ERP10 may strengthen:

- help
- onboarding
- usability
- operational documentation synchronization

---

# 1.131 Version 1.1 Reuse

Version 1.1 may introduce structured contextual Knowledge if there is clear user value.

---

# 1.132 Advanced Knowledge Capabilities That Can Wait

Do not block roadmap for:

- enterprise knowledge graph
- semantic ontology engine
- AI knowledge curator
- automatic organizational memory extraction
- expertise recommendation
- social knowledge network
- automated knowledge scoring
- sophisticated knowledge analytics
- company-wide semantic reasoning engine

---

# 1.133 Anti-Duplication Rule

Permanent:

> **Domain 44 governs enterprise knowledge and organizational memory. It does not duplicate Domain 10 documents, Domain 17 search, Domain 25 training/workforce structures, Domain 29 data governance, Domain 42 Agent memory, or transactional business records.**

---

# 1.134 Anti-Documentation-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **Official knowledge must explain the certified business architecture, not gradually create a different unofficial business process through documentation.**

---

# 1.135 Anti-Overengineering Rule

Permanent:

> **Capture the knowledge GiftHatke needs to operate, train, support, migrate, and improve. Do not build a knowledge platform simply because enterprise knowledge architecture can become sophisticated.**

---

# 1.136 Critical Domain Invariants

1. Knowledge ≠ transactional System of Record.
2. Knowledge platform expansion ≠ SMP1 critical path.
3. Article content ≠ current transactional business state.
4. Organizational memory ≠ one employee's personal memory.
5. Knowledge exists ≠ Knowledge approved.
6. Author ≠ owner ≠ approver.
7. Documentation cannot override certified business rules.
8. Confident writing ≠ trustworthy provenance.
9. Same article title ≠ same instructions forever.
10. Draft saved ≠ official Knowledge published.
11. Company A guidance ≠ automatically Company B guidance.
12. Can read ≠ can edit/approve.
13. Internal procedure ≠ external help article.
14. Knowledge reference ≠ ownership of referenced business record.
15. Search rank ≠ authority.
16. Old document exists ≠ old document still governs operations.
17. Decision record explains rationale ≠ current configuration.
18. Someone said it ≠ official enterprise knowledge.
19. Correct when written ≠ correct today.
20. Longer document ≠ better knowledge.
21. More documents ≠ more organizational knowledge.
22. Training material ≠ authoritative policy.
23. AI retrieved Knowledge ≠ AI business authority.
24. AI-generated Draft ≠ approved Knowledge.
25. Document asset ≠ Knowledge meaning.
26. Incident closed ≠ organizational learning captured.
27. Critical Knowledge should survive people/platform changes.
28. SMP1 requires preservation of critical documentation, not a Knowledge platform.
29. Knowledge maturity must follow real operational need.
30. Official knowledge must remain aligned with certified architecture.

---

Stage 1 permanently establishes the implementation-grade foundation for:

- enterprise Knowledge

- Domain ownership

This is sufficient to establish a permanent organizational Knowledge architecture without introducing a new Knowledge-platform workstream into SMP1.
