# ENTERPRISE KNOWLEDGE OPERATING SYSTEM & ORGANIZATIONAL MEMORY CANON
## Stage 2 — Knowledge Asset, Article, Policy, Procedure, Decision Record, Source, Version, Owner, Approval, Taxonomy, Relationship & Organizational Memory Entity Model Canon

---

# 2.1 Purpose

Stage 2 defines the permanent entity model for enterprise Knowledge, organizational memory, policies, procedures, decision records, sources, versions, approvals, relationships, ownership, taxonomy, and lifecycle.

The objective is:

> **Create a durable Knowledge model that preserves meaning, authority, provenance, lifecycle, ownership, and retrieval without duplicating transactional ERP records or requiring a dedicated Knowledge platform during SMP1.**

---

# 2.2 Entity Model Principle

The entities defined in this Canon are logical architectural entities.

They do not require:

- one database table per entity
- microservices
- a Knowledge graph
- a separate Knowledge platform

during current implementation.

---

# 2.3 Core Entity Set

Future-capable entities include:

- Knowledge Asset
- Knowledge Type
- Knowledge Status
- Knowledge Version
- Knowledge Owner
- Knowledge Author
- Knowledge Approver
- Knowledge Source
- Knowledge Provenance
- Knowledge Scope
- Knowledge Classification
- Knowledge Taxonomy
- Knowledge Topic
- Knowledge Tag
- Knowledge Relationship
- Policy
- Procedure
- Work Instruction
- Guide
- FAQ
- Decision Record
- Lesson Learned
- Troubleshooting Record
- Knowledge Review
- Approval Record
- Publication Record
- Supersession Record
- Knowledge Feedback
- Knowledge Access Policy
- Knowledge Reference
- Knowledge Attachment Reference
- Organizational Memory Record

---

# 2.4 Knowledge Asset

Knowledge Asset is the canonical root entity representing a reusable body of enterprise knowledge.

Potential fields:

- Knowledge Asset ID
- title
- Knowledge Type
- status
- owner
- current Version
- scope
- classification
- created date
- updated date

---

# 2.5 Knowledge Asset Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-asset-boundary44s2"
Knowledge Asset
≠
Business Transaction
```

---

# 2.6 Knowledge Type

Defines the functional class of Knowledge Asset.

Potential values:

- POLICY
- PROCEDURE
- WORK_INSTRUCTION
- GUIDE
- FAQ
- DECISION_RECORD
- LESSON_LEARNED
- TROUBLESHOOTING
- REFERENCE
- TRAINING_REFERENCE

---

# 2.7 Type Boundary

Knowledge Type describes how Knowledge is used.

It does not determine authority by itself.

---

# 2.8 Policy Entity

Represents mandatory organizational guidance.

Potential fields:

- Policy ID
- Knowledge Asset ID
- owner
- effective date
- approval authority
- scope

---

# 2.9 Policy Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="policy-boundary44s2"
Policy Document
≠
System Permission Enforcement
```

System controls remain enforced by the relevant Domain.

---

# 2.10 Procedure Entity

Represents the approved method for performing a business process.

---

# 2.11 Procedure Fields

Potential:

- Procedure ID
- Knowledge Asset
- owning Domain
- applicable Roles
- process reference
- current Version

---

# 2.12 Procedure Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="procedure-boundary44s2"
Procedure Describes Process
≠
Procedure Owns Process State
```

---

# 2.13 Work Instruction

Represents detailed task execution guidance.

Examples:

- how to engrave a specific material
- how to prepare a shipment
- how to reconcile a failed marketplace sync

---

# 2.14 Work Instruction Boundary

Work Instruction should not duplicate the full Procedure unless justified.

---

# 2.15 Guide

Represents explanatory, advisory, or educational content.

---

# 2.16 Guide Boundary

A Guide may explain options.

It does not automatically impose policy.

---

# 2.17 FAQ

Represents concise reusable answers to common operational questions.

---

# 2.18 FAQ Boundary

FAQ should link back to authoritative Knowledge where material.

---

# 2.19 Decision Record

Represents an important decision and rationale.

Minimum fields:

- Decision Record ID
- title
- decision
- context
- rationale
- owner
- decision date
- affected Domains
- status

---

# 2.20 Decision Record Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="decision-record-boundary44s2"
Decision Record
≠
Current Runtime Configuration
```

---

# 2.21 Lesson Learned

Represents reusable organizational learning.

Potential fields:

- Lesson ID
- event/project/incident reference
- lesson
- recommended change
- owner
- status

---

# 2.22 Lesson Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="lesson-boundary44s2"
Lesson Captured
≠
Improvement Implemented
```

---

# 2.23 Troubleshooting Record

Represents known issue resolution guidance.

Potential:

- symptom
- likely cause
- diagnosis
- resolution
- escalation

---

# 2.24 Troubleshooting Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="troubleshooting-boundary44s2"
Known Fix
≠
Guaranteed Root Cause
```

---

# 2.25 Knowledge Status

Recommended:

```text id="knowledge-status44s2"
DRAFT
IN_REVIEW
APPROVED
PUBLISHED
SUPERSEDED
ARCHIVED
RETIRED
```

---

# 2.26 Draft

Knowledge may be edited collaboratively.

It is not official guidance.

---

# 2.27 In Review

Indicates content is being evaluated.

---

# 2.28 Approved

Content has passed required approval.

---

# 2.29 Published

Content is available to intended audience.

---

# 2.30 Approved vs Published

Permanent:

```text id="approved-published44s2"
APPROVED
≠
PUBLISHED
```

Approval and availability may be separate.

---

# 2.31 Superseded

Indicates newer approved Knowledge has replaced this version or asset.

---

# 2.32 Archived

Retained primarily for history/reference.

---

# 2.33 Retired

Indicates Knowledge is no longer relevant for normal use.

---

# 2.34 Knowledge Version

Represents a specific immutable or logically fixed revision of a Knowledge Asset.

Potential fields:

- Version ID
- Knowledge Asset ID
- version number
- content reference
- author
- created date
- effective date
- status

---

# 2.35 Version Principle

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-version-principle44s2"
Knowledge Asset
=
Persistent Identity

Knowledge Version
=
Specific Revision
```

---

# 2.36 Version History

Historical versions should remain traceable where governance requires.

---

# 2.37 Version Number

May use:

- simple sequence
- semantic revision
- release-aligned identifier

depending on business need.

---

# 2.38 Version Boundary

Do not create complex semantic versioning for ordinary operating documents without need.

---

# 2.39 Effective Date

Defines when approved Knowledge becomes operationally applicable.

---

# 2.40 Expiry Date

Optional for:

- temporary policy
- temporary procedure
- vendor guidance
- transitional instruction

---

# 2.41 Review Date

Represents planned review point.

---

# 2.42 Review Date Boundary

Review due date does not automatically make Knowledge invalid unless policy says so.

---

# 2.43 Knowledge Owner

Represents accountable role/person for Knowledge accuracy and maintenance.

Potential fields:

- Owner ID
- user/Role
- ownership type
- effective dates

---

# 2.44 Owner Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-owner-boundary44s2"
Knowledge Owner
≠
Knowledge Author
```

---

# 2.45 Knowledge Author

Represents creator or material editor.

---

# 2.46 Multiple Authors

A Version may have:

- primary author
- contributors

where useful.

---

# 2.47 Knowledge Approver

Represents authorized person/Role approving official Knowledge.

---

# 2.48 Approver Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-approver-boundary44s2"
Editor Permission
≠
Approval Authority
```

---

# 2.49 Approval Record

Captures formal approval decision.

Minimum:

- Approval ID
- Knowledge Version
- approver
- decision
- date
- comments/conditions

---

# 2.50 Approval Decision

Potential:

- APPROVED
- APPROVED_WITH_CONDITIONS
- REJECTED
- RETURNED_FOR_CHANGES

---

# 2.51 Approval Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="approval-record-boundary44s2"
Approval Record
must identify
Specific Knowledge Version
```

---

# 2.52 Publication Record

Captures when a specific approved Version became available.

Potential:

- Publication ID
- Version
- audience
- publisher
- publication date

---

# 2.53 Publication Boundary

Published Knowledge should not point users silently to a Draft Version.

---

# 2.54 Knowledge Source

Represents origin of Knowledge.

Potential:

- certified business architecture
- approved policy
- vendor documentation
- legislation/regulation
- incident
- project
- management decision
- employee expertise

---

# 2.55 Source Fields

Potential:

- Source ID
- type
- reference
- owner/origin
- date
- reliability/authority classification

---

# 2.56 Source Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="source-boundary44s2"
Source Exists
≠
Source Is Authoritative
```

---

# 2.57 Knowledge Provenance

Represents chain from source to current approved Knowledge.

Potential:

```text id="knowledge-provenance44s2"
Source

↓

Author

↓

Version

↓

Review

↓

Approval

↓

Publication
```

---

# 2.58 Provenance Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="provenance-boundary44s2"
No Provenance
=
Lower Trust
```

for material official Knowledge.

---

# 2.59 Knowledge Scope

Defines where Knowledge applies.

Potential dimensions:

- Enterprise
- Legal Entity
- Company
- Business Unit
- Department
- Domain
- Role
- Process
- Environment

---

# 2.60 Enterprise Scope

Applies across GiftHatke unless narrower rule exists.

---

# 2.61 Company Scope

Domain 40 governs Company context.

---

# 2.62 Role Scope

May identify intended audience, not permission authority.

---

# 2.63 Scope Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="scope-boundary44s2"
Applicable to Role
≠
Visible Only to Role
```

Applicability and access are different.

---

# 2.64 Knowledge Classification

Represents information sensitivity.

Potential:

- PUBLIC
- INTERNAL
- CONFIDENTIAL
- RESTRICTED

---

# 2.65 Classification Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="classification-boundary44s2"
Knowledge Classification
≠
Knowledge Authority
```

---

# 2.66 Knowledge Access Policy

May define who can:

- read
- edit
- approve
- publish
- archive

---

# 2.67 Access Control Boundary

---

# 2.68 Knowledge Taxonomy

Represents structured grouping for discoverability.

Potential dimensions:

- Domain
- business function
- process
- audience
- topic

---

# 2.69 Taxonomy Principle

Start simple.

Example:

```text id="simple-taxonomy44s2"
Domain

↓

Process

↓

Topic
```

---

# 2.70 Taxonomy Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="taxonomy-boundary44s2"
Complex Taxonomy
≠
Better Findability
```

---

# 2.71 Knowledge Topic

Represents reusable subject classification.

Examples:

- Purchasing
- Inventory
- Laser Production
- Shipping
- Customer Support

---

# 2.72 Knowledge Tag

Represents flexible lightweight labels.

- onboarding
- exception
- marketplace

# 2.73 Tags Boundary

---

# 2.74 Knowledge Relationship

Connects Knowledge Assets.

Potential types:

- RELATED_TO
- DERIVED_FROM
- SUPERSEDES
- REPLACED_BY
- DEPENDS_ON
- APPLIES_TO
- EXPLAINS
- SUPPORTS

# 2.75 Relationship Direction

Some relationships are directional.

Example:

```text id="supersedes44s2"
Procedure v2
SUPERSEDES
Procedure v1
```

# 2.76 Related Knowledge

---

# 2.77 Supersession Record

Explicitly records replacement.

Potential:

- old asset/version

- effective date
- reason

---

# 2.78 Supersession Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="supersession-boundary44s2"
Superseded
≠
Deleted
```

---

# 2.79 Knowledge Reference

Links Knowledge to external or internal authoritative entities.

- ERP module
- policy
- incident
- project
- release
- integration

# 2.80 Business Record Reference

---

# 2.81 Knowledge Attachment Reference

May point to:

- PDF
- diagram
- video
- image
- template

---

# 2.82 Attachment Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="attachment-boundary44s2"
Attachment
≠
Knowledge Authority by Itself
```

---

# 2.83 Organizational Memory Record

Represents structured retained institutional context not necessarily suitable as a formal Procedure.

Potential types:

- historical rationale
- project history
- architecture decision
- migration learning
- business milestone
- operational lesson

---

# 2.84 Memory Record Fields

Potential:

- Memory ID
- title
- type
- context
- source
- owner
- date
- related Knowledge/Domain

---

# 2.85 Memory Record Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="memory-record-boundary44s2"
Organizational Memory
≠
Current Operating Instruction
```

unless separately approved as such.

---

# 2.86 Architecture Decision Record

May be a subtype of Decision Record.

Potential:

- decision
- alternatives
- rationale
- consequences
- status

---

# 2.87 Architecture Record Example

```text id="adr-example44s2"
Decision:
Preserve Apps Script v1.0
as certified reference baseline.

Rationale:
Business architecture preservation
during standalone migration.
```

---

# 2.88 Architecture Decision Boundary

Historical architecture decision remains context.

Current production authority comes from certified current architecture.

---

# 2.89 Knowledge Review

Represents quality/freshness review.

Potential:

- Review ID
- Version
- reviewer
- review date
- result
- changes required

---

# 2.90 Review Results

Potential:

- CURRENT
- UPDATE_REQUIRED
- SUPERSEDE
- ARCHIVE

---

# 2.91 Review Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="review-boundary44s2"
Reviewed
≠
Approved New Version
```

---

# 2.92 Knowledge Feedback

Represents user feedback about content.

Potential:

- incorrect
- outdated
- unclear
- missing detail
- useful

---

# 2.93 Feedback Fields

Potential:

- Feedback ID
- Knowledge Asset
- user
- category
- message
- date
- status

---

# 2.94 Feedback Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="feedback-boundary44s2"
Feedback Submitted
≠
Official Knowledge Changed
```

---

# 2.95 Feedback Resolution

May result in:

- no change
- clarification
- correction
- new Version
- retirement

---

# 2.96 Knowledge Change Request

Optional future entity for controlled material changes.

---

# 2.97 Change Request Boundary

Do not introduce formal change-request workflow for every minor typo.

---

# 2.98 Knowledge Audience

Potential:

- All Employees
- Production Team
- Customer Success
- Finance
- Administrators
- Executives
- Partners
- Customers

---

# 2.99 Audience Boundary

Intended audience ≠ Security permission.

---

# 2.100 External Knowledge Asset

May represent:

- Customer Help Article
- Partner Documentation
- Developer Documentation

---

# 2.101 External vs Internal Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="external-internal44s2"
External Knowledge Asset
≠
Internal Procedure
```

Even if they discuss the same process.

---

# 2.102 Knowledge Template

Optional entity/reference for standardized structure.

Examples:

- SOP template
- Policy template
- Decision Record template

---

# 2.103 Template Boundary

Templates support consistency.

They do not create Knowledge automatically.

---

# 2.104 Knowledge Language

Future Knowledge may carry:

- language
- locale

where localization exists.

---

# 2.105 Translation Relationship

A translated Knowledge Asset/version should remain linked to source content.

---

# 2.106 Translation Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="translation-boundary44s2"
Translation Published
≠
Source Version Automatically Synchronized Forever
```

Changes require review.

---

# 2.107 Localization

Domain 40 may influence:

- language
- regional applicability
- local policy

---

# 2.108 Knowledge Freshness Metadata

Potential:

- last reviewed
- next review
- source updated
- suspected stale

---

# 2.109 Stale Flag

Potential state:

```text id="stale-flag44s2"
STALE_REVIEW_REQUIRED
```

without immediately archiving the asset.

---

# 2.110 Freshness Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="freshness-boundary44s2"
Recently Edited
≠
Accurate
```

---

# 2.111 Knowledge Confidence

Avoid arbitrary confidence scores for approved policy/procedure.

Authority and provenance are more meaningful.

---

# 2.112 AI-Generated Flag

Knowledge Version may record:

- AI-assisted
- human-authored
- imported

as provenance metadata where useful.

---

# 2.113 AI-Generated Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="ai-generated-boundary44s2"
AI-Assisted Content
≠
Lower or Higher Authority Automatically
```

Approval determines official status.

---

# 2.114 Knowledge Citation

Future AI/search responses may cite:

- Knowledge Asset
- Version
- source

for traceability.

---

# 2.115 Citation Boundary

Citation points to source.

It does not prove source is current unless status/version confirms it.

---

# 2.116 Search Index Record

Domain 17 may index:

- title
- summary
- topics
- body
- authority
- current Version

---

# 2.117 Search Index Boundary

Search index is derived data.

It is not authoritative Knowledge storage.

---

# 2.118 Knowledge Embedding/Vector Record

Future semantic retrieval may maintain derived embeddings.

---

# 2.119 Embedding Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="embedding-boundary44s2"
Embedding
≠
Knowledge Asset
```

---

# 2.120 Knowledge Graph Relationship

Future Knowledge graph may derive structured relationships.

Not required now.

---

# 2.121 Graph Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-graph-boundary44s2"
Graph Relationship
≠
Automatic Business Truth
```

---

# 2.122 Entity Relationship Summary

Canonical:

```text id="entity-relationship-summary44s2"
Knowledge Asset

↓

Knowledge Version

↓

Source / Provenance

↓

Review

↓

Approval

↓

Publication
```

---

# 2.123 Ownership Relationship

Canonical:

```text id="ownership-relationship44s2"
Knowledge Asset

↓

Domain / Scope

↓

Knowledge Owner

↓

Author / Contributors

↓

Approver
```

---

# 2.124 Retrieval Relationship

Canonical:

```text id="retrieval-relationship44s2"
Knowledge Asset

↓

Taxonomy / Topics / Tags

↓

Search Index

↓

User / AI Retrieval
```

---

# 2.125 Historical Relationship

Canonical:

```text id="historical-relationship44s2"
Old Version

↓

Superseded By

↓

Current Version

while

Old Version Remains Historical Evidence
```

---

# 2.126 Decision Memory Relationship

Canonical:

```text id="decision-memory44s2"
Business / Architecture Decision

↓

Decision Record

↓

Affected Domains / Releases / Projects

↓

Future Organizational Context
```

---

# 2.127 Document Relationship

Canonical:

```text id="document-relationship44s2"
Knowledge Asset

↓

Content / Attachment Reference

↓

Domain 10 Document or Asset
```

---

# 2.128 Training Relationship

Canonical:

```text id="training-relationship44s2"
Official Knowledge

↓

Training Material

↓

Employee Learning
```

Training material remains derived.

---

# 2.129 Incident Learning Relationship

Canonical:

```text id="incident-learning44s2"
Incident

↓

Lesson Learned

↓

Procedure / Control Improvement
```

---

# 2.130 ERP Release Relationship

Knowledge may reference:

- release
- feature
- certified version

for documentation synchronization.

---

# 2.131 Release Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="release-boundary44s2"
ERP Release Exists
≠
Knowledge Automatically Updated
```

---

# 2.132 SMP1 Minimum Entity Requirement

For SMP1, no new formal Knowledge entity database is required.

---

# 2.133 SMP1 Existing Knowledge

SMP1 should preserve existing:

- documentation
- architecture decisions
- migration instructions
- operational handover
- test/reconciliation guidance

using practical storage.

---

# 2.134 SMP1 Minimal Metadata

Where useful, existing documentation may track simply:

- title
- owner
- Version
- status
- updated date

without building Domain 44 software.

---

# 2.135 SMP1 No Knowledge Graph

Do not implement:

- ontology
- semantic graph
- AI memory platform
- knowledge recommendation
- specialized Knowledge database

for SMP1.

---

# 2.136 First Future Implementation

When Domain 44 becomes operationally necessary, begin with:

```text id="first-implementation44s2"
Knowledge Asset
+
Version
+
Owner
+
Status
+
Source
+
Review Date
+
Searchable Content
```

---

# 2.137 Second Future Implementation

Later add:

- Approval Records
- relationships
- feedback
- Decision Records
- lessons learned

---

# 2.138 Third Future Implementation

Only when scale requires:

- semantic search
- embeddings
- Knowledge graph
- AI retrieval optimization

---

# 2.139 ERP9 Reuse

ERP9's Settings/Master Data changes may provide references for:

- Company scope
- Domain
- Role
- configuration-related Knowledge.

---

# 2.140 ERP10 Reuse

ERP10 may strengthen contextual:

- help
- onboarding
- documentation links
- operational support.

---

# 2.141 Version 1.1 Reuse

Version 1.1 may introduce lightweight:

- embedded help
- Decision Records
- searchable official Knowledge

if operational demand exists.

---

# 2.142 Advanced Entities That Can Wait

Do not block roadmap for:

- Knowledge reputation
- expert profile
- social comments
- article popularity scoring
- recommendation graphs
- ontology entities
- concept inference
- AI-curated topic clusters
- automated expertise maps
- enterprise semantic graph

---

# 2.143 Anti-Duplication Rule

Permanent:

> **Domain 44 entities represent governed Knowledge, meaning, provenance, and organizational memory. They do not duplicate business transactions, Document storage, Search indexes, employee profiles, AI memory, or operational telemetry.**

---

# 2.144 Anti-Documentation-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **A Knowledge Asset may describe certified architecture, but its entity model cannot become an alternative source of business rules or transactional states.**

---

# 2.145 Anti-Overengineering Rule

Permanent:

> **The first practical Knowledge model is simple: what the Knowledge is, which version is current, who owns it, where it came from, who approved it, and when it must be reviewed. Everything beyond that must solve a real organizational problem.**

---

# 2.146 Critical Entity Invariants

1. Knowledge Asset ≠ business transaction.
2. Knowledge Type ≠ authority.
3. Policy document ≠ system enforcement.
4. Procedure describes process ≠ owns process state.
5. Decision Record ≠ current runtime configuration.
6. Lesson captured ≠ improvement implemented.
7. Knowledge status and Knowledge version are separate.
8. Approved ≠ Published.
9. Knowledge Asset identity ≠ specific Version.
10. Review due ≠ automatically invalid.
11. Owner ≠ Author.
12. Editor ≠ Approver.
13. Approval applies to a specific Version.
14. Source exists ≠ source authoritative.
15. Scope applicability ≠ access permission.
16. Classification ≠ authority.
17. Taxonomy complexity ≠ discoverability quality.
18. Superseded ≠ deleted.
19. Attachment ≠ Knowledge authority.
20. Organizational Memory ≠ current operating instruction.
21. Reviewed ≠ new Version approved.
22. Feedback ≠ official Knowledge change.
23. Intended audience ≠ Security permission.
24. External help content ≠ internal Procedure.
25. Recently edited ≠ accurate.
26. AI-assisted content ≠ automatically approved.
27. Search index ≠ authoritative Knowledge storage.
28. Embedding ≠ Knowledge Asset.
29. Knowledge graph relationship ≠ business truth.
30. SMP1 requires preservation of Knowledge, not implementation of Domain 44 software.

---

Stage 2 permanently establishes the implementation-grade entity architecture for:

- Knowledge Assets

- taxonomy/topics/tags
- Knowledge relationships
- supersession
- references/attachments
- Organizational Memory
- architecture decisions
- reviews
- feedback
- audience
- external Knowledge
- templates
- language/localization
- freshness
- AI provenance
- citations
- Search/embedding/graph derived entities
- ERP release relationships
- SMP1 minimum/non-requirements
- ERP9/ERP10/Version 1.1 reuse

- anti-documentation-drift

This is sufficient to define a durable Knowledge and organizational-memory entity model while keeping SMP1 completely free from unnecessary Knowledge-platform implementation.

# ENTERPRISE KNOWLEDGE OPERATING SYSTEM & ORGANIZATIONAL MEMORY CANON
## Stage 3 — Knowledge Lifecycle, Capture, Review, Approval, Publication, Supersession, Archival, Decision Memory, Feedback & Organizational Learning Operating Model Canon

---

# 3.1 Purpose

Stage 3 defines how enterprise Knowledge moves from initial capture through review, approval, publication, use, maintenance, supersession, archival, and organizational learning.

The objective is:

> **Ensure important GiftHatke knowledge remains current, attributable, reviewable, easy to improve, and clearly separated from Draft opinion, outdated guidance, and transactional business truth.**

---

# 3.2 Core Operating Principle

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-operating-principle44s3"
Knowledge Need

↓

Capture

↓

Validate

↓

Review

↓

Approve

↓

Publish

↓

Use

↓

Review / Improve

↓

Supersede / Archive
```

---

# 3.3 Knowledge Lifecycle States

Canonical:

```text id="knowledge-lifecycle-states44s3"
DRAFT

↓

IN REVIEW

↓

APPROVED

↓

PUBLISHED

↓

SUPERSEDED / ARCHIVED / RETIRED
```

---

# 3.4 Knowledge Need Identification

Knowledge creation should begin from a real need such as:

- repeated operational question
- new business process
- ERP release
- incident
- policy change
- training requirement
- key-person dependency
- migration requirement

---

# 3.5 Need Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-need-boundary44s3"
Possible Topic
≠
Documentation Requirement
```

---

# 3.6 Knowledge Request

Future teams may request:

- new article
- procedure
- update
- clarification

through a simple workflow.

---

# 3.7 No Documentation Backlog Inflation

Do not create hundreds of low-value documentation tasks merely because every process could theoretically be documented.

---

# 3.8 Prioritization

Higher priority Knowledge includes:

- critical operations
- frequent questions
- high-risk processes
- onboarding
- business continuity
- certified workflow changes

---

# 3.9 Critical Knowledge

Examples:

- Order handling
- Inventory adjustment
- Production exception
- Finance closing
- shipping failure
- system recovery

---

# 3.10 Knowledge Capture

Knowledge may originate from:

- Domain owner
- operational expert
- existing documentation
- incident
- decision
- project
- vendor source

---

# 3.11 Capture Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="capture-boundary44s3"
Captured Information
≠
Approved Knowledge
```

---

# 3.12 Initial Draft

Draft should identify:

- topic
- purpose
- intended audience
- source
- owner

where material.

---

# 3.13 Draft Authority

Draft Knowledge should never be presented as official guidance.

---

# 3.14 Draft Visibility

Drafts may be visible to collaborators according to access policy.

---

# 3.15 Draft Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="draft-boundary44s3"
Draft Exists
≠
Team Must Follow It
```

---

# 3.16 Knowledge Authoring

Author should focus on:

- clarity
- correctness
- business language
- actionable guidance

---

# 3.17 Authoring Standard

Good operational Knowledge should answer:

- What is this?
- When do I use it?
- What do I do?
- What are the exceptions?
- Who owns escalation?

---

# 3.18 No Unnecessary Theory

Operational Procedures should not become architecture essays unless the audience needs that context.

---

# 3.19 Source Validation

Before review, identify the authoritative source.

Potential:

- certified Domain
- policy
- legal requirement
- business owner
- approved decision

---

# 3.20 Source Conflict

If source material conflicts:

Do not publish until resolved.

---

# 3.21 Review

Review evaluates:

- accuracy
- completeness
- clarity
- currentness
- alignment to certified business process

---

# 3.22 Reviewer Selection

Reviewer should understand the affected:

- Domain
- process
- policy
- Risk

---

# 3.23 Review Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="review-boundary44s3"
Reviewed
≠
Approved
```

---

# 3.24 Review Outcome

Potential:

- Ready for Approval
- Changes Required
- Reject
- Merge With Existing Knowledge

---

# 3.25 Duplicate Detection

Review should check whether authoritative Knowledge already exists.

---

# 3.26 Duplicate Handling

Prefer:

- update canonical article
- link related material

instead of creating competing instructions.

---

# 3.27 Approval

Approval confirms the specific Knowledge Version is suitable for official use.

---

# 3.28 Approval Authority

Approval depth should reflect Risk.

---

# 3.29 Low-Risk Approval

Simple Guide may need only Domain owner review.

---

# 3.30 High-Risk Approval

Finance/Security/Legal Procedures may need specific authorized approver.

---

# 3.31 Approval Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="approval-boundary44s3"
Approved Version
≠
All Future Versions Approved
```

---

# 3.32 Approval Conditions

Potential:

- limited scope
- temporary validity
- follow-up required

---

# 3.33 Rejected Knowledge

Rejected content remains Draft/history where useful.

It should not be published as current guidance.

---

# 3.34 Publication

Publication makes approved Knowledge available to intended audience.

---

# 3.35 Publication Preconditions

Potential:

- approved Version
- audience defined
- access correct
- effective date set

---

# 3.36 Publication Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="publication-boundary44s3"
Approved
≠
Published
```

---

# 3.37 Effective Date

Published Knowledge may become effective:

- immediately
- on future date
- with release/cutover

---

# 3.38 Future-Dated Knowledge

Should clearly show:

- NOT YET EFFECTIVE

until activation date.

---

# 3.39 Publication Audience

Potential:

- All Staff
- Finance
- Production
- Customer Success
- Admin
- Partners
- Customers

---

# 3.40 Publication Scope

Company/Role/Domain scope must remain visible where relevant.

---

# 3.41 Knowledge Notification

Notify affected users for material changes.

---

# 3.42 Notification Boundary

Do not notify all staff for every typo or minor formatting update.

---

# 3.43 Material Change

Examples:

- changed process
- changed policy
- changed approval
- new exception handling
- critical safety/compliance update

---

# 3.44 Minor Change

Examples:

- spelling
- formatting
- broken link
- harmless clarification

---

# 3.45 Change Classification

A Knowledge update may be:

- Minor
- Material
- Critical

where useful.

---

# 3.46 Version Creation

Material change should normally create a new Version.

---

# 3.47 Minor Edit

Minor non-substantive correction may not require full approval cycle if governance permits.

---

# 3.48 Version Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="version-change-boundary44s3"
Formatting Change
≠
Business Rule Change
```

---

# 3.49 Knowledge Use

Users consume Knowledge through:

- search
- contextual help
- training
- direct link
- workflow reference

---

# 3.50 Usage Boundary

Knowledge consumption does not itself prove:

- understanding
- compliance
- successful task completion

---

# 3.51 User Feedback

Users should be able to report:

- Incorrect
- Outdated
- Unclear
- Missing

---

# 3.52 Feedback Intake

Feedback should capture:

- Knowledge Asset
- user
- category
- comment
- date

---

# 3.53 Feedback Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="feedback-boundary44s3"
Feedback Submitted
≠
Knowledge Automatically Changed
```

---

# 3.54 Feedback Triage

Potential:

- no change
- clarification
- urgent correction
- full review
- retirement

---

# 3.55 Critical Incorrect Knowledge

If published Knowledge is dangerously wrong:

- withdraw/suspend it promptly
- publish correction
- preserve history

---

# 3.56 Temporary Withdrawal

Knowledge may be marked:

- UNDER REVIEW
- TEMPORARILY WITHDRAWN

where appropriate.

---

# 3.57 Withdrawal Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="withdrawal-boundary44s3"
Knowledge Withdrawn
≠
Historical Version Deleted
```

---

# 3.58 Periodic Review

Official Knowledge should be reviewed based on Risk and change rate.

---

# 3.59 Review Triggers

Potential:

- scheduled review
- ERP release
- process change
- policy update
- incident
- user feedback
- legal change

---

# 3.60 High-Change Knowledge

May require more frequent review.

---

# 3.61 Stable Knowledge

Should not be repeatedly reviewed without purpose.

---

# 3.62 Review Outcome

Potential:

- Still Current
- Update Required
- Supersede
- Archive
- Retire

---

# 3.63 Current Confirmation

A review may simply confirm:

- current Version remains valid.

---

# 3.64 Update Required

Creates new Draft Version.

---

# 3.65 Supersession

When new Knowledge replaces old:

```text id="supersession-flow44s3"
New Version Approved

↓

Publish

↓

Old Version Marked SUPERSEDED

↓

Link Old → New
```

---

# 3.66 Supersession Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="supersession-boundary44s3"
Superseded
≠
Deleted
```

---

# 3.67 Archive

Archive retains Knowledge primarily for:

- history
- Audit
- reference

---

# 3.68 Archived UX

Archived Knowledge should not normally appear as current answer.

---

# 3.69 Archive Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="archive-boundary44s3"
Archived
≠
Current Guidance
```

---

# 3.70 Retirement

Retirement indicates Knowledge is no longer useful for normal operations.

---

# 3.71 Retirement vs Archive

Retired may indicate obsolete subject.

Archived indicates retained historical material.

---

# 3.72 Knowledge Deletion

Permanent official Knowledge should generally not be physically deleted unless:

- legal/privacy
- data-retention
- duplicate cleanup

requires it.

---

# 3.73 Historical Preservation

Maintain enough history to know:

- what instruction existed
- when
- who approved it

where material.

---

# 3.74 Decision Record Lifecycle

Canonical:

```text id="decision-lifecycle44s3"
Decision Proposed

↓

Decision Made

↓

Rationale Recorded

↓

Published to Relevant Audience

↓

Superseded if Future Decision Changes It
```

---

# 3.75 Decision Record Timing

Important decision should ideally be recorded close to when it is made.

---

# 3.76 Decision Memory Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="decision-memory-boundary44s3"
Decision Changed Later
≠
Original Decision Record Erased
```

---

# 3.77 Decision Supersession

New decision should link to:

- prior decision
- reason for change

---

# 3.78 Architecture Decisions

Material GiftHatkeOS architecture decisions should preserve:

- context
- choice
- rationale
- consequences

---

# 3.79 TITAN LOCK Decisions

Certified roadmap/architecture decisions may be preserved as Decision Records.

---

# 3.80 Operational Decision Memory

Not every daily management choice needs permanent Decision Record.

---

# 3.81 Decision Significance

Good candidates:

- architecture change
- major process change
- policy change
- strategic vendor choice
- migration/cutover decision

---

# 3.82 Lesson Learned Lifecycle

Canonical:

```text id="lesson-lifecycle44s3"
Event / Incident / Project

↓

Lesson Identified

↓

Validate

↓

Record

↓

Apply to Procedure / Control / Training if Needed
```

---

# 3.83 Lesson Validation

A single anecdote should not automatically become organization-wide rule.

---

# 3.84 Lesson Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="lesson-boundary44s3"
Lesson Identified
≠
Policy Changed
```

---

# 3.85 Incident Learning

After material incident:

Ask:

- what failed?
- why?
- what reusable Knowledge should change?

---

# 3.86 Incident Closure Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="incident-learning-boundary44s3"
Incident Resolved
≠
Organizational Learning Completed
```

---

# 3.87 Post-Incident Update

May update:

- Troubleshooting
- Procedure
- fallback
- escalation
- training

---

# 3.88 Project Learning

Projects may produce:

- implementation notes
- lessons learned
- decisions
- operating handover

---

# 3.89 Migration Learning

SMP1 should capture material:

- field interpretation
- reconciliation lesson
- cutover issue
- runtime difference

where useful for support/audit.

---

# 3.90 Handover Knowledge

Business handover should prioritize:

- what users need to operate
- support
- escalate
- recover

---

# 3.91 New Employee Onboarding

Official Knowledge may feed structured onboarding.

---

# 3.92 Onboarding Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="onboarding-boundary44s3"
Employee Read Article
≠
Employee Proven Competent
```

Domain 25 owns workforce capability.

---

# 3.93 Training Update

If official Procedure changes materially:

Relevant training may need review.

---

# 3.94 Training Synchronization

Canonical:

```text id="training-sync44s3"
Official Knowledge Changes

↓

Training Impact Review

↓

Training Updated if Needed
```

---

# 3.95 Policy Update

When Policy changes:

Related Procedures should be reviewed.

---

# 3.96 Dependency Impact

Knowledge relationships may trigger review of dependent material.

---

# 3.97 Example

```text id="knowledge-dependency44s3"
Returns Policy Updated

↓

Review:

Returns Procedure
Customer Support Guide
Training Material
```

---

```text id="release-knowledge-boundary44s3"
≠
```

```text id="smp1-knowledge-lifecycle44s3"

↓

↓
```

Introduce simple:

- Review

workflow.

- feedback

---

- knowledge reputation workflows
- social publishing
- crowdsourced approval

- continuous semantic knowledge reconciliation.

# 3.149 Anti-Duplication Rule

Permanent:

> **Domain 44 manages the lifecycle of Knowledge. Domain 11 may provide workflow mechanics, Domain 10 document storage, Domain 17 retrieval, Domain 25 training, Domain 39 assurance, and certified Business Domains remain authoritative for operational truth.**

---

# 3.150 Anti-Documentation-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **Knowledge lifecycle processes may update how certified business architecture is explained. They must not become an unofficial mechanism for changing that architecture.**

---

# 3.151 Anti-Overengineering Rule

Permanent:

> **The operating model should make important Knowledge trustworthy and current. It should not turn every team note into a governed enterprise artifact.**

---

# 3.152 Critical Operating Invariants

1. Possible topic ≠ documentation requirement.
2. Captured information ≠ approved Knowledge.
3. Draft exists ≠ team must follow it.
4. Reviewed ≠ approved.
5. Approved Version ≠ future Versions approved.
6. Approved ≠ Published.
7. Formatting change ≠ business-rule change.
8. Knowledge consumed ≠ user understood or complied.
9. Feedback submitted ≠ Knowledge automatically changed.
10. Withdrawn ≠ deleted.
11. Superseded ≠ deleted.
12. Archived ≠ current guidance.
13. Decision changed ≠ original Decision Record erased.
14. Lesson identified ≠ policy changed.
15. Incident resolved ≠ organizational learning completed.
16. Employee read article ≠ employee proven competent.
17. Policy update may require Procedure review.
18. Related content review ≠ automatic rewrite.
19. Software changed ≠ every document changed.
20. Runtime changed ≠ business procedure changed.
21. Legacy docs preserved ≠ legacy runtime authoritative.
22. Temporary workaround ≠ permanent architecture.
23. Owner missing ≠ Knowledge automatically invalid.
24. Useful internally ≠ safe externally.
25. Source updated ≠ translation still current.
26. AI-generated Draft ≠ automatic publication.
27. Historical context ≠ current Procedure.
28. SMP1 requires critical-document maintenance, not a Knowledge workflow platform.
29. Knowledge lifecycle must remain Risk-proportional.
30. Documentation cannot become a backdoor for architecture change.

---

# 3.153 Stage 3 Certification

Stage 3 permanently establishes the implementation-grade operating model for:

- Knowledge need identification
- prioritization
- capture
- Drafting
- source validation
- review
- duplicate handling
- approval
- publication
- effective dates
- audience/scope
- material/minor changes
- versioning
- feedback
- withdrawal
- periodic review
- supersession
- archival/retirement
- Decision Records
- architecture memory
- Lessons Learned
- incident/project/migration learning
- handover
- training synchronization
- dependency impact
- ERP release documentation review
- runtime-vs-business Knowledge
- conflict resolution
- emergency/temporary Knowledge
- ownership transfer
- confidential/external publication
- translations
- AI-assisted authoring
- Organizational Memory
- Knowledge health
- Audit
- SMP1 practical lifecycle
- ERP9/ERP10/Version 1.1 reuse
- anti-duplication
- anti-documentation-drift
- anti-overengineering

This is sufficient to govern trustworthy organizational Knowledge throughout its lifecycle while keeping SMP1 focused on preserving and updating only the documentation needed for successful standalone migration and business operations.

# ENTERPRISE KNOWLEDGE OPERATING SYSTEM & ORGANIZATIONAL MEMORY CANON
## Stage 4 — Knowledge Repository, Publishing, Search Integration, Contextual Help, Provenance, Decision Memory, Feedback & Organizational Memory Service Architecture Canon

---

# 4.1 Purpose

Stage 4 defines the service architecture required to store, publish, retrieve, contextualize, review, relate, and preserve enterprise Knowledge and organizational memory.

The objective is:

> **Provide a controlled Knowledge service layer that can evolve from simple documentation into searchable, contextual, AI-usable organizational memory without duplicating document storage, search engines, workflow systems, or transactional ERP services.**

---

# 4.2 Service Architecture Principle

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-service-principle44s4"
Knowledge Services
=
Governed Meaning + Lifecycle + Retrieval Context

not
=
Second Transactional ERP
```

---

# 4.3 Core Future Services

Potential:

- Knowledge Registry Service
- Knowledge Version Service
- Knowledge Publishing Service
- Knowledge Ownership Service
- Knowledge Provenance Service
- Knowledge Review Service
- Knowledge Approval Service
- Knowledge Relationship Service
- Knowledge Taxonomy Service
- Knowledge Feedback Service

- Lesson Learned Service
- Contextual Help Service
- Knowledge Retrieval Service

- Knowledge Audit Service
- Organizational Memory Service
- Knowledge AI Gateway

Not all are required initially.

---

# 4.97 Import Boundary

Imported file initially may be:

- reference
- Draft
- historical

not automatically approved.

---

# 4.98 Bulk Import

Large imports should preserve:

- source
- original date
- ownership where known
- migration provenance

---

# 4.99 Legacy Documentation Mapping

- still current business Knowledge
- runtime-specific legacy
- historical reference
- superseded

---

# 4.100 Legacy Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="legacy-service-boundary44s4"
Imported Legacy Documentation
≠
Current Standalone Instruction
```

# 4.101 Export Service

- handover packs
- policy collections
- audit evidence

---

# 4.102 Export Boundary

---

# 4.103 Offline Knowledge

If offline copies are used:

show:

- exported date
- Version

where material.

---

# 4.104 Knowledge Repository Architecture

Future logical model:

```text id="repository-architecture44s4"
Knowledge Metadata

+

Current / Historical Content References

+

Ownership / Provenance / Lifecycle

+

Search Projection
```

# 4.105 Storage Independence

Domain 44 should remain technology-independent.

Possible future storage:

- relational DB metadata
- object/document storage
- search index

without changing Knowledge semantics.

---

# 4.106 No Knowledge Microservices Requirement

Permanent:

> **Certified Knowledge services are logical capabilities, not a requirement for separate deployable microservices.**

---

# 4.107 Modular Monolith Fit

Standalone GiftHatkeOS may implement Knowledge capabilities inside the modular monolith if/when needed.

---

# 4.108 Service Boundary Principle

Service boundaries should represent:

- responsibility

not infrastructure fashion.

Domain 29 governs:

- classification
- retention
- confidential/sensitive content
- external sharing

---

Domain 44 governs Knowledge semantics.

# 4.117 AI Integration

Domain 42 may consume approved Knowledge but does not become owner of it.

# 4.118 Platform Integration

Domain 41 provides:

- runtime
- database
- search infrastructure
- storage
- access infrastructure

---

# 4.119 SMP1 Required Service Architecture

For SMP1:

```text id="smp1-service-scope44s4"
Dedicated Domain 44 Services Required:
NONE
```

---

- storage
- version control/history
- accessibility
- ownership

using existing tooling.

---

# 4.121 SMP1 Migration Documentation

Required documentation may include:

- source-to-target mapping
- migration runbook
- reconciliation procedures
- cutover procedure
- rollback procedure
- operational handover

---

# 4.122 SMP1 No Repository Replatforming

Do not migrate documentation into a new custom Knowledge system merely because SMP1 is migrating ERP runtime.

---

# 4.123 SMP1 No Search Platform Work

Do not build:

- semantic Knowledge Search
- vector database
- Knowledge graph
- AI documentation assistant

for migration critical path.

---

# 4.124 First Future Service Step

When operational need appears:

Implement simple:

```text id="first-service-step44s4"
Knowledge Registry

+

Version

+

Owner

+

Publish Status

+

Search
```

---

# 4.125 Second Future Service Step

Later:

- Review/Approval
- feedback
- contextual help
- Decision Records

---

# 4.126 Third Future Service Step

Only when scale justifies:

- semantic retrieval
- AI Knowledge Gateway
- relationship intelligence
- advanced organizational memory

---

# 4.127 ERP9 Reuse

ERP9 may provide structured references for:

- Company
- configuration
- master data
- Business Domains

used by contextual Knowledge.

---

# 4.128 ERP10 Reuse

ERP10 may benefit most directly from:

- contextual help
- user guidance
- support Knowledge
- polished documentation links

---

# 4.129 Version 1.1 Reuse

Version 1.1 may introduce:

- lightweight Knowledge Registry
- embedded Help
- searchable operational guidance

if business adoption shows a clear need.

---

# 4.130 Advanced Services That Can Wait

Do not block roadmap for:

- enterprise Knowledge graph service
- autonomous Knowledge curator
- semantic ontology service
- expertise graph
- recommendation engine
- social Knowledge platform
- AI organizational-memory daemon
- automatic policy propagation
- Knowledge scoring engine
- sophisticated document intelligence platform

---

# 4.131 Anti-Duplication Rule

Permanent:

> **Domain 44 services govern Knowledge meaning, authority, lifecycle, provenance, relationships, and organizational memory. They reuse Domain 10 for documents, Domain 17 for Search, Domain 11 for Workflow, Domain 28 for access, and Domain 41 for infrastructure rather than recreating them.**

---

# 4.132 Anti-Documentation-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **Knowledge services may publish and retrieve certified operating guidance. They may not mutate certified business architecture through documentation workflows.**

---

# 4.133 Anti-Platform-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **GiftHatkeOS does not need to become an enterprise wiki or Knowledge-management software product to operate effectively. Knowledge capability should evolve only to support its own teams and business continuity.**

---

# 4.134 Anti-Overengineering Rule

Permanent:

> **The first useful Knowledge architecture is a trustworthy current article with an owner, Version, source, status, and searchability. Do not build semantic infrastructure before that simple system has real operational value.**

---

# 4.135 Critical Service Invariants

1. Knowledge services ≠ transactional ERP.
2. Knowledge Registry ≠ file storage.
3. Current Knowledge Asset ≠ mutable document history.
4. Content stored ≠ content published.
5. Author ≠ Owner ≠ Approver.
6. Review complete ≠ new Version approved.
7. Approval must apply to a specific Version.
8. Domain 44 should not duplicate Workflow engine.
9. Knowledge relationship ≠ transactional relationship.
10. Taxonomy ≠ enterprise ontology.
11. Feedback ≠ direct official edit.
12. Decision Memory ≠ configuration store.
13. Lesson stored ≠ Procedure changed.
14. Organizational Memory ≠ current operating instruction.
15. Contextual help ≠ transaction control.
16. Relevant search result ≠ authoritative result.
17. Search index ≠ Knowledge System of Record.
18. Can read ≠ can edit/approve/publish.
19. Search must not leak confidential Knowledge.
20. Freshness alert ≠ proof of error.
21. Code changed ≠ documentation definitely changed.
22. Knowledge API ≠ business transaction API.
23. AI retrieval cannot bypass user access.
24. Knowledge retrieval ≠ authority to execute business action.
25. AI Draft ≠ Published Knowledge.
26. Imported legacy documentation ≠ automatically current.
27. Exported copy ≠ perpetual authoritative copy.
28. Logical Knowledge services ≠ microservices requirement.
29. SMP1 requires no dedicated Domain 44 service implementation.
30. Knowledge architecture must mature only when operational demand justifies it.

---

- Knowledge Registry

This is sufficient to define a future Knowledge service architecture while preserving the critical TITAN LOCK principle that **SMP1 remains a standalone ERP migration, not a Knowledge-platform implementation programme.**

# ENTERPRISE KNOWLEDGE OPERATING SYSTEM & ORGANIZATIONAL MEMORY CANON
## Stage 5 — Knowledge Governance, Authority, Ownership, Access, Classification, Approval Rights, Retention, AI Use & Organizational Accountability Canon

---

# 5.1 Purpose

Stage 5 defines how GiftHatkeOS governs enterprise Knowledge so that official guidance remains trustworthy, appropriately restricted, attributable, reviewable, current, and safe for both humans and AI.

The objective is:

> **Ensure Knowledge authority, ownership, approval, access, retention, AI use, and accountability are explicit enough to preserve organizational trust without creating excessive documentation bureaucracy.**

---

# 5.2 Governance Philosophy

Permanent principles:

- Knowledge authority must be visible.
- ownership must be explicit for material Knowledge.
- authoring and approval are different responsibilities.
- access and authority are different dimensions.
- confidential Knowledge must remain protected.
- stale Knowledge must not silently present as current.
- archived Knowledge must not guide current operations by default.
- AI may retrieve Knowledge but does not gain authority from it.
- transactional truth remains in certified Business Domains.
- governance depth must remain proportional to Risk.

---

# 5.3 Governance Layers

Canonical:

```text id="knowledge-governance-layers44s5"
Enterprise Governance

↓

Domain Ownership

↓

Knowledge Asset Ownership

↓

Version Review / Approval

↓

Publication / Access

↓

Use / Feedback / Review
```

---

# 5.4 Knowledge Authority

Every material Knowledge Asset should carry a clear authority state.

Potential:

- OFFICIAL
- APPROVED
- DRAFT
- INFORMAL
- HISTORICAL

---

# 5.5 Authority Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-authority-boundary44s5"
Knowledge Is Accessible
≠
Knowledge Is Authoritative
```

---

# 5.6 Official Knowledge

Official Knowledge represents approved current organizational guidance.

---

# 5.7 Draft Knowledge

Drafts may support collaboration but must remain visibly non-authoritative.

---

# 5.8 Informal Knowledge

Useful team notes may exist without entering formal governance.

---

# 5.9 Historical Knowledge

Historical content may be retained for:

- Audit
- architecture memory
- dispute analysis
- migration history

but should not normally guide current operations.

---

# 5.10 Authority Hierarchy

For operational guidance, preferred order:

```text id="authority-hierarchy44s5"
Current Approved Policy / Procedure

↓

Current Approved Guide / Work Instruction

↓

Reference Material

↓

Draft / Informal Notes

↓

Historical / Archived Material
```

---

# 5.11 Authority Conflict

If two official sources conflict:

- escalate to owning authority
- resolve
- supersede one where appropriate

---

# 5.12 Conflict Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="conflicting-official-knowledge44s5"
Two Official Sources Conflict
≠
User Chooses Whichever Is Convenient
```

---

# 5.13 Knowledge Ownership

Material official Knowledge should have one accountable owner or owning Role.

---

# 5.14 Ownership Responsibilities

Potential:

- accuracy
- scope
- source validity
- review
- update
- retirement

---

# 5.15 Owner Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-owner-boundary44s5"
Knowledge Owner
≠
Everyday Editor
```

---

# 5.16 Domain Owner

The relevant certified Domain remains authoritative over business meaning.

Example:

```text id="finance-knowledge-owner44s5"
Finance Knowledge
→
Finance Domain Authority
```

---

# 5.17 Domain Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="domain-knowledge-boundary44s5"
Documentation Team
≠
Authority to Redefine Finance Rules
```

---

# 5.18 Author

Author creates or materially edits content.

---

# 5.19 Author Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="author-approval-boundary44s5"
Authored
≠
Approved
```

---

# 5.20 Contributor

Contributors may help prepare Knowledge without holding owner or approval authority.

---

# 5.21 Approver

Approver certifies a specific Version for its intended scope.

---

# 5.22 Approval Rights

Approval authority may depend on:

- Knowledge Type
- Domain
- Risk
- Company
- classification

---

# 5.23 Approval Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="approval-rights-boundary44s5"
Can Edit
≠
Can Approve
```

---

# 5.24 Self-Approval

Low-risk Knowledge may allow same person to author and approve if governance permits.

High-risk Knowledge may require separation.

---

# 5.25 Separation of Duties

Potentially appropriate for:

- Finance policy
- Security procedure
- Legal/compliance guidance
- high-impact operational control

---

# 5.26 Separation Boundary

Do not impose multi-person approval on every FAQ or simple Help article.

---

# 5.27 Risk-Proportional Governance

Canonical:

```text id="risk-proportional-governance44s5"
Higher Knowledge Consequence
=
Stronger Governance
```

---

# 5.28 High-Risk Knowledge

Examples:

- payment procedure
- access/security procedure
- legal/compliance instruction
- emergency recovery procedure

---

# 5.29 Low-Risk Knowledge

Examples:

- UI navigation Guide
- basic FAQ
- non-critical shortcut

---

# 5.30 Knowledge Scope

Governance should consider applicable:

- Enterprise
- Company
- Department
- Domain
- Role
- Process

---

# 5.31 Company Scope

Domain 40 remains authoritative.

---

# 5.32 Company Scope Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="company-knowledge-scope44s5"
Approved for Company A
≠
Approved for Company B
```

---

# 5.33 Role Applicability

Knowledge may be intended for specific Roles.

---

# 5.34 Applicability vs Access

Permanent:

```text id="role-applicability44s5"
Applies to Role
≠
Only Role Allowed to Read
```

unless Security requires it.

---

# 5.35 Knowledge Classification

Recommended classifications may include:

- PUBLIC
- INTERNAL
- CONFIDENTIAL
- RESTRICTED

---

# 5.36 Classification Ownership

Domain 29 provides information-classification governance.

---

# 5.37 Classification Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="classification-authority44s5"
CONFIDENTIAL
≠
More Authoritative
```

Classification describes sensitivity, not correctness.

---

# 5.38 Public Knowledge

May be externally shareable.

---

# 5.39 Internal Knowledge

Designed for employees/internal users.

---

# 5.40 Confidential Knowledge

May include:

- commercially sensitive procedures
- internal operations
- contracts
- employee-sensitive content

---

# 5.41 Restricted Knowledge

May include highly sensitive:

- Security
- credential
- incident
- recovery

information.

---

# 5.42 Access Governance

Knowledge access may distinguish:

- Read
- Edit
- Review
- Approve
- Publish
- Archive

---

# 5.43 Read Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="read-edit-boundary44s5"
Can Read
≠
Can Edit
```

---

# 5.44 Edit Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="edit-approve-boundary44s5"
Can Edit
≠
Can Approve
```

---

# 5.45 Publish Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="approve-publish-boundary44s5"
Can Approve
≠
Can Publish
```

where publication is separately controlled.

---

# 5.46 Search Access

Search must respect the same authorization as direct article access.

---

# 5.47 Search Leakage

Permanent:

```text id="search-leakage-boundary44s5"
Cannot Read Article
≠
Allowed to See Its Confidential Snippet
```

---

# 5.48 Contextual Help Access

Embedded Knowledge should also respect access rules.

---

# 5.49 External Publication Governance

Before publishing Knowledge externally:

Review:

- sensitivity
- accuracy
- audience
- contractual/security implications

---

# 5.50 External Publication Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="external-publishing44s5"
Safe Internally
≠
Safe Externally
```

---

# 5.51 Customer Knowledge

Customer-facing Help should not expose:

- internal controls
- confidential procedures
- unsupported promises

---

# 5.52 Partner Knowledge

Partner-facing documentation may expose:

- approved APIs
- operating procedures
- integration guidance

but not unrestricted internal architecture.

---

# 5.53 Developer Knowledge

Developer documentation remains governed by Domain 13/43 where relevant.

---

# 5.54 Retention

Knowledge retention should depend on:

- operational value
- Audit need
- legal requirement
- historical significance
- privacy

---

# 5.55 Retention Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="retention-boundary44s5"
Superseded
≠
Must Be Deleted
```

---

# 5.56 Historical Retention

Important prior versions may be retained to prove:

- what guidance existed
- when it applied
- who approved it

---

# 5.57 Deletion

Physical deletion may be appropriate for:

- duplicate junk
- privacy obligation
- accidental sensitive content
- retention requirement

---

# 5.58 Deletion Authority

Deletion of official historical Knowledge should require appropriate authority.

---

# 5.59 Knowledge Destruction Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-deletion44s5"
Not Current
≠
Safe to Delete
```

---

# 5.60 Retention vs Access

Historical content may be retained while normal users no longer see it.

---

# 5.61 Privacy

Knowledge may contain personal information.

Domain 29 governs privacy handling.

---

# 5.62 Personal Data Boundary

Do not use organizational Knowledge as an uncontrolled store for employee/customer personal data.

---

# 5.63 Sensitive Operational Data

Avoid embedding:

- passwords
- API secrets
- private keys

inside Knowledge articles.

---

# 5.64 Secret Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="secret-knowledge-boundary44s5"
Knowledge Article
≠
Secret Vault
```

---

# 5.65 Credential Documentation

Knowledge may explain:

- where credentials are managed
- rotation procedure

but should not store the actual Secret.

---

# 5.66 Policy Authority

A Policy becomes authoritative through:

- correct owner
- approval
- effective scope
- current Version

not merely its title.

---

# 5.67 Procedure Authority

Procedure must remain aligned with:

- certified process
- active policy
- actual system behavior

---

# 5.68 Procedure Drift

Permanent:

```text id="procedure-drift44s5"
Team Repeatedly Works Differently
≠
Procedure Automatically Changes
```

Investigate whether:

- team behavior is wrong
or
- Procedure requires update.

---

# 5.69 Knowledge Exception

Temporary deviation from Procedure should not be silently inserted as new standard.

---

# 5.70 Exception Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-exception44s5"
One Exception
≠
New Enterprise Rule
```

---

# 5.71 Emergency Knowledge

Urgent corrections may use accelerated governance.

---

# 5.72 Emergency Approval

Should preserve:

- owner
- reason
- approver
- timestamp
- follow-up review

---

# 5.73 Temporary Workaround

Must clearly identify:

- temporary status
- scope
- expiry/review

---

# 5.74 Temporary Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="temporary-knowledge44s5"
Temporary Workaround
≠
Permanent Procedure
```

---

# 5.75 Knowledge Freshness Accountability

Owner is responsible for material Knowledge remaining current.

---

# 5.76 Review Reminder

System may remind owners when:

- review due
- linked source changed
- linked process changed

---

# 5.77 Overdue Review

Overdue does not necessarily mean incorrect.

It does mean:

- review is pending.

---

# 5.78 Stale Knowledge Governance

Known stale content should be:

- marked
- updated
- withdrawn
- superseded

depending on Risk.

---

# 5.79 Stale Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="stale-knowledge-governance44s5"
Known Stale
≠
Safe to Present as Current
```

---

# 5.80 Knowledge Quality Accountability

Owners should care about:

- correctness
- clarity
- usefulness

not document length.

---

# 5.81 Quality Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-quality44s5"
More Pages
≠
Higher Quality
```

---

# 5.82 Duplicate Official Knowledge

Competing official instructions should be minimized.

---

# 5.83 Canonical Source

Where multiple supporting documents exist:

One current canonical source should be identifiable.

---

# 5.84 Duplicate Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="duplicate-official44s5"
Many Copies
≠
Many Sources of Truth
```

---

# 5.85 Knowledge Feedback Governance

Users may flag incorrect or unclear content.

---

# 5.86 Feedback Authority

Feedback creates a review signal.

It does not create a direct official change.

---

# 5.87 High-Risk Feedback

Reports that a Security/Finance/legal procedure is wrong should be prioritized.

---

# 5.88 Feedback Abuse

Repeated low-quality feedback should not automatically trigger unnecessary governance work.

---

# 5.89 Organizational Memory Governance

Historical context should preserve:

- source
- date
- owner
- context

where important.

---

# 5.90 Memory Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="memory-authority44s5"
Organizational Memory
≠
Current Operational Authority
```

---

# 5.91 Decision Record Governance

Material decisions should identify:

- decision authority
- context
- rationale
- date
- affected areas

---

# 5.92 Decision Authority

Only decisions actually made by authorized governance should be represented as final decisions.

---

# 5.93 Decision Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="decision-authority44s5"
Proposal Discussed
≠
Decision Approved
```

---

# 5.94 Historical Decisions

A superseded decision remains valuable organizational memory.

---

# 5.95 Lesson Learned Governance

Lesson should identify:

- source event
- validated insight
- owner
- recommended action

---

# 5.96 Lesson Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="lesson-governance44s5"
Lesson Accepted
≠
Control / Procedure Implemented
```

---

# 5.97 Training Governance

Training material should reference current official Knowledge where appropriate.

---

# 5.98 Training Authority

Domain 25 owns employee training/capability.

Domain 44 owns Knowledge source.

---

# 5.99 Training Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="training-authority44s5"
Training Deck
≠
Policy Authority
```

---

# 5.100 AI Use of Knowledge

Domain 42 AI may use approved Knowledge for:

- retrieval
- explanation
- Drafting
- summarization
- recommendations

---

# 5.101 AI Access Governance

AI must operate under the requesting user's applicable access.

---

# 5.102 AI Access Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="ai-access-boundary44s5"
AI Has System Connectivity
≠
AI May Bypass User Knowledge Access
```

---

# 5.103 AI Authority Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="ai-authority44s5"
AI Reads Policy
≠
AI Becomes Policy Authority
```

---

# 5.104 AI Current-Fact Boundary

For current operational facts:

AI should query owning transactional Domain.

Not infer state from documentation.

---

# 5.105 Example

Permanent:

```text id="ai-stock-example44s5"
Inventory Guide Says
"Check Current Stock"

≠

Inventory Guide Contains
Authoritative Current Stock
```

---

# 5.106 AI Source Selection

AI should prefer:

- approved/current sources
- applicable Company
- applicable Role
- stronger provenance

---

# 5.107 AI Historical Use

When historical context is requested:

AI may retrieve archived/superseded material if user has access.

---

# 5.108 AI Historical Boundary

AI must clearly distinguish:

- current guidance
- historical guidance

---

# 5.109 AI Drafting

AI-created draft must retain:

- source references
- Draft status

where appropriate.

---

# 5.110 AI Publication

Permanent:

```text id="ai-publication44s5"
AI Generated Draft
≠
Official Publication
```

---

# 5.111 AI Suggested Changes

AI may recommend:

- possible conflict
- possible stale content
- missing documentation

---

# 5.112 AI Change Authority

AI must not autonomously modify high-authority Knowledge without governed approval.

---

# 5.113 AI Hallucination Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="ai-hallucination44s5"
AI Cannot Find Source
≠
AI May Invent Procedure
```

---

# 5.114 AI Confidence Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="ai-confidence44s5"
High AI Confidence
≠
Authoritative Knowledge
```

---

# 5.115 AI Citation Governance

Where material, AI should identify:

- source
- current Version
- authority

to support user verification.

---

# 5.116 AI Memory Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="ai-memory-boundary44s5"
Agent Memory
≠
Organizational Memory
```

---

# 5.117 AI Memory Promotion

If useful Agent-discovered Knowledge should become organizational Knowledge:

It enters normal:

- capture
- review
- approval

workflow.

---

# 5.118 AI Promotion Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="ai-memory-promotion44s5"
AI Learned Pattern
≠
Enterprise Knowledge Until Governed
```

---

# 5.119 Knowledge Auditability

Material governance events should remain traceable.

Potential:

- owner changed
- Version approved
- publication
- access change
- withdrawal
- archive

---

# 5.120 Audit Boundary

Knowledge audit provides Evidence.

Domain 39 governs formal assurance.

---

# 5.121 Accountability

Every material official Knowledge Asset should be answerable to:

- Who owns it?
- Who approved it?
- Which Version is current?
- Where did it come from?
- Who may use it?
- When should it be reviewed?

---

# 5.122 Unknown Ownership

Official critical Knowledge with no owner is a governance defect.

---

# 5.123 Unknown Provenance

Official high-impact Knowledge with unknown source should be reviewed.

---

# 5.124 Unknown Current Version

Permanent:

```text id="unknown-version44s5"
Cannot Identify Current Version
=
Knowledge Governance Failure
```

for critical operational guidance.

---

# 5.125 Compliance Governance

Domains 24/39 remain authority for legal/compliance requirements and assurance.

---

# 5.126 Security Governance

- retention

- retrieval infrastructure

while Domain 44 supplies authority/freshness metadata.

Certified Business Domains remain authoritative for business behavior.

Certified architecture cannot be modified through Knowledge publication alone.

```text id="architecture-change-boundary44s5"
New Documentation Approved
≠

```

```text id="smp1-governance44s5"
Required Domain 44 Governance:
Only Critical Documentation Control
```

---

# 5.134 SMP1 Minimum Governance

For migration/handover-critical documents:

- identifiable owner
- current Version
- source
- status
- accessible location

is sufficient.

---

# 5.135 SMP1 Sensitive Information

Migration/runbook documentation must not expose:

- Production Secrets
- passwords
- private keys

---

Preserve important:

- certification
- migration
- reconciliation
- cutover
- handover

documentation.

# 5.137 SMP1 Non-Requirements

Do not establish:

- Knowledge governance board
- company-wide editorial workflow
- Knowledge Risk committee
- AI Knowledge governance service
- enterprise ontology governance
- automated retention engine

for SMP1.

---

# 5.138 First Future Governance Step

When Knowledge volume grows:

Introduce simple controls for:

- owner
- current Version
- approval
- access
- review date.

---

# 5.139 Second Maturity Step

Later add:

- classification
- dependency review
- feedback
- historical retention rules.

---

# 5.140 Third Maturity Step

Only at sufficient scale add:

- AI governance
- advanced retention automation
- semantic Knowledge governance.

---

---

# 5.142 ERP10 Reuse

- role-based Help

- user guidance consistency.

---

# 5.143 Version 1.1 Reuse

Version 1.1 may formalize lightweight Knowledge ownership/approval if operational need exists.

---

# 5.144 Advanced Governance That Can Wait

Do not block roadmap for:

- Knowledge governance council
- enterprise editorial department
- automated authority scoring
- AI trust scoring
- Knowledge reputation system
- semantic policy conflict engine
- complex records-management platform
- advanced ontology governance
- autonomous Knowledge approval.

---

# 5.145 Anti-Duplication Rule

Permanent:

> **Domain 44 governs the authority, ownership, lifecycle, access, and accountability of Knowledge. It does not replace Domain 28 authorization, Domain 29 data governance, Domain 10 Document governance, Domain 39 assurance, or certified Business Domain authority.**

---

# 5.146 Anti-Documentation-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **No Knowledge owner, editor, publisher, or AI Agent may use documentation governance as a backdoor to redefine certified business architecture.**

---

# 5.147 Anti-AI-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **AI may retrieve, explain, compare, summarize, and propose Knowledge. It may not silently promote its own output into official organizational truth.**

---

# 5.148 Anti-Overengineering Rule

Permanent:

> **For most GiftHatke Knowledge, governance should answer six practical questions: What is current? Who owns it? Who approved it? Who may see it? Where did it come from? When should it be reviewed?**

---

# 5.149 Critical Governance Invariants

1. Accessible Knowledge ≠ authoritative Knowledge.
2. Two conflicting official sources ≠ user choice.
3. Documentation team ≠ Business Domain authority.
4. Authored ≠ approved.
5. Can edit ≠ can approve.
6. Higher-risk Knowledge warrants stronger governance.
7. Company A approval ≠ Company B approval.
8. Applicability ≠ access permission.
9. Confidential ≠ more authoritative.
10. Can read ≠ edit ≠ approve ≠ publish.
11. Search cannot leak restricted content.
12. Safe internally ≠ safe externally.
13. Superseded ≠ automatically deleted.
14. Not current ≠ safe to destroy.
15. Knowledge article ≠ Secret vault.
16. Team behavior differing from Procedure ≠ Procedure automatically wrong.
17. One exception ≠ new enterprise rule.
18. Temporary workaround ≠ permanent Procedure.
19. Known stale Knowledge ≠ safe current guidance.
20. More pages ≠ higher Knowledge quality.
21. Many copies ≠ many sources of truth.
22. Organizational Memory ≠ current operating authority.
23. Proposal discussed ≠ decision approved.
24. Lesson accepted ≠ improvement implemented.
25. Training material ≠ Policy authority.
26. AI connectivity ≠ unrestricted Knowledge access.
27. AI reads Policy ≠ AI becomes authority.
28. AI confidence ≠ authoritative Knowledge.
29. Agent memory ≠ Organizational Memory.
30. AI-discovered pattern ≠ enterprise Knowledge until governed.
31. Unknown current Version of critical guidance is a governance failure.
32. Documentation approval ≠ certified architecture change.
33. SMP1 needs only critical-document governance.
34. Domain 44 governance must remain Risk-proportional.
35. Governance must protect trust without creating documentation bureaucracy.

---

- AI drafting

- Agent Memory boundaries
- Audit/accountability

- architecture preservation
- SMP1 minimum governance
- ERP9/ERP10/Version 1.1 reuse
- anti-duplication
- anti-documentation-drift
- anti-AI-drift
- anti-overengineering

This is sufficient to govern GiftHatke organizational Knowledge safely without introducing an enterprise Knowledge-management bureaucracy into the standalone migration programme.

# ENTERPRISE KNOWLEDGE OPERATING SYSTEM & ORGANIZATIONAL MEMORY CANON
## Stage 6 — Knowledge Events, Review & Publication Routing, Release Synchronization, Staleness Detection, Decision Capture, Incident Learning, AI Retrieval & Organizational Memory Orchestration Canon

---

# 6.1 Purpose

Stage 6 defines how Knowledge lifecycle events, reviews, approvals, publication, release impact, stale-content detection, decision capture, lessons learned, AI retrieval, and organizational memory should be orchestrated.

The objective is:

> **Ensure important Knowledge changes move through predictable, traceable, Risk-proportional flows while preventing documentation, AI, or automation from silently redefining certified business architecture.**

---

# 6.2 Core Orchestration Principle

```text id="knowledge-orchestration-principle44s6"

↓

↓

Validate Source

↓

Review

↓

Approve if Required

↓

Publish / Supersede / Archive

↓

Notify Relevant Audience

↓

Preserve Audit
```

- automated historical interpretation
- self-maintaining Knowledge Base.

# 6.144 Anti-Duplication Rule

Permanent:

> **Domain 44 orchestrates Knowledge lifecycle and organizational learning. Domain 11 owns generic workflow, Domain 15 scheduling, Domain 9 notifications, Domain 17 Search, Domain 28 Security, Domain 29 data governance, Domain 42 AI behavior, and Business Domains remain authoritative for business truth.**

---

# 6.145 Anti-Documentation-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **No review, publication, release synchronization, or AI-assisted Knowledge process may silently alter certified business architecture.**

---

# 6.146 Anti-Automation-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **Automation may identify, route, remind, compare, and propose. It does not remove the need for appropriate authority where Knowledge materially affects business operations.**

---

# 6.147 Anti-Overengineering Rule

Permanent:

> **The first useful Knowledge automation is simple: remind the right owner when something important may be stale, route a review, publish the approved version, and preserve the previous one.**

---

# 6.148 Critical Orchestration Invariants

1. Knowledge Event ≠ Business Transaction Event.
2. Need detected ≠ article automatically published.
3. Draft event ≠ official authority.
4. Review complete ≠ approval complete.
5. Approval applies to specific Version.
6. Published ≠ user automatically notified.
7. Knowledge changed ≠ everyone notified.
8. Superseded ≠ deleted.
9. Feedback says wrong ≠ article automatically wrong.
10. Conflict detected ≠ system automatically chooses winner.
11. Review overdue ≠ Knowledge automatically invalid.
12. Possible stale ≠ proven wrong.
13. Release published ≠ every Knowledge Asset changed.
14. Runtime changed ≠ business procedure automatically changed.
15. Legacy docs preserved ≠ legacy runtime current.
16. Discussion ≠ decision.
17. Architecture decision recorded ≠ deployed.
18. Incident ≠ new Policy.
19. Handover document delivered ≠ handover proven successful.
20. Procedural question routes to Knowledge; transactional fact routes to Business Domain.
21. AI missing source ≠ permission to fabricate policy.
22. AI Draft ≠ automatic publication.
23. AI detects conflict ≠ AI chooses enterprise policy.
24. AI-extracted Lesson ≠ validated Knowledge.
25. Significant event ≠ permanent memory automatically required.
26. Source update ≠ translation automatically current.
27. Internal approval ≠ external publication approval.
28. Search index update ≠ publication approval.
29. SMP1 requires no dedicated Domain 44 automation.
30. Automation must support governance without becoming governance authority.

---

- Knowledge events

- external publication
- access changes
- search/contextual Help updates
- broken references
- Audit
- Domain 9/10/11/14/15/17/28/29/38/39/41/42 integration
- SMP1 non-requirement
- ERP9/ERP10/Version 1.1 reuse
- anti-duplication
- anti-documentation-drift
- anti-automation-drift

This is sufficient to orchestrate future Knowledge lifecycle and organizational learning while keeping SMP1 firmly focused on migration, reconciliation, handover, and the certified business platform.

# ENTERPRISE KNOWLEDGE OPERATING SYSTEM & ORGANIZATIONAL MEMORY CANON
## Stage 7 — Knowledge Workspace, Search, Contextual Help, Policy/Procedure Reading, Decision History, Feedback, Review, AI Answers & Organizational Memory UX Canon

---

# 7.1 Purpose

Stage 7 defines how people should discover, read, understand, review, maintain, and apply enterprise Knowledge through GiftHatkeOS.

The objective is:

> **Make current authoritative Knowledge easy to find and use while clearly distinguishing Draft, historical, confidential, superseded, AI-generated, and transactional information.**

---

# 7.2 UX Philosophy

Permanent principles:

- current approved Knowledge should be obvious.
- authority and Version should be visible when material.
- users should not need to understand documentation architecture.
- search should prefer current authoritative content.
- historical content should remain available but clearly labeled.
- contextual Help should reduce navigation.
- confidential Knowledge must remain protected.
- feedback should be simple.
- editing/review/approval should remain Role-aware.
- AI answers must preserve source and authority boundaries.

---

# 7.3 Core Future Workspaces

Potential:

- Knowledge Home
- Search
- Knowledge Library
- Knowledge Article
- Policy Library
- Procedure Library
- Decision History
- Lessons Learned
- My Reviews
- Drafts
- Feedback Queue
- Contextual Help
- Organizational Memory
- AI Knowledge Assistant

Not all are required initially.

---
