Critical Procedures should remain readable on:

- phone
- tablet

where frontline users may need them.

---

# 7.124 Accessibility

Status should not rely only on:

- color
- icon

Use textual labels.

---

# 7.125 Search Language

Users should be able to search business language rather than exact article names.

---

# 7.126 Terminology

Use GiftHatke terminology consistently.

Example:

- Current Stock
- Opening Stock
- Stock On Order

rather than multiple inconsistent labels.

---

# 7.127 Glossary

Future glossary may explain standardized terms.

---

# 7.128 Glossary Boundary

Glossary defines terminology.

It does not replace operational Procedure.

---

# 7.129 Knowledge UX in Settings

Settings may include:

- Help
- Documentation
- Integrations documentation

without creating a new massive navigation area initially.

---

# 7.130 First Practical GiftHatkeOS UX

When implemented, a simple:

```text id="first-practical-ux44s7"
Help

↓

Search Documentation

↓

Current Article
```

may be sufficient.

---

# 7.131 SMP1 Requirement

For SMP1:

```text id="smp1-ux-requirement44s7"
Dedicated Knowledge UX Required:
NONE
```

---

# 7.132 SMP1 Practical Access

Migration/handover docs may remain accessible through current:

- repository
- documentation pack
- file system
- existing Knowledge Base

as appropriate.

---

# 7.133 SMP1 Critical Requirement

Team must be able to find:

- migration runbook
- reconciliation guide
- rollback instructions
- operational handover
- support procedures

without implementing new Knowledge UI.

---

# 7.134 SMP1 Non-Requirements

Do not build:

- enterprise wiki UI
- AI Knowledge Assistant
- organizational memory timeline
- Decision Record browser
- semantic Knowledge search
- feedback portal
- review dashboard

for SMP1.

---

# 7.135 First Future UX Step

When users struggle to find documentation:

Add:

- Search
- current-status labels
- simple Knowledge Library

---

# 7.136 Second Maturity Step

When maintenance becomes difficult:

Add:

- Review workspace
- feedback
- version history
- contextual Help

---

# 7.137 Third Maturity Step

Only when enough Knowledge exists:

Add:

- Decision History
- Organizational Memory
- AI-assisted retrieval

---

# 7.138 ERP9 Reuse

ERP9 may link Settings/master-data screens to relevant contextual guidance.

---

# 7.139 ERP10 Reuse

ERP10 is a natural stage for improving:

- contextual Help
- onboarding
- error guidance
- documentation discoverability

without delaying core business certification.

---

# 7.140 Version 1.1 Reuse

Version 1.1 may introduce lightweight in-product Help if users demonstrably need it.

---

# 7.141 Advanced UX That Can Wait

Do not block roadmap for:

- enterprise social Knowledge feed
- expert recommendation
- AI conversational Knowledge portal
- semantic graph explorer
- Knowledge popularity dashboard
- personalized learning feeds
- automatic article recommendations
- advanced collaborative editing
- full public Help Center platform.

---

# 7.142 Anti-Duplication Rule

Permanent:

> **Domain 44 UX presents governed Knowledge. It does not recreate transactional ERP screens, Document storage, Search infrastructure, training management, or Business Domain state.**

---

# 7.143 Anti-Documentation-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **In-product Help and Knowledge UX explain certified workflows. They cannot become an alternative place where users invent unofficial workflow states or business rules.**

---

# 7.144 Anti-AI-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **AI Knowledge UX must expose uncertainty and source boundaries rather than making generated answers look more authoritative than the underlying Knowledge.**

---

# 7.145 Anti-Overengineering Rule

Permanent:

> **The first Knowledge UX needs to do three things well: help users find the current answer, show whether it is authoritative, and make outdated information difficult to mistake for current guidance.**

---

# 7.146 Critical UX Invariants

1. Knowledge Library ≠ file explorer.
2. Visible article ≠ current official guidance.
3. Draft must be visibly non-authoritative.
4. Superseded/historical content must be clearly labeled.
5. Same title ≠ same Version.
6. Top search result ≠ automatically most authoritative.
7. No search result ≠ permission to invent guidance.
8. Contextual Help ≠ transaction enforcement.
9. Policy opened ≠ policy understood/acknowledged.
10. Procedure read ≠ task completed correctly.
11. Decision Record ≠ current runtime state.
12. Historical timeline ≠ operating Procedure.
13. Lesson Learned ≠ mandatory Policy.
14. Feedback ≠ automatic article change.
15. Review due ≠ automatically invalid.
16. Editing Draft ≠ editing live published Knowledge.
17. Search must not reveal restricted snippets.
18. Company applicability must be visible where material.
19. Internal Knowledge ≠ external Help content.
20. Translation exists ≠ translation current.
21. AI answer ≠ System of Record.
22. AI no-source condition ≠ permission to fabricate Procedure.
23. AI suggestion ≠ approved change.
24. Exported/offline copy ≠ guaranteed current copy.
25. SMP1 requires access to critical documents, not a Knowledge UI.
26. Contextual Help should reduce friction, not create another module users must manage.
27. Authority, currentness, and applicability should be understandable without opening governance metadata.
28. Historical Knowledge should remain retrievable without competing with current guidance.
29. Knowledge UX must use business language.
30. Knowledge UI complexity must follow real adoption needs.

---

# 7.147 Stage 7 Certification

Stage 7 permanently establishes the implementation-grade UX architecture for:

- Knowledge Home
- Knowledge Library
- authority/status visibility
- article/procedure/policy layouts
- Version/effective dates
- Search
- Search ranking/filtering
- Contextual Help
- workflow guidance
- policy/procedure reading
- related Knowledge
- supersession/version history
- Decision History
- Organizational Memory
- Lessons Learned
- troubleshooting
- feedback
- reviews
- approvals
- Draft editing
- publication/withdrawal
- confidential access
- Company/Role scope
- external Help
- Partner/developer documentation
- translations
- AI Knowledge Assistant
- AI source/no-source handling
- AI Draft/suggestions
- provenance/Audit
- notifications
- bookmarks/exports
- mobile/accessibility
- terminology/glossary
- SMP1 non-requirement
- ERP9/ERP10/Version 1.1 reuse
- anti-duplication
- anti-documentation-drift
- anti-AI-drift
- anti-overengineering

This is sufficient to define a clear future Knowledge experience while keeping the current execution path focused on standalone migration and business operations rather than building a new Knowledge portal.

# ENTERPRISE KNOWLEDGE OPERATING SYSTEM & ORGANIZATIONAL MEMORY CANON
## Stage 8 — Knowledge Quality, Coverage, Freshness, Search Effectiveness, Reuse, Decision Memory, Learning Impact, Documentation Health & Organizational Knowledge Intelligence Canon

---

# 8.1 Purpose

Stage 8 defines how GiftHatkeOS should measure whether enterprise Knowledge is current, useful, discoverable, trusted, sufficiently complete, reused effectively, and genuinely improving organizational continuity.

The objective is:

> **Evaluate Knowledge by whether people can find and apply the right current guidance, whether critical organizational memory is preserved, and whether outdated or missing Knowledge is visible before it creates operational Risk.**

---

# 8.2 Intelligence Philosophy

Permanent principles:

- Knowledge volume is not Knowledge quality.
- search volume is not search effectiveness.
- article views are not proof of usefulness.
- documentation coverage must focus on important operations.
- freshness must be meaningful, not cosmetic.
- Decision Records should preserve rationale, not create metric vanity.
- Knowledge reuse is valuable only when it improves work.
- organizational learning should lead to improvement where appropriate.
- AI analytics may assist but not define Knowledge authority.
- Knowledge metrics must remain proportional to real operational need.

---

# 8.3 Core Intelligence Areas

Potential:

- Knowledge Coverage
- Knowledge Quality
- Knowledge Freshness
- Ownership Health
- Review Health
- Search Effectiveness
- Retrieval Success
- Contextual Help Usage
- Feedback Quality
- Knowledge Reuse
- Procedure Adoption
- Decision Memory Coverage
- Lesson Learned Follow-Through
- Documentation Synchronization
- Knowledge Risk
- Knowledge Access
- AI Retrieval Quality
- Knowledge Continuity
- Organizational Memory Health

---

# 8.4 Knowledge Inventory

Potential measures:

- total current official Assets
- Draft Assets
- superseded Assets
- archived Assets
- ownerless Assets
- review-overdue Assets

---

# 8.5 Inventory Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-inventory-boundary44s8"
More Articles
≠
More Knowledge Quality
```

---

# 8.6 Knowledge Coverage

Coverage asks:

> Do important business processes have the guidance they actually need?

---

# 8.7 Coverage Scope

Useful areas may include:

- critical daily operations
- exceptions
- onboarding
- Finance controls
- Security operations
- migration/support
- recovery

---

# 8.8 Coverage Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="coverage-boundary44s8"
Document Every Possible Topic
≠
Good Coverage
```

---

# 8.9 Critical Knowledge Coverage

Potential:

```text id="critical-coverage44s8"
Documented Critical Processes
/
Identified Critical Processes
```

where a formal measure is useful.

---

# 8.10 Coverage Gap

Examples:

- team repeatedly asks how to perform a critical task
- only one person knows recovery procedure
- no current procedure exists for important exception

---

# 8.11 Coverage Gap Boundary

Missing documentation should trigger prioritization based on Risk, not automatic massive documentation work.

---

# 8.12 Knowledge Quality

Quality dimensions may include:

- correctness
- clarity
- completeness
- applicability
- currentness
- actionability
- provenance

---

# 8.13 Quality Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="knowledge-quality-boundary44s8"
Long
≠
Clear
≠
Correct
```

---

# 8.14 Quality Review

For critical Knowledge, human review remains primary.

Potential signals:

- repeated corrections
- user feedback
- conflict reports
- failed task due to unclear instruction
- stale references

---

# 8.16 Quality Score Boundary

Permanent:

> **Do not reduce Knowledge trustworthiness to a single opaque quality score.**

---

# 8.17 Knowledge Freshness

Freshness asks:

- Is the current approved guidance still aligned with real operation?

# 8.18 Freshness Signals

- policy superseded

- broken reference

# 8.19 Freshness Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="freshness-boundary44s8"
Recently Edited
≠
Current and Correct
```

---

# 8.20 Review Age

but should not become a universal quality proxy.

---

# 8.21 Overdue Review

Potential metric:

- overdue critical Assets

rather than all overdue material equally.

---

# 8.22 Review Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="review-age-boundary44s8"
Review Overdue
≠
Knowledge Automatically Wrong
```

---

# 8.23 Stale Knowledge Risk

- high-risk
- tied to important operations

# 8.24 Stale Usage

Potential:

```text id="stale-usage44s8"
Stale Critical Article
+
High Usage
=
High Review Priority
```

---

Potential:

- official Assets with owner
- ownerless critical Assets
- owner departed
- owner assignment overdue

---

# 8.26 Ownership Boundary

Permanent:

```text id="ownership-health-boundary44s8"
Owner Assigned
≠
Owner Actively Maintaining
```

Potential:

- approval scope correct
- approval expired/review needed

# 8.28 Approval Boundary

```text id="approval-health-boundary44s8"
Approval Record Exists
≠
Knowledge Still Applicable
```

# 8.29 Search Effectiveness

Search should help users locate correct current Knowledge efficiently.

```text id="search-success-boundary44s8"
≠
```

# 8.35 Search Reformulation

Frequent reformulation may signal:

Current official Knowledge should normally outrank:

- archived
- superseded

content.

# 8.38 Retrieval Precision

For high-risk questions:

```text id="retrieval-quality-boundary44s8"
Good Retrieval
```

# 8.43 Usage Boundary

```text id="article-usage-boundary44s8"
Frequently Viewed
≠
Good Article
```

# 8.44 Low Usage

# 8.47 Duplicate Content Intelligence

# 8.48 Duplicate Boundary

Duplicates should trigger review, not automatic deletion.

# 8.52 Feedback Rate

# 8.54 Feedback Boundary

```text id="feedback-intelligence-boundary44s8"
Many Feedback Items
≠
Poor Knowledge System Automatically
```

# 8.55 Repeated Feedback

# 8.56 Knowledge Conflict Intelligence

# 8.58 Conflict Boundary

# 8.59 Documentation Synchronization

Measure whether Knowledge keeps pace with real approved change.

Potential:

Permanent:

# 8.63 Broken Link Boundary


```text id="smp1-intelligence44s8"
Required Domain 44 Intelligence:
```

signals.

# 8.134 Version 1.1 Reuse

Version 1.1 may introduce lightweight documentation-health visibility if teams actually struggle with Knowledge maintenance.

---

# 8.135 Advanced Intelligence That Can Wait

Do not block roadmap for:

- enterprise Knowledge ROI modeling
- semantic coverage scoring
- expert-network analytics
- Knowledge popularity algorithms
- organizational-memory prediction
- automatic expertise inference
- AI content-ranking engine
- employee Knowledge graphs
- sophisticated learning analytics
- cross-company Knowledge benchmarking.

---

# 8.136 Anti-Metric-Gaming Rule

Permanent:

> **Do not optimize Knowledge operations for article count, page views, search volume, or AI answer volume. Optimize for correct current guidance, critical coverage, findability, continuity, and operational usefulness.**

---

# 8.137 Anti-Duplication Rule

Permanent:

> **Domain 44 measures Knowledge health, currentness, findability, reuse, and organizational memory. Domain 17 owns Search infrastructure, Domain 25 workforce learning, Domain 28 Security, Domain 29 privacy/data governance, Domain 39 assurance, and Business Domains own operational performance.**

---

# 8.138 Anti-AI-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **AI Knowledge metrics must evaluate whether AI used the right governed sources. They must not elevate AI fluency, confidence, or answer volume into a substitute for Knowledge authority.**

---

# 8.139 Anti-Overengineering Rule

Permanent:

> **The first meaningful Knowledge intelligence can fit on one page: which critical guidance is missing, stale, ownerless, conflicting, or difficult to find. Everything beyond that must solve a real operational problem.**

---

# 8.140 Critical Intelligence Invariants

1. More articles ≠ more Knowledge quality.
2. Document everything ≠ good coverage.
3. Long ≠ clear ≠ correct.
4. Recently edited ≠ current/correct.
5. Review overdue ≠ automatically wrong.
6. Owner assigned ≠ actively maintained.
7. Approval record exists ≠ still applicable.
8. Search click ≠ answer found.
9. Zero-result search ≠ new article automatically required.
10. Many relevant-looking results ≠ good retrieval.
11. Frequently viewed ≠ good article.
12. Copied everywhere ≠ successful reuse.
13. Many feedback items ≠ poor Knowledge system automatically.
14. AI conflict flag ≠ proven conflict.
15. Release check complete ≠ every document updated.
16. More Decision Records ≠ better governance.
17. Lesson recorded ≠ organization learned.
18. Handover docs delivered ≠ team ready.
19. Fewer support tickets ≠ documentation definitely better.
20. More readers ≠ better access governance.
21. Fluent AI answer ≠ correct Knowledge answer.
22. AI inability to answer ≠ Knowledge failure automatically.
23. Store everything forever ≠ good organizational memory.
24. Artificial numeric Knowledge Risk ≠ meaningful precision.
25. Knowledge backlog size ≠ business impact.
26. Article-writing volume ≠ employee value.
27. Different screenshot ≠ business-process change.
28. SMP1 needs no Knowledge analytics platform.
29. Critical Knowledge health should focus on business Risk.
30. Knowledge intelligence exists to improve operations, not to produce vanity dashboards.

# ENTERPRISE KNOWLEDGE OPERATING SYSTEM & ORGANIZATIONAL MEMORY CANON
## Stage 9 — Knowledge Testing, Authority Validation, Search & Access Verification, Documentation Synchronization, AI Grounding, Historical Integrity, Migration/Handover Readiness & Production Acceptance Canon

---

# 9.1 Purpose

Stage 9 defines how GiftHatkeOS should verify that enterprise Knowledge is authoritative, current, accessible to the right users, protected from the wrong users, synchronized with certified business architecture, safely consumable by AI, historically preserved, and operationally useful.

The objective is:

> **Prove that users and AI can reliably reach the correct current Knowledge, that outdated or unauthorized Knowledge cannot masquerade as current guidance, and that critical migration and handover documentation is trustworthy enough for real operations.**

---

# 9.2 Testing Philosophy

Permanent principles:

- test current guidance.
- test historical guidance.
- test authority labels.
- test access boundaries.
- test Company scope.
- test Search ranking.
- test conflicting Knowledge.
- test stale Knowledge handling.
- test release synchronization.
- test AI grounding.
- test missing-source behavior.
- test migration/handover documentation.
- test operational usefulness, not merely article existence.

---

# 9.3 Knowledge Acceptance Scope

Where Domain 44 capability exists, validation may cover:

- Knowledge identity
- Type
- Version
- status
- owner
- source
- approval
- publication
- scope
- classification
- Search
- contextual Help
- supersession
- archival
- feedback
- AI retrieval
- Decision Records
- Lessons Learned
- historical integrity

as applicable.

# 9.132 Certification Outcomes

Use where formal certification is appropriate:

- PASS
- PASS WITH CONTROL
- FAIL

under Domain 39 governance.

---

# 9.133 PASS

Means relevant Knowledge controls demonstrate:

- current authority identifiable
- access enforced
- current/historical distinction preserved
- Search behaves correctly
- Knowledge aligns with certified architecture
- AI grounding respects source/access
- critical docs are operationally usable.

---

# 9.134 PASS WITH CONTROL

May be acceptable for non-blocking issue with:

- known owner
- treatment
- accepted Risk
- no material incorrect operational guidance.

---

# 9.135 FAIL

Examples:

- critical current Procedure cannot be identified
- unauthorized restricted Knowledge disclosure
- superseded instruction shown as current
- Procedure materially contradicts certified business rule
- AI exposes restricted Knowledge
- AI fabricates official Procedure without source
- critical SMP1 runbook materially wrong
- rollback/cutover guidance inconsistent with real implementation.

---

# 9.136 Critical Certification Blockers

Minimum:

1. Critical Knowledge current Version unknown.
2. Restricted Knowledge accessible to unauthorized user.
3. Search presents superseded critical Procedure as current.
4. Current official Procedure contradicts certified business architecture.
5. Critical migration/cutover documentation materially incorrect.
6. AI bypasses Knowledge access control.
7. AI presents fabricated guidance as approved official Knowledge.
8. Historical records are silently overwritten.
9. Critical handover documentation cannot be found by intended team.
10. Production runbook references obsolete runtime or commands.

---

- authority
- access
- Search
- synchronization
- AI grounding
- operational-document tests.

# 9.138 Evidence Preservation

Previous FAIL results should remain historical Evidence.

---

# 9.139 No Cosmetic Certification

Permanent:

> **A polished Knowledge Base is not certified merely because it looks organized. Certification depends on correctness, authority, access, currentness, historical integrity, and operational usefulness.**

- Search
- supersession

before advanced AI/semantic features.

---

# 9.141 Advanced AI Gate

Only after core Knowledge governance is stable should AI features be tested for:

- grounded retrieval
- access-safe responses
- correct citations
- current-vs-historical distinction.

---

# 9.142 Semantic Retrieval Gate

If semantic Search is introduced:

Test that similarity does not outrank:

- authority
- access
- currentness

for critical guidance.

---

# 9.143 Knowledge Graph Gate

If Knowledge graph exists:

Derived relationships must not be treated automatically as authoritative business truth.

---

# 9.144 ERP9 Reuse

ERP9 changes should use targeted Knowledge synchronization tests where documentation is affected.

---

# 9.145 ERP10 Reuse

ERP10 may include acceptance of:

- contextual Help
- user guidance
- error/support documentation

as part of enterprise polish.

---

# 9.146 Version 1.1 Reuse

If lightweight Knowledge capability is introduced in Version 1.1, Stage 9 provides its Production acceptance baseline.

---

# 9.147 Advanced Testing That Can Wait

Do not block roadmap for:

- enterprise semantic benchmark suites
- AI organizational-memory stress testing
- expert-recommendation validation
- Knowledge graph consistency laboratory
- large-scale content personalization tests
- global multilingual Knowledge certification
- autonomous Knowledge-agent testing
- sophisticated content ROI experiments.

---

# 9.148 Anti-Duplication Rule

Permanent:

> **Domain 44 tests Knowledge authority, lifecycle, retrieval, historical integrity, and organizational usefulness. Domain 17 tests Search infrastructure, Domain 28 Security, Domain 29 data governance, Domain 39 formal assurance, Domain 41 recovery infrastructure, Domain 42 AI behavior, and Business Domains test business truth.**

---

# 9.149 Anti-Documentation-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **Knowledge acceptance must always compare official guidance against certified business architecture. Documentation cannot pass certification when it describes an unofficial process that differs from the system of record.**

---

# 9.150 Anti-AI-Drift Rule

Permanent:

> **AI Knowledge acceptance is grounded in source authority, access enforcement, currentness, and explicit uncertainty. Fluency is not a certification criterion.**

---

# 9.151 Anti-Overengineering Rule

Permanent:

> **For GiftHatke, the most important Knowledge tests are practical: can people find the right current Procedure, can the wrong person be kept out, can old guidance be recognized as old, can AI stay grounded, and can the team operate without depending on one person's memory?**

---

# 9.152 Critical Testing Invariants

1. Critical current Version unknown = FAIL.
2. Historical Knowledge ≠ current guidance.
3. No owner ≠ delete automatically.
4. Version 2 approval ≠ Version 3 approval.
5. Approved ≠ published.
6. Company A approval ≠ Company B approval.
7. Unauthorized user ≠ confidential snippet access.
8. Top Search result must respect currentness/authority.
9. No result ≠ fabricate Procedure.
10. Help failure ≠ transaction failure.
11. Procedure must align with certified business rules.
12. Screenshot change ≠ process change automatically.
13. Release completed ≠ every document changed.
14. Runtime changed ≠ business meaning changed.
15. Legacy docs preserved ≠ legacy runtime current.
16. History preserved ≠ history rewritten.
17. Feedback ≠ direct official mutation.
18. Conflict detected ≠ system selects policy.
19. Decision Record ≠ implementation completed.
20. Historical Memory ≠ current Procedure.
21. Lesson recorded ≠ improvement implemented.
22. Translation source updated ≠ translation current.
23. Internal approval ≠ external publication approval.
24. Exported copy ≠ guaranteed current copy.
25. Current transactional facts must come from Business Domains.
26. AI may not reveal restricted Knowledge.
27. No grounded source ≠ permission for AI invention.
28. AI Draft ≠ Published Knowledge.
29. Knowledge service outage should not collapse core ERP.
30. Documentation exists ≠ team can find/use it.
31. SMP1 Knowledge acceptance applies to critical documents, not a Knowledge platform.
32. Rollback documentation ≠ proven rollback capability.
33. Search similarity must not override authority/currentness.
34. Polished presentation ≠ Knowledge certification.
35. Production Knowledge acceptance must prove practical operational trust.

---

# 10.1 Purpose

Stage 10 consolidates and formally certifies Domain 44 as the permanent GiftHatkeOS architecture for enterprise Knowledge, organizational memory, policies, procedures, decision history, lessons learned, Knowledge ownership, provenance, searchability, lifecycle, AI grounding, and historical continuity.

The objective is:

> **Ensure GiftHatke can preserve what the organization knows, why important decisions were made, how work should be performed, and which guidance is current—without confusing Knowledge with transactional business truth or turning SMP1 into a Knowledge-platform programme.**
